In order to be able to recharge a card, processors often store a payment token. This can be used to recharge a credit card, but only to put money into your account, not anyone elses. The rules around how these may be used vary and most Processors only use them for regular Recurring Payments.

You have the option to View, Edit, or Cancel the Recurring Contribution here. You can edit the Recurring Contribution Amount, Number of Installments, Next Scheduled Contribution Date, Financial Type, Status, Start Date, and whether or not the donor receives an email notification on each payment installation. The donation frequency (e.g. weekly, monthly) cannot be changed from within CiviCRM.

If you View the Recurring Contribution, you will also be able to View, Edit, or Process the card on file. Viewing or editing will bring up the customer and card information.

For iATS users, there is an administrative page where you can view recent iATS transactions. On the menu, navigate to Contributions > iATS Payments Administration to see the report.

docs.title: Payment processors
docs.text:
CiviCRM connects to a variety of different Payment Processors. Out-of-the-box, it comes with support for approximately 15 Payment Processors. Many other community contributed processors are available to download from the CiviCRM Extensions Directory.

Additional Payment Processors may also be available from third-party sites.

Community contributed processors are not supported by CiviCRM but there is no reason why they should not be just as reliable as the out-of-the-box Processors. If you do use a community contributed Processor, be sure that you have access to adequate technical support for that Processor, either in house, from the author of the Payment Processor, or from a trusted third party.

Browse a comparison of the available Payment Processors in the System Administrator Guide.

docs.title: Selecting a payment processor
docs.text: Payment providers differ in cost, suitability for your use case, and availability. If possible, talk to similar nearby organisations that use CiviCRM about their experiences with Payment Processors. You can also configure more than one Payment Processor and give constituents the option to choose the one they prefer.

docs.title: Onsite vs offsite processors
docs.text:
With an onsite Payment Processor, the user enters credit card details directly on your site. With an offsite processor, the user goes to another site to make the payment and then returns to yours. You can typically brand the payment site to a limited extent—for example, with your organisation name, logo and colours—but the workflow is less seamless, and a percentage of people tend not to complete the payment.

As well as providing a more seamless experience for end users, onsite Payment Processors allow site admins to process card payments (Contributions, Membership Fees, Event Payments, etc.) from CiviCRM admin pages.

The disadvantage of processing payments directly on your site is that you will need to have an SSL certificate to ensure the security of the users card details as they are transmitted over the internet. SSL certificates cost money (typically an annual fee) and they are not straight forward to set up. Your hosting provider or system administrator can help you here. You may also want to read the Security section in the Initial set up chapter of this book.

CiviCRM never stores credit card details on your server. It only transmits them to the payment processor.

docs.title: Regional availability
docs.text: For many countries there are no Payment Processors written that support their currencies. If you do not have Payment Processor support for the Payment Processor you want to use, consider writing your own processor or asking a third party to do so.

docs.title: Merchant account vs built-in
docs.text: Most organizations that accept credit card payments will have their own merchant account through a bank, however these usually have monthly charges which may not suit smaller organizations (though they generally have lower percentage payments). You can expect to pay a fee for the merchant account and to the Payment Processor, though these may be bundled together. Some, like World Pay and Paypal, do not require separate merchant accounts.

docs.title: Support for recurring contributions
docs.text:
Support for Recurring Contributions and auto-renewing memberships is an important feature for many organizations. However not all of the Payment Processors available for CiviCRM support this feature. Many processors that allow you to manage Recurring Contributions from within CiviCRM but PayPal and Authorize.net require you to log into their own portals to manage Recurring Contributions. Some, like Moneris, have "incomplete" support.

If you have configured a Payment processor that includes Recurring Payments as a feature, you can enable Recurring Contributions in your Contribution Page settings. For more details on page-specific configuration, refer to the Online Contributions chapter.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: Determining which Payment Processor is least expensive depends on the number and average size of the transaction you process. So the question is not which processor is the cheapest, but which is the cheapest for you. Commission percentages, per-transaction charges, and fixed monthly charges vary along with set-up costs. In general, if you process many transactions, an account with a monthly fee but low commission might be a good option. On the other hand, if you expect infrequent transactions, it is best to avoid monthly fees and accept paying a higher commission.

docs.title: Usability
docs.text: If you do not collect the credit card information yourself on your own site, you need to consider whether the payment workflow is intuitive and easy to use. Paypal Standard is often confusing to end users because they are not sure whether or not they need to create a PayPal account. Such a barrier can result in decreased contributions.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: CiviCRM supports the processors that are incorporated into the core codebase, to the extent that they ensure they do not break in upgrade - support and enhancements of community contributed processors are generally expected to come from the community.

docs.title: Writing a new payment processor
docs.text: If you cannot find a suitable Payment Processor, or want to use a specific payment provider that is not currently supported by CiviCRM, you can write a new Payment Processor integration, or pay someone else to do so.

docs.title: Set up and manage Personal Campaign Pages
Set-up
docs.text:
All Personal Campaign Pages must be linked to an existing online contribution page or event, created in CiviCRM by navigating to either: Contributions > New Contribution Page or Events > New Event. Once a contribution page or event has been generated, while editing the settings go to the Personal Campaigns tab and click 'enable personal campaign pages'. A number of other options may then be configured, including:

  • Approval Required: check this option to moderate all PCP creation requests. An administrator must approve the page before it becomes active, at which point the user will be notified via email, and may proceed to promote it (ensure "notify email" is also used to notify an administrator when PCP pages are awaiting review).
  • Notification Email: Each time a new PCP is created, an email will be sent to the named administrators (separate multiple email addresses with commas).
  • Supporter Profile: select a profile of fields to be collected from the user creating the PCP.
  • Owner Email Notification: an email can be automatically sent to the PCP owner whenever a donation is made through their page. You can select whether emails will always or never be sent automatically for all PCP pages created under that particular event or contribution page. Alternatively, you can allow the PCP owner to choose during the page set up process whether or not they would like to receive notification of donations made through their page.
  • Allow 'tell a friend' functionality: the PCP owner may send emails to their contacts, encouraging them to visit their page and contribute.
  • Campaign Type: when enabling PCPs for an event, you may give the event registrant the option to either create a fundraising event of their own, or a contribution page (e.g. to raise money in support of their attendance).

After PCP creation has been enabled, there are two ways to create a PCP:

  • An individual donating to a contribution page or registering for an event is given the option to build their own PCP via a button on the 'thank you' page.
  • If the individual forgets to click the link upon donation, or you wish to give all visitors the opportunity to create a PCP without the prerequisite of donating or registering themselves, you can give your constituents a direct link. This link could be emailed to the constituent, embedded in a page or added as a menu item. Note that.

The invitation button:

The invitation link:

http://<EXAMPLE.ORG>/civicrm/contribute/campaign?action=add&reset=1&pageId=<CONTRIBUTION_OR_EVENT_ID>&component=<EVENT_OR_CONTRIBUTE>

To use this link, replace the following:

  • *YOUR-SITE.ORG*: enter your domain's address.
  • *CONTRIBUTION_OR_EVENT_ID*: give the ID number of the event or contribution page. This can be obtained through navigating to 'Manage Events' or 'Manage Contribution Pages' and looking for the ID against the item in question.
  • *EVENT_OR_CONTRIBUTE*: If the invitation is for a Personal Campaign Page in support of a contribution page, use component=contribute. If the invitation is in support of an event, use component=event.

docs.title: Managing Personal Campaign Pages
docs.text:
When an individual has clicked the 'create your own fundraising page' button or a direct link, they will be presented with a form to fill out their information, including: a title, message, monetary goal amount and text for the donate button. They may also attach a photo, enable a progress - thermometer style - bar, include an honor role of their donors who have not elected to be anonymous, and whether the campaign is active (they may choose to activate it at a later time).

If PCP moderation has been enabled (the 'approval required' option), an administrator must log into the CiviCRM back-end and enable the page at Contributions > Personal Campaign Pages before the individual is able to use it. Simply seek the PCP in the list, look toward the end of the row and click 'Approve', 'Reject' or 'Delete' (at a later date, you may also enable/disable the PCP by clicking the 'More' link). The individual will be sent a confirmation email, and may proceed to use it. Ensure administrators are always alerted to this step by entering a notification email address in the contribution page settings (see 'Set-up' above).

Finally, following approval the PCP owner will be sent an email outlining how they may begin promoting their page and editing it, providing they have been given user access. The user and administrator can edit the PCP settings at any time through the menu item: Contributions > Personal Campaign Pages> click Edit, Delete or Disable/Enable.

docs.title: Personal Campaign Pages
docs.text:
CiviCRM's features include allowing your constituents to create their own fundraising pages - and then ask others to fund their cause. These pages are called Personal Campaign Pages or "PCPs".

A Personal Campaign Page allows your constituents to personalize the fundraiser, event, organization, etc., by offering their personal reasons and/or experiences with the organization on their own personal page. Also, your contributors may in turn send the Personal Campaign Pages to their circle of friends. You can enable the "tell a friend" feature to help someone share their page even more.

Examples of this feature in action are typically called "Sponsor My 5k Walk", "Help Fund Our Trip" or "Let's Raise Money to Build A School".

docs.title: Administrator features
docs.text:
Administrators managing fundraising pages may use the following features via the Contribution Page Configuration:

  • Requiring approval before a newly-created fundraising page becomes active
  • Turning on or off 'tell a friend' so fundraisers can email others
  • Setting an email address to notify admin when a new page is created
  • Allowing PCP owners to always, sometimes or never receive notification when a donation is made via their page
  • Choosing a profile of fields to collect from PCP supporters
  • Customizing the text in the create button

Once PCP pages are active, administrators can:

  • Disable or deny Personal Contribution Pages
  • Edit PCP content
  • View the amount of money collected by each PCP
  • Run reports (using CiviReport) showing a summary of PCP fundraising
  • Enter 'offline' contributions (i.e. checks) and credit the money to a PCP

docs.title: Fundraiser features
docs.text:
Those creating their PCPs enjoy the following ways to personalize their page:

  • A title of their choice
  • Descriptive text
  • Selecting a monetary goal amount they hope to raise
  • A single image they can upload that will appear on their page
  • Choosing whether or not an 'honor roll' of supporter names will be shown on their page
  • Option to display a 'thermometer' showing progress towards their goal
  • Create a username (or login using a username they already have) so they can edit their PCP later

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• CiviCRM's PCP functionality doesn't allow for team management. For instance, a fundraising leader recruiting members to a team, managing membership and then keeping track of which member brought in how much money is not supported by CiviCRM at this time.
  • There is a limit of a single image uploaded to a PCP by the fundraiser. The image is not automatically re-sized.
  • The thermometer and honor roll appearance can be modified, but changes are applied to all pages. These customizations cannot be done without the expertise of a coder.
  • The automated emails (system workflow messages) sent to the PCP administrator and the page owner at various stages during a campaign can be modified. A working knowledge of Smarty 2 (http://www.smarty.net/) is required. The default notification for the PCP owner when a donation is received is:

docs.title: Configure premiums
docs.text:
Configure Premiums, such as T-shirts or subscriptions, to offer on your contribution pages:

  1. Navigate to Administer > CiviContribute > Premiums (Thank-You Gifts).
  2. Edit an existing Premium, or click Add Premium to add a new one.
  3. Enter the premium’s Name, Description, SKU (an optional product code), Premium Image (an optional image of the item), Minimum Contribution Amount to receive the Premium, Market Value of the Premium, Actual Cost (optional), Financial Type (optional), and Options (e.g. colors and sizes).
  4. If you’re offering a Subscription or Service, click Subscription or Service Settings to define additional information, such as Period Type (e.g., Fixed or Rolling), Fixed Period Start Day, Duration, and Frequency.

docs.title: Reports and analysis
docs.text: You can use CiviReport or CiviCRM's search features to report on and analyse contributions. CiviCRM includes thirteen Contribution Reports.

docs.title: Contribution reports
docs.text: Report What it provides Contribution Summary Report Groups contributions by criteria including the contact that made the contribution, time period, type and location, and shows summary statistics. You can use it to analyse, for example, what percentage of income comes from different fundraising campaigns or from events versus memberships. Contribution Detail Report Provides a detailed report for a specific subset of contributions. It is automatically called when you click any row in the Contribution Summary Report, but you can also call it on its own. Repeat Contribution Report Compares contacts' total contributions across two time periods and shows the percentage increase or decrease. Use it to identify contacts who have stepped up their giving or are giving less than before. SYBUNT report Finds donors who gave in “Some Years But Not This Year”. LYBUNT report Finds donors who gave “Last Year But Not This Year”. Contribution by Household Report Aggregates contributions by household. For organizations that use household records, this can show contributions made by a particularly active family. It also includes donations attached to the household record. Contribution by Organization report Aggregates contributions by organization. For organizations that use organization records, this can show contributions made by employees of one organization so you can thank them as a whole. It also includes donations attached to the organization record, such as a donation made by the organization after a collective office fundraising event. Top Donors Report Lists the top donors during a time period you define. You can include as many donors as you want, such as your top 100 donors. If you leave the Show no. of Top Donors field empty, the report includes all contacts included by the other filters. Personal Campaign Page Report Gives an overview of the status of all Personal Campaign Pages. You can filter by contribution page to see Personal Campaign Pages for a single campaign, and by other appropriate criteria. Soft Credit Report Shows your soft credits and who is at least partially responsible for other people's donations. Contribution Aggregate by Relationship Report Lists a contact's donation history, grouped by year, alongside contributions attributed to any of the contact's related contacts. Recurring Contributions Report Provides information about the status of recurring contributions. Bookkeeping Transactions Report Provides transaction details for all payments, including financial type and accounts, transaction number, invoice ID, payment instrument and check number.

docs.title: More analysis
docs.text: The standard reports are configured to display particular information and may not provide what you need. You can download and install extensions to access additional reports. If you still can't extract the information you need, consider commissioning a new report or custom search and contributing it back to the community.

docs.title: Sales tax and VAT
docs.text: If your organization charges Sales Tax or VAT, enable this feature.

docs.title: Enable Sales Tax/VAT
docs.text:
Go to Administer > CiviContribute > CiviContribute Component Settings and check the Enable Tax and Invoicing box.

On this screen, you can also set:

  • Tax Term — the text your organization wants to use for the relevant Sales Tax or VAT.
  • Tax Display Settings — how your organization wants to display the Tax/VAT:
    • No breakdown, total only
    • Shows as inclusive price - $120 (includes $20 tax)
    • Shows as exclusive price - $100 + $20 tax

docs.title: Add a Financial Account for Sales Tax/VAT
docs.text:
Once Sales Tax/VAT is enabled, create one or more Financial Accounts for Tax/VAT at Administer > CiviContribute > Financial Account. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Add Financial Account.

To create the Sales Tax Account, set Financial Account Type to Liability. Select Enabled and Is Tax, and specify the Tax Rate. If you use Quick Books, the Account Type Code should be set to SALESTAX. Accounting Code should be based on the organization's specific Accounting Codes.

docs.title: Assign the account to a Financial Type
docs.text:
After creating the Financial Account, go to Adminster > CiviContribute > Financial Types. Find the Financial Type this Sales Tax applies to and click Accounts, then Assign Account.

For Financial Account Relationship, choose Sales Tax Account is. In the Financial Account field, select your Sales Tax account. Click Save.

The Sales Tax Financial Account will appear with the other Financial Accounts for that Financial Type.

For more advanced configuration with accounting software packages like QuickBooks, involve your organization's bookkeeper or accountant in setting up your Financial Types and Financial Accounts.

docs.title: Soft credits
docs.text: Soft credits help your organisation understand the sources of its contributions. They let you assign credit for a donation to one or more people who are not the donor.

docs.title: Soft credit types
docs.text:
CiviCRM's soft crediting allows users to assign Soft Credit Types to contributions. Assigning an appropriate reserved or custom Soft Credit Type enables administrators to properly attribute contributions received through one or more charitable contribution types (such as Donor Advised Funds, Scholarships, Family Bequests, etc) whether solicited (P2P) or not.

CiviCRM uses the following reserved Soft Credit Types:

  • In Honor of
  • In Memory of
  • Solicited
  • Personal Campaign Page
  • Gift

For example, if an active member of your organisation encourages 10 other people to contribute, soft credits let you credit that member and each actual donor without counting a contribution twice. You can also credit parts of a donation to multiple people.

In the screenshot below, Magan Cooper's contribution of $1,500.00 is credited to three different people.

Soft Credit Types can also attribute contributions in more complicated situations. For example, Joe is an active member of a community foundation that regularly contributes to your organisation. Joe solicits a contribution from Jane on behalf of the foundation, and your organisation receives a check from the foundation. The contribution can be attributed without duplicating it:

  • The community foundation is the donor.
  • Joe would receive the solicited Soft Credit.
  • Jane would receive the donor advised Soft Credit.

This scenario is illustrated below.

As well as recording Soft Credits, we can also report on them. The contribution detail report has optional columns which show Soft Credit details. When checked, these will show four extra columns in CiviReport, which can be used to view soft credit information.

docs.title: Honoree information and profiles
docs.text:
When creating a contribution page, you can allow end users to make a contribution on behalf of an Honoree. To do so, select the Honoree Section Enabled checkbox. This reveals additional fields for specifying the Honor Types and Profile to include in the section.

Once configured, end users can enter Honoree info for online contributions. CiviCRM checks whether the Honoree already exists using your site's default duplicate checking rules. If no duplicate is found, it creates a new contact record. A soft credit is added to the Honoree's contact record.

docs.title: Soft credits and personal campaign pages
docs.text: Soft credits are closely related to Personal Campaign Page. When someone donates by a Personal Campaign Page, their donation is soft credited to the owner of the Personal Campaign Page.

docs.title: What is CiviContribute?
docs.text:
CiviContribute is the component that lets you record and report on financial and in-kind contributions to your organization. It allows you to:

  • accept donations and other financial or in-kind contributions
  • process membership signups and renewals
  • accept and manage events fees
  • run specific fundraising campaigns
  • let your supporters fundraise for you through personalised campaign pages
  • quickly enter contribution and membership payments using "batches"
  • export batches of financial transactions to import to your accounting software
  • report and evaluate fundraising results and trends

Throughout CiviCRM, the term contribution refers to any financial transaction or payment taking place in the system, such as a donation, event fee payment or membership fee payment. It also includes in-kind contributions.

docs.title: Scenario: contributing to leadership
docs.text:
A community arts group, Arts in Action, conducts leadership workshops for youth under 25 throughout the year. They use CiviCRM extensively to plan and run the workshops, combining CiviEvent and CiviContribute to make administration as efficient as possible.

The workshops are funded in three ways: participant fees, local arts funding, and donations. Most donations come from previous workshop participants who have continued as Arts in Action constituents.

Twice a year, Arts in Action sends a call for workshop donations using CiviMail, with a link to a donations page on the site. Some donors make recurring donations; others make one-off donations. A thank-you email and receipt is automatically sent to every donor when a payment is successfully processed. All donations are tagged for the workshops, so staff can report on total workshop donations and look at individual contact records to see who has donated.

Participants register and pay for workshops through an online form. Registration has a flat fee, with additional fees for optional workshops, food and lodging preferences. Participants make their choices in the form and pay by credit card. If a participant is not already a contact in the database, a new record is created at registration. The payment is recorded in that contact's contribution record, which is also linked to the workshop event.

Arts in Action also lets participants pay later. Many do not have a credit card and need to pay in cash at the workshop. CiviContribute distinguishes an actual payment from a commitment to pay. That information appears in the registrants report, which is printed and used on the day to check attendance and payment. At the workshop registration desk, a computer is used to manually enter cash and cheque payments in each participant's contribution record.

Arts in Action has assessed that word of mouth and participants bringing friends are the most effective ways to publicise the workshops. They enable participants to forward the registration link to friends through the "tell-a-friend" mechanism. After completing the registration form, participants can forward it by email or social networking platforms to friends and colleagues who may also be interested in attending.

After every workshop, the Arts in Action accountant uses a report template to generate a report showing the workshop's total income from each of the three sources. Staff also track donation trends and make sure the Board knows who the larger donors are. Key statistics are displayed graphically on staff members' CiviCRM dashboard.

docs.title: Popular extensions
docs.text:
These are widely used extensions in the relevant category of the official CiviCRM Extensions Directory. Usage is a popularity signal, not a compatibility or suitability guarantee.

  • CiviSEPA — SEPA Direct Debit Extension — reported usage: 925
  • no overwrite — reported usage: 918
  • Summary Fields — reported usage: 663
  • Line Item Editor — reported usage: 565
  • Percentage Price Field — reported usage: 385

All extensions for this component

Check development status, current CiviCRM compatibility, CMS requirements, and release notes before installation.

Usage snapshot reviewed: 2026-10-13.

docs.title: Widgets
docs.text:
CiviContribute widgets help you and your supporters promote a fund-raising campaign with an automatically updated visual representation of the campaign.

When you create a widget, you receive code to embed it on your website or another website.

docs.title: Creating a widget
docs.text:
1. Go to Contributions > Manage Contribution Pages. In the list of Contribution Pages, click Configure for your Contribution Page.
  2. Select Widgets from the tabs at the top of the page.
  3. Click Enable Widget.
  4. Enter a Title for your widget. It will generally be the same name as your Contribution Page, but it does not have to be.
  5. Optionally, enter the URL to Logo Image. To use this feature, you need to upload an image to your web server and obtain its URL (web address). You may need to ask your system administrator for help.
  6. Enter a Button Title for potential donors to click to go to your donate page. In the example above, the button title is Contribute.
  7. Use the editor to enter as much About text as you want. Adjust the amount of text based on where you want to use your widget.
  8. Click Save and Preview when you are ready to preview your widget or have finished and want to update its code.

  9. Find the code for embedding the widget on a web page on the right. You may need help from your system administrator or the person who administers your website to use this code.

  10. Use the Select Code link to select all the necessary code.

  11. Copy and paste the code into the place on your website where you want the widget to display.

docs.title: Customizing your widget
docs.text:
1. At the bottom of the configuration page, expand the Edit Widget Colors fieldset.

  2. Get hexadecimal (or hex) codes for the colors you want to use. The fields let you modify the colors for each area of the widget. W3schools provides a color picker that gives you hex values for selected colors.

  3. Modify the colors. A designer you have worked with on your website may have specific standards for the colors to use.
  4. Click Save and Preview to see how your changes look.

docs.title: Using widgets with WordPress
docs.text: WordPress has a plugin, CiviCRM Contribution Page Widget, that lets you embed a widget from CiviCRM anywhere that a WorderPress widget can go.

docs.title: CiviMail A/B testing
docs.text:
CiviMail A/B Testing lets you send two test e-mails to two random samples of your recipients. After the test mailings are complete, you can use the available metrics to choose which mailing to send to the remaining recipients.

Before conducting a new A/B Test, put your recipients in a Mailing List. To learn more about configuring a Mailing List, see the chapters on Groups and Tags.

docs.title: Create a new A/B test
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Mailings > New A/B Test.
  2. On the Setup screen, define the campaign that corresponds with the mailing and select the type of test. You can test:
  3. Different Subject lines
  4. Different From lines
  5. Entirely different emails
  1. On the Target screen, define your recipients and the distribution percentage. Drag the blue percentage bar to change the percentage of test mailings and, in turn, the percentage of final mailings sent to the remaining participants. The test mailings and final mailing sum to 100%.
  1. On the Compose screen, enter the fields for your chosen test type. The screen changes depending on the type of A/B Test:

  2. For different From lines, enter From (A) and From(B).

  3. For different Subject lines, enter Subject(A) and Subject(B).

  4. For entirely different emails, add a From and Subject for each mailing.

  5. Choose an email template that you have previously composed. Once you have selected the template and specified the From and Subject field, send a test email before scheduling or sending your final mailing.

docs.title: Review results and select a final mailing
docs.text: Once the test mailings are complete, navigate to Mailings > Manage A/B Tests and select Results. On the A/B Test Results screen, monitor the results and select which mailing should be submitted as the Final mailing.

docs.title: Everyday tasks
docs.text: This page covers everyday email tasks. For instructions on sending a mass mailing, see Mass mailings using CiviMail.

docs.title: Send an email to one person (with CC and BCC)
docs.text:
You can use CiviCRM to email an individual when you want other people at your organisation to see the email or you want to use a pre-defined template.

  1. Find the person you wish to email using either method:
    • Use the Quick Search box on the top left. Click inside the box and begin typing part of the person's name or email address. Choose the person from the choices presented.
    • Navigate to Search > Find Contact. Enter part of the person's name or email address, click Search, then click the person's name in the search results.
  2. From the contact summary page, click Actions > Send an email, or click the Activities tab and choose Send an Email from the dropdown menu.
  3. Add any additional recipients using the CC and BCC fields.
  4. If you have templates defined, you can choose one from the Use Template dropdown menu. Selecting a template populates the text content and HTML content fields with its message content, which you can then edit.
  5. Enter your content or add to the template. To send only a Plain Text version, ignore the HTML Format section, click the Plain Text Format section, and enter your message in the box.
  6. Click Send.

To see the recorded activity for the email you sent, click the contact's Activities tab.

docs.title: Send a quick email to fewer than 50 contacts
docs.text:
The actions dropdown menu in search results offers “Send Email to Contacts” for emailing more than one contact at a time. This method is relatively quick, but it has no options for tracking email and does not give contacts the option to opt out. It is limited to 50 contacts and should not be used for mass mailings. For mass mailings, use CiviMail.

  1. Click Search > Find Contacts (or Advanced Search). Choose your search criteria and click Search, or use another search to find the contacts you wish to email.
  2. In the search results, choose some or all of the contacts and click Actions > Email -send now (to 50 or less).
  3. Follow the steps under “Send an email to one person (with CC and BCC)” above.

The email is recorded as an Activity for each recipient and for the sender. The activity record also lists all other message recipients. Unlike mass mailing, there is no one place where all emails sent using the Send Email function are listed.

Note

When a message is sent to multiple recipients, each recipient sees only their own email address in the To field. Because recipients cannot see who else received the email, you might want to identify the group in your message—for example, “TO: Members of the board, staff”.

docs.title: Insert an image in an email
docs.text:
1. Click the image button in the WYSIWYG editor.

  2. In the Image Properties window, click Browse Server to look for image files on your server.

  3. In the left sidebar, navigate through the file directory and select the image if it is already on your server. Otherwise, click Upload to choose a file from your computer.

  4. In your computer's file-browsing window, find the image, select it, and click Open. You can repeat this process to upload multiple files to CiviCRM at once.

  5. Double-click the image you want to insert. You will return to the email's Image Properties window.
  6. Adjust the image's size, alignment, and border as needed. You can also fill in the Alternative Text field. Alternative text appears when the image is unavailable to a reader—for example, when they choose not to load images in their email client or use a screen reader due to a visual impairment. To avoid losing information and make email accessible to all user communities, always include alternative text for images.

  7. Click OK to insert the image.

docs.title: Manage email addresses on hold
docs.text: If an email address is put on hold, you can unhold it or fix/delete it.

docs.title: Release a hold
docs.text:
1. Go to Advanced Search.

  2. In Basic Search Criteria, check the box to search for Emails On Hold.

  3. Select the contacts with held email addresses. Choose Unhold Emails from the dropdown list and click Go.

docs.title: Correct or update held emails
docs.text:
First, create a group(s) for bad emails. Then:

  1. In the top menu, go to Reports.
  2. Select Mail Bounce Report.
  3. The report will show contacts whose emails have bounced.
  4. Open Report Criteria at the top of the mailing to limit the report to a specific bounce type.
  5. Add the contacts in your search results to the group you created.
  6. Pull up the group via Advanced Search. It is also recommended that you select Email on Hold to avoid querying records that have previously bounced but may have already been updated.
  7. Select Batch Update via Profile for all results whose email addresses you can correct/update. This requires a profile that contains just Primary Email.
  8. Select this profile and click Update.

docs.title: Maintaining healthy email lists
docs.text:
After setting up and configuring Email lists, you need to manage them and consider compliance. Healthy lists have low rates of bounced emails and unsubscribes.

A high bounce rate may raise concerns about being blacklisted or receiving a complaint from your SMTP provider. High bounce and unsubscribe rates typically point to a deeper organization issue.

docs.title: Understanding email bounces
docs.text: Each time you send a bulk email from CiviMail, some emails may bounce. Some bounces are temporary; others are permanent.

docs.title: Why do emails bounce?
docs.text:
A bounced email did not reach its recipient. Reasons include:

  • The email address was input incorrectly.
  • The email address is out of commission.
  • The inbox is full and temporarily cannot accept more messages.
  • The recipient has an automatic away reply because they are on vacation and out of the office.

CiviCRM handles bounce types differently. Temporary bounces do not affect a contact record, and CiviCRM will attempt to send future mailings to the address. Permanent bounces may put a contact email on Hold. No future emails will be sent to an address on Hold unless someone fixes it and removes the hold.

The System Administrator Guide's Inbound email chapter has a detailed table of bounce types and the number of bounces allowed before an address is put on hold.

docs.title: On-hold emails and unsubscribes
docs.text:
An email address on hold is different from an unsubscribe. Someone unsubscribes by clicking “unsubscribe from this mailing” in an email. The link is created by either of these tokens: {action.unsubscribe} or {action.unsubscribeUrl}.

Recipients who unsubscribe from a single mailing list are removed from the group used as that mailing list.

docs.title: Opting out and unsubscribing
docs.text:
Recipients can opt out of all bulk emails by clicking a link you provide in every mass email. You can still send individual or small volume emails to someone who has opted out using Send Email from the contact's record or after a search. Scheduled reminders will also still be sent to contacts who have opted out. Be careful about the emails you send to someone who has opted out if you do not want to be accused of sending spam.

The opt-out link is created by either of these tokens: {action.optOut} or {action.optOutUrl}. You can include these tokens in the body of your mailing or in a footer message.

docs.title: The Do not email privacy option
docs.text:
If a contact has Do not email selected, you cannot send them individual or small volume emails using Send Email from their record or after a search. They will not receive bulk emails sent through CiviMail. They will still receive scheduled reminders unless you specifically exclude them from those reminders.

If Do not email was set manually after the person contacted you in person, it is probably a good idea to exclude them from scheduled reminders. The Schedule Reminders chapter outlines how to do that.

docs.title: Making sure a contact receives no emails
docs.text: Someone could change CiviCRM settings incorrectly or manually misuse an email address. The only way to fully guarantee that a contact receives no emails is to remove all email addresses from their record. In that case, the contact would not be able to log in to your website.

docs.title: Mass mailings using CiviMail
docs.text: The Mailings functionality offered by CiviMail provides benefits over the Send Email activity: you can track respondents, process bounces, and allow people to unsubscribe. This page first covers creating and sending a mass mailing, then tracking and managing mailings.

docs.title: Choosing recipients: Groups versus search results
docs.text:
You can select recipients by sending to existing Groups or to search results. Most steps are the same, but a mailing to search results requires you to choose a Group from the Unsubscription Group dropdown menu.

Every mass mailing needs a way to track unsubscribe requests. A simple unsubscribe process is required by law in many countries and may help prevent mailings from being treated as spam. Mailings sent to Groups have this capacity built in: the next time a mass email is sent to that Group, anyone who has unsubscribed will not be included. Mailings sent to search results do not have this built-in way to track unsubscribes, so you must provide one.

If a contact who matches your search results is already unsubscribed from the Unsubscription Group you designate, that contact will not be sent the mailing. If a contact unsubscribes through the unsubscription link in the mailing, they will be unsubscribed from that Group and will not receive further emails sent to it. This applies whether or not they were originally a member of the Group.

The Unsubscription Group collects unsubscribe information only; it does not supply contacts to the mailing. Contacts in that Group who do not match your search criteria will not be included. To include them, include the relevant Group.

For example, your organization is having a big event next week. Several emails have already gone out about it, but you have added many new people to your database in the last week and want to send them an event announcement. Search for new contacts via Search > Custom Search > Date Added to CiviCRM and use those results as the basis of the mailing. If your organisation stores its event email list in a Group called Event Alerts, you would probably choose Event Alerts as the Unsubscription Group.

If you do not have an appropriate Group for the Unsubscribe Group, you may want to create one called something like "Miscellaneous Mail Unsubscribes". You could add that Group to future mailings to exclude people who have unsubscribed.

docs.title: Choosing recipients: When mailing recipients are set
docs.text:
When you submit a mailing, its recipient list is set based on the contacts who are members of its groups at that moment. The list does not change after scheduling, even if the mailing is scheduled for a month in the future. However, contacts who are opted out, marked do not email, deceased, deleted, or whose email is on hold at the time of sending will not receive the mailing.

For a mailing to a smart group, recipients are set based on the smart group criteria when the mailing is scheduled. They are not updated when it is sent.

If you select All NNN records in search results and send those contacts a mailing from the Actions dropdown menu, you create a hidden smart group. Its members are updated based on the search criteria when the mailing is submitted. To avoid creating a hidden smart group, select all the records using the checkbox at the top of each page, then use NNN Selected records only. This creates a non-smart group whose membership will never update based on the search criteria.

docs.title: The Mailing set-up screens
docs.text:
If you are sending to an existing Group, go to Mailings > New Mailing. You will see this screen:

If you are basing the mailing on search results, perform your search—for example, using Search > Advanced Search—then choose Email - Schedule/Send via CiviMail from the Actions drop down. You will see this screen:

The screens are similar. For a search-based mailing, however, you must choose an Unsubscribe Group, and the "Search Results" group is included in the Recipients list and cannot be removed. The HTML pane is open by default; it was closed to fit the bottom buttons into these images. See Choosing recipients: Groups versus search results.

You can save your mailing at any stage by clicking Save Draft.

docs.title: Mailing Tab
docs.text:
The Mailing tab contains all the compulsory fields for a new mailing. It may be the only tab you need to visit.

  • Mailing Name: Enter a name that lets you and others in your organization identify the mailing’s purpose. Starting each name with a date, such as "2015/04/25 - Monthly Newsletter", is recommended. This makes it easier to include or exclude its recipients in future mailings. The name is for internal use only and is not shown to recipients. You will enter the Subject later.
  • Campaign: Associate the email with a particular campaign if needed.
  • Template: Select an existing message template to populate the HTML Format and Plain-Text Format fields. You can edit the content for this mailing, but you cannot update the template or create a new template through this form. CiviCRM ships with three sample newsletter templates. Users with the Administer CiviCRM permssion can customise them with your organisation’s details, or create new message templates, at Administer > CiviMail > Message Templates.
  • From: This is populated with the default sender email address. You can select another address from the dropdown list. Users with Administer CiviCRM permssion can add addresses at Administer > CiviMail > From Email addresses.
  • Recipients: Choose who will receive the mailing if you are mailing to Groups, or further refine or add recipients if you are mailing to search results. Select Groups to include, shown in green, or exclude, shown in red with a strike-through, from the "Recipients" dropdown. Only groups of the type "Mailing List" are available.

You can also include or exclude recipients of previous mailings. For example, to avoid sending the same email twice to some people, choose the original mailing in "Exclude Past Recipients From". The message will then go only to members of the group who did not receive the original mailing. The estimated final number of recipients appears to the right of the Recipients field, highlighted in yellow.

  • The "wrench": Click the wrench to the right of the Recipients field and to the left of the recipient estimate to access Edit Options.

  • Dedupe by email: CiviCRM always dedupes a mailing based on unique contact records. A contact in three included groups receives only one copy. If multiple contacts use the same email address, this option determines how many copies are sent: unticked sends one per contact; ticked sends one per address. Set the default at Administer > CiviMail > CiviMail Component Settings by ticking or unticking "CiviMail dedupes e-mail addresses by default". You can override the default for any email.

  • Location Type: By default, CiviMail sends to the address location(s) set for "Bulk Mailings" or, if no location type has that setting, to the address location set as "Is Primary". In Edit Options, you can change the Location Type and the Selection Method. You can filter by Location Type to send only to email addresses with the specified location type, or exclude addresses with that location type.

  • Unsubscribe Group (for search-based mailings only): Choose this carefully. See the example in Choosing recipients: Groups versus search results.

  • Subject: This is the subject of the sent emails. You can include tokens. The Subject, not the Mailing Name, is used when creating an activity or mailing record for each contact.
  • HTML (expanding section): Compose the mailing here. You can personalize each email using tokens. If you only want to send a plain text email, ignore the HTML section. Click Plain Text to open that accordion and enter your message.
  • Preview: This panel is a footer to the Define Mailing screen and appears in whichever tab is selected. You can:
  • Preview the HTML or Plain Text version. The HTML preview shows formatting and tokens converted with your data, but not attachments. Email clients are not guaranteed to display the email exactly as shown; the preview can still help you check font consistency, basic layout, and color.
  • Send a test email to a single email address. If the address does not already exist in CiviCRM, a new contact record will be created.
  • Send a test email to an existing group in CiviCRM. The test mailing fills in all the Tokens and includes any attachments you plan to send.

It is a good idea to send a test to yourself and view it in your email client. For a complex layout, send it to your test group and check it in various mail clients; see Testing templates in the Set-up section for more tips. Preferably, more than one person should receive the test and give feedback.

The remaining tabs are:

docs.title: Attachments tab
docs.text: Upload files to send as attachments with your email.

docs.title: Header and Footer tab
docs.text: Each new mailing includes the default Header and default Footer defined at Mailings > Headers, Footers, and Automated Messages. To use different ones, select them on this tab. Define additional Headers and Footers via Mailings > Headers, Footers, and Automated Messages (see Set-Up for details).

docs.title: Publication tab
docs.text:
Mailing Visibility has two options: "User and User Admin Only" and "Public Pages."

  • Public Pages makes the content viewable as a web page by everyone with the "View public CiviMail content" permission.
  • "User and User Admin Only" means that only users who received the mailing or administrators can view its content as a web page. Recipients must log in to view the message.

To link to the web version, insert the Mailing permalink token in your email message. It generates a URL where the message can be viewed. To display it properly in HTML messages, add the proper link tags using the Source icon in the editor.

docs.title: Responses tab
docs.text:
• Track Replies checkbox: Sends recipients’ replies to a CiviMail specific address rather than the sender’s address, so they can be stored in CiviCRM. Checking it reveals two options:
  • Forward Replies: Check this if you also want the From address to receive recipients’ replies.
  • Auto-respond to Replies: Send a specific automatic reply to anyone who replies. Set up an autoresponder ahead of time in Mailings > Headers, Footers, and Automated Messages.
  • Opt-Out Message: Sent to a recipient who has opted-out from all the mailing lists.
  • Resubscribe Message: Sent to a recipient who has resubscribed to one of the mailing lists.
  • Unsubscribe Message: Sent to a recipient who has unsubscribed from one of the mailing lists.

You can edit these three messages at Mailings > Headers, Footers, and Automated Messages.

docs.title: Tracking tab
docs.text:
• Track Click-Throughs: Tracks how many users, and which users, clicked links in your message. All links are redirected through your server and overwritten with custom links containing your domain name.

!!! note "Note for HTML mail" Some phishing filters may mark links displayed differently in HTML code and in the text as unsafe. It is therefore best not to use something like <a href="http://example.com">http://Example.com</a> but rather use <a href="http://example.com">click here to go to Example</a> instead.

!!! note "Note for Plain Text Email" If you use short, user-friendly URLs, they will all be overwritten with long links containing the name of your site and a long code looking like this http://example.com/sites/all/modules/civicrm/extern/url.php?u=529&qid=29011.

  • Track Opens: Tracks how many people opened the email they received. This method has limitations: if a recipient does not show images in their email client—often called "blocking remote content"—their email will not be marked as opened, even if they open it. Blocking remote content is common.

You can set whether Click Through and Open Tracking are on or off by default at Administer > CiviMail > CiviMail Component Settings.

Once you have defined the mailing, click Next > at the lower left.

docs.title: Review Panel
docs.text:
This panel summarizes the email’s details. The blue words are buttons:

  • ~XX recipients shows the names and email addresses of the contacts who will be sent the email.
  • HTML and Plain Text show the email to be sent, including any header or footer.
  • Each envelope displays the named message.

Ticks and crosses with strike-throughs show which tracking and response options you have and have not chosen. Use the panel to confirm your choices.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
Choose to send the email immediately or schedule a date and time, then click Submit Mailing. By default, CiviMail checks every 15 minutes for emails ready to send, so the start could be delayed by up to 15 minutes.

Mailings to large numbers of recipients are sent in batches of about 400 to reduce the likelihood of being caught in spam filters. Sending can therefore take several hours, depending on your server configuration.

docs.title: Tracking Sent Mass Mailings
docs.text:
To review statistics for a past mailing, go to Mailings > Scheduled and Sent Mailings. Find the mailing in the list or use the filters above it, then click Report in the "action" column. The report shows tracked actions, including the number of opens, link click-throughs, and the percentage of bounces (see Managing bounces below).

Click a statistic’s name to see the contacts it applies to and other details, such as the time an email was opened for tracked opens. Where a mass mailing has been sent to a contact, you can also view its "Bulk Email" record in the Activities tab of that contact’s profile.

To filter further—for example, to find recipients who opened the email and are between 21 and 30 years old, or registered for a given event—click Advanced Search next to a statistic. This starts an advanced search with the email attributes pre-filled. Clicking the link next to Tracked Opens, for example, sets the search fields to find contacts who opened the email, ready for you to add criteria. For more information, see Searching.

docs.title: Managing Mass Mailings
docs.text:
Mass mailings appear in three areas under the Mailings menu:

  • Draft and Unscheduled Mailings: As soon as you name a message in Step 1 and click Next, it appears here. If you click Save & Continue Later or abandon a message after some steps, click Continue next to it to resume work. You can also Delete drafts here.
  • Scheduled and Sent Mailings: A mailing you send or schedule stays here until it is archived or deleted. Click Report to track delivery, or Copy to start another mailing based on it. Archive and Delete are under more. For a mailing that is scheduled but not yet sent, Cancel is available instead of Archive. Pause and Resume are also under more. Pausing is gradual, not instantaneous; you can use it when you want another scheduled or pending mailing to send before the one you pause.
  • Archived Mailings: This area lists messages archived from Scheduled and Sent Mailings. They cannot be included in or excluded from a recipient list. The area otherwise has the same functionality as Scheduled and Sent Mailings, including viewing Reports and using Copy.

docs.title: Modifying system workflow message templates
docs.text:
The content and layout of these messages are pre-configured. They include program logic to display data sent to constituents, such as contribution amounts, payment methods and event fees.

Navigate to Administer > Communication > Message Templates and click the System Workflow Message tab to see the messages you can modify. Both HTML and Text formats are provided. Your organization may want to modify or add text, or add branding such as a logo to the HTML versions.

Your changes here can complicate CiviCRM upgrades

CiviCRM occasionally changes system workflow message templates during version upgrades. If you customize a template, CiviCRM stops applying updates to it. This preserves your changes, but you might miss important template updates as new functionality becomes available.

The System Administrator Guide has instructions for merging conflicting edits to these templates when you have customized a template and a CiviCRM upgrade would also have changed it. The process is not easy, so avoiding edits can save you or your system administrator time.

Don't break anything

Do not modify the program logic in these templates. Test the workflow and review the emails sent after making changes. In most cases, you can restrict changes to the top row in the HTML layout. If changes cause problems, errors or missing information, you can revert to the system default for that workflow.

Use tokens for logo and branding

As of CiviCRM 5.76, you do not need to edit Message Templates to insert your organization logo or other branding. Instead, use the {site.message_header} Site Token.

After customizing a system workflow message template, you can revert to CiviCRM’s version by clicking the "Revert to Default" link next to the template.

docs.title: Variables and tokens in workflow message templates
docs.text:
Workflow message templates can use both tokens and Smarty variables. A dollar sign distinguishes a Smarty variable from a token: {contribution.tax_amount} is a token, whereas {$taxAmount} and {$contribution.tax_amount} are Smarty variables.

In general, tokens are consistent across multiple screens. Available Smarty variables depend on what has been coded and vary considerably. CiviCRM is switching to tokens in workflow message templates where possible, but some variables are specific to a message template or are more complex. Work is underway to standardize and document the available Smarty variables.

As of 5.53, all contribution workflow message templates should support all contact and contribution tokens and the following Smarty variables:

Variable Meaning Detail eg. $isShowLineItems is the contribution using a price set TRUE or FALSE {if $isShowLineItems}...{/if} $isShowTax is sales tax enabled for the site TRUE or FALSE {if $isShowTax}...{/if} $taxRateBreakDown array of the amount charged at each tax rate. [] for no tax or {foreach from=$taxRateBreakdown item=taxDetail key=taxRate}{$taxDetail.percentage}%{/if}{/foreach}

$lineItem is an array of line items. Example usage:

  {if $isShowLineItems}
    <tr>
    <td colspan="2" {$valueStyle}>
      <table>
      <tr>
        <th>{ts}Item{/ts}</th>
        <th>{ts}Qty{/ts}</th>
        <th>{ts}Each{/ts}</th>
        {if $isShowTax && '{contribution.tax_amount|raw}' !== '0.00'}
          <th>{ts}Subtotal{/ts}</th>
          <th>{ts}Tax Rate{/ts}</th>
          <th>{ts}Tax Amount{/ts}</th>
        {/if}
        <th>{ts}Total{/ts}</th>
      </tr>
      {foreach from=$lineItems item=line}
        <tr>
        <td>
          {$line.title}
        </td>
        <td>
          {$line.qty}
        </td>
        <td>
          {$line.unit_price|crmMoney:'{contribution.currency}'}
        </td>
        {if $isShowTax && '{contribution.tax_amount|raw}' !== '0.00'}
          <td>
            {$line.unit_price*$line.qty|crmMoney:'{contribution.currency}'}
          </td>
          {if $line.tax_rate || $line.tax_amount != ""}
            <td>
              {$line.tax_rate|string_format:"%.2f"}%
            </td>
            <td>
              {$line.tax_amount|crmMoney:'{contribution.currency}'}
            </td>
          {else}
            <td></td>
            <td></td>
          {/if}
        {/if}
        <td>
          {$line.line_total+$line.tax_amount|crmMoney:'{contribution.currency}'}
        </td>
        </tr>
      {/foreach}
      </table>
    </td>
    </tr>

  {/if}

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Message templates let you reuse entire emails or parts of emails in mass mailings and when using the Send Email activity.

CiviCRM has two categories of Message Templates:

  • User-driven Messages are created by staff to communicate with constituents and be reused. Examples include thank-you letters and meeting announcements.
  • System Workflow Messages are pre-configured messages used by CiviCRM features. Examples include contribution receipts and event registration confirmations.

docs.title: Creating user-driven templates
docs.text:
The easiest way to create a message template is to check Save as New Template on the message creation screen. This option is available when using the Send Email activity and when sending a mass mailing.

You can also create templates from scratch or edit existing templates at Mailings > Message Templates or Administer > Communications > Message Templates.

  1. Click Add Message Template.
  2. Enter a Message Title and a Message Subject. You can use tokens to personalize the subject line.
  3. Scroll down to the HTML Format section and create your template. Online resources that are not specific to CiviCRM offer instructions for creating HTML email templates. One approach is to find and copy an email template from a website that offers samples.
  4. To paste HTML from an external template, write HTML directly, or modify HTML created in the WYSIWYG editor, switch to the code view using the toolbar icon called "Source". Its appearance and label vary depending on whether you use Drupal, Joomla, or WordPress.

Message templates are available even when CiviMail is disabled.

docs.title: Full HTML documents
docs.text:
Some HTML content pasted into a User-Driven template—for example, content copied from an email design tool or an older CiviCRM sample template—is a full HTML document. It has its own <!DOCTYPE>, <html>, <head> and <body> tags, rather than just the content that goes inside the body of an email.

If you switch such a template to the rich text (WYSIWYG) editor, only the content inside <body> is kept. The <!DOCTYPE>, <html> and <head> wrapper, and anything in it, is discarded. CiviCRM warns you before this happens.

In most cases, this is harmless: when CiviMail sends a User-Driven message, it combines a separate Header, the message itself, and a separate Footer into one email. The message template therefore only needed the inner content.

It is not harmless if something in the document’s <head> is required for how the email displays. A common example is a <style> block used to make the layout responsive on different screen sizes, such as one using a <meta name="viewport"> tag and media queries. Switching a template like this to the rich text editor will silently drop the styling that makes it responsive. If you are unsure, keep editing in Raw HTML mode or check with whoever built the template.

docs.title: Tips for creating templates
docs.text:
HTML allowed in emails is more restricted than HTML used for web pages. For instance, it needs tables for layout and inline CSS, and must not include background images. These tips can help a template display well in mail clients:

  • Table border: The HTML <table> element has an optional border attribute. Its default value is 0, so it does not appear unless you set it. Setting it to 1—for example, <table border="1">—makes table edges visible and can help identify layout problems. HTML email templates usually have multiple tables, including nested tables. Make changes one at a time and switch to the HTML view to see the results. A table usually has more than one parameter, so leave spaces between parameters.
  • Table cellpadding and cellspacing: These table parameters can improve readability. Try different settings in different tables.
  • Width: Do not send an email wider than 600 pixels, to ensure maximum compatibility across email clients. Keep the outermost table and any tables inside it within 600 pixels. Keep the total width of each image within 600 pixels too. An image’s horizontal padding parameter can increase its width beyond its width parameter.
  • Images: Images need to be online and accessible. Edit each image to an appropriate width and height, then save it with as small a file size as possible. Free online resources can help you resize images if you do not have image-editing software or do not know how to use it.
  • HTML editor: CiviCRM comes with two WYSIWYG editors, CKEditor and TinyMCE, and Textarea, a plain text editor. If another editor is configured as part of your Drupal, Joomla, or WordPress installation, you can use it instead. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Display Preferences and select a different WYSIWYG Editor.

docs.title: Plain text and HTML formats
docs.text:
All messages can be sent in either plain text or HTML. Today, the vast majority of people use email clients that can read HTML messages.

It is good practice to send a plain text version as well as an HTML version so that all recipients can view the message. There are two ways to do this:

  1. Recommended: Leave the text version fully blank. During sending, a text version will be generated from the HTML version.
  2. Enter a text version in the text box on the message template screen. You will need to keep it up to date manually. This takes time, and if the text version is not maintained, people using plain text-only email clients may receive an incorrect or incomplete message. This may include visually impaired people whose email-reading software prefers the text version.

To create a plain text version manually from HTML:

  1. Copy and paste the text from the HTML Format field into the Plain Text Format field. Do this from the WYSIWYG view, not the Source view: you need the text, not the code. The plain text field automatically strips formatting and other elements that do not work in plain text.
  2. Copy the URLs of all links to the appropriate places in the Plain Text Format field.
  3. If the HTML version contains tables, modify the text layout manually to make it readable.

docs.title: Configure message templates
docs.text:
To configure message templates, begin at the Administer CiviCRM page. In the Communications section, choose Message Templates.

You will see a list of existing templates. If none exist, you will see:

There are no Message Templates entered. You can add one.

Click add one to create a template.

You can create NEW message templates or use the links to the right of each existing template to Edit, Preview, Disable or Delete it.

docs.title: NEW
docs.text:
To create a NEW message template, choose >>New Message Template. You will be taken to the New Message Template page.

Create a Message Title. This title organizes your messages and will not appear in the email.

Tokens

The next three fields can all use tokens to personalize messages with names, dates, amounts of gifts and other details.

Here is a list of the tokens you can use

Create the Message Subject for your email. Use tokens if desired.

Create your HTML Message. Include tokens to personalize your messages.

Leave Text Message blank unless you have a strong reason not to.

Choose Enabled? to enable the message template for use.

Click Save to save the template or Cancel to cancel.

If successful, you will see:

"The Message Template "Membership Renewal Initial Message" has been saved."

docs.title: EXISTING
docs.text: For EXISTING templates, you can Edit, Disable or Delete each template using the links to its right.

docs.title: EDIT
docs.text:
Select Edit to open the Edit Template page, where you can change each option. You can also enable or disable the template by checking or unchecking Enabled? at the bottom of the page. Click Save to save the template.

If successful, you will see:

The Message Template "Membership Renewal Initial Message" has been saved.

docs.title: DISABLE
docs.text:
Select Disable to temporarily disable an Existing Template. You will see:

"Are you sure you want to disable this Message Template? "

Click OK to continue or Cancel to cancel. To re-enable the template, click Enable.

docs.title: DELETE
docs.text:
Select Delete to delete the template. You will see:

Do you want to delete this message template?

Click Delete to continue or Cancel to cancel the deletion.

docs.title: Reports and analysis
docs.text: CiviMail has tools for reporting and analysis; reporting is one of the key reasons to use CiviMail.

docs.title: Individual mail reports
docs.text: You can view a report for each mailing from Mailings > Scheduled and Sent Mailings. Reports use live information, so you can track emails in real time by refreshing the page. Each report has several sections. The data available depends on which items you enabled tracking for when you set up the mailing.

docs.title: Delivery summary
docs.text:
The delivery summary shows high-level statistics about the mailing. Clicking its links shows lists of contacts who took the corresponding actions.

  • Intended Recipients shows the number of people the mailing was intended to reach.
  • Unique Opens shows the number of people (or bots) that CiviCRM thinks have opened the email if you have chosen to enable Open tracking.
  • Total Opens shows the total number of times that CiviCRM thinks people (or bots) have opened the email if you have chosen to enable Open tracking.

How Open Tracking works

In the world of email, there is no 100% reliable way of knowing when someone has opened an email. CiviCRM uses a trick that is common amongst mass mailers — it embeds a small image with a unique name in each email. When a client views the email and downloads the image, CiviCRM knows that they have read the email. Because this technique is common, to protect people's privacy, most email clients ask users to confirm whether they want to download images in emails. Hence your report really tells you the number of people who downloaded the images; the actual number of readers is higher than the number reported. Tracked opens statistics should be taken as indicative, rather than accurate. In our experience, a 30% reported opening rate can be considered good. This is obviously different for each organisation and each group you send emails to.

Do not focus too much on the absolute numbers. Instead, use them to compare mailings. You might experiment with layouts, writing styles, and lengths to see what works best for your constituents.

  • Click-throughs shows the total number of times people have clicked links in your email if you have enabled click tracking.
  • Forwards shows the number of times people have forwarded the email using the forward link, a token that you can include in your mailing.
  • Replies shows the number of times people have replied to the email if you have enabled reply tracking.
  • Bounces shows the number of email addresses that could not be successfully delivered to if you have enabled bounce processing.
  • Unsubscribe requests shows the number of people who have clicked any unsubscribe links included in your email.

docs.title: Click-through summary
docs.text: This section shows two statistics for each link: Clicks, the number of times the link has been clicked, and Unique clicks, the number of people who have clicked on links.

docs.title: Managing bounces and contacts with invalid emails
docs.text:
If your server is set up to process bounces, contacts will be marked as On Hold when their email bounces. Further messages to those addresses will be suppressed. You can search for emails that are on hold from the Bounces report or with an advanced search, then investigate why the emails are bouncing.

Review bounces by clicking the Bounces link in the Delivery Summary. You can see the reasons for individual bounces, such as an incorrect email address (e.g., contact@gooogle.com), fix them, and remove their On Hold status. You can then re-use the mailing and simply add it to the EXCLUDE Recipients of These Mailing(s) list on the Select Recipients screen of the re-used mailing setup.

In the Mailings area of Search > Advanced search, you can search by bounce type.

docs.title: Mailing reports with CiviReport
docs.text:
CiviReport has four reports—Mail Bounce Report, Mail Summary Report, Mail Clickthrough Report, and Mail Opened Report—that offer similar functionality to the reports described above. Using CiviReport from the Reports menu has two main advantages:

  • You can run reports for multiple mailings.
  • You can use other CiviReport features, including adding reports to dashboards and getting reports emailed.

Read the Reporting section for more information.

docs.title: Scheduled reminders
docs.text:
Scheduled reminders automatically send email or SMS messages to contacts when certain criteria are met. For example, you can send participants an SMS the day before a training course, or send contacts a series of membership renewal emails as their membership end date approaches.

Scheduled reminders are available for these CiviCRM components (Entities):

  • Contacts
  • Activities
  • Memberships
  • Events
  • Contributions

You can create reminders for these components at Administer > Communications > Schedule Reminders. You can also set up event reminders on the event configuration pages.

docs.title: Tokens available to scheduled reminders
docs.text:
In addition to the standard tokens available in CiviMail, scheduled reminder messages can contain tokens for the events, activities, contributions, and memberships they relate to. This lets you use one reminder template for different events, membership types, contribution types, or activity types.

In event messages, a token such as event location is replaced with the location of the specific event. In membership messages, you can use each individual’s expiry date. Membership and event ID tokens are also available and can be used to create links to specific pages, such as the membership renewal page.

The checksum token lets you authenticate people to specific pages without requiring them to log in, and show forms with details already filled in.

docs.title: Creating and managing scheduled reminders
docs.text:
Create a reminder at Administer > Communications > Schedule Reminders or during the creation of an event. The options shown when you click Add Reminder depend on the Entity you choose, but the general process is similar for all reminders.

  1. Give the reminder a name that will help you and others identify it.
  2. Select the required Entity. The options you can base the reminder on appear in the adjacent window. This is a multi-select field, so you can choose more than one option. Depending on your selection in the middle field, a third set of options appears in the right box. This is usually also a multi-select field.
  3. Choose when to send the reminder: on a set date, or an amount of time before or after the start or end of your chosen entity.
  4. Check the Repeat box if you want to send the reminder more than once to the same group of people. You can then choose the interval and when repetition should end.
  5. Check Record activity for automated email if you want a record of the contacts who received the reminder.
  6. Fill in From Name and/or From Email if you do not want the reminder to come from your site’s default name and email address.
  7. Limit or add to the recipient list. See Limiting or adding to your recipient list below.

  8. Choose to send the reminder as an email, an SMS, or either, depending on the contact’s preferred method(s) of communications.

    Note

    The SMS option will only be available if you have set up an SMS Gateway

  9. Compose the message using Message Templates or write it from scratch.

  10. Click Save when you are done.

You can edit, disable, or delete reminders at Administer > Communications > Schedule Reminders.

Warning

Your system administrator will need to ensure that the Send Scheduled Reminders scheduled job is enabled and runs at least once a day. Refer to the Scheduled Jobs section for configuration details.

docs.title: Using scheduled reminders for contacts
docs.text:
Contact reminders can be based on:

  • Birth Date
  • The date the contact record was created (Created Date)
  • The date the contact record was modified (Modified Date)
  • Custom contact date fields, such as a marriage date or the date a qualification expires

You can send a reminder every year on the same date (an anniversary), particularly for birthdays or marriages. Alternatively, you can send it only once in relation to the actual date, as you might for an expiring qualification.

By default, reminders created from this screen apply to all contacts with dates set for the specified field. To send a reminder to only some of those contacts—for example, birthday greetings to children but not adults—limit the recipients as described in Limiting or adding to your recipient list below.

docs.title: Using scheduled reminders for activities
docs.text:
Activity reminders can be based on any combination of core and custom activity types. Options include:

  • Send to contacts with the specified activity types and any combination of activity statuses, such as scheduled, completed, or cancelled.
  • Send only to Activity Assignees (contacts in the Assigned To field), Activity Targets (contacts in the With Contact field), or Activity Sources (the logged-in user who added the Activity) for the specified activity types and statuses. See Limiting or adding to your recipient list below.

For example, you could:

  • Log calls with major donors using the Phone Call activity and automatically email your executive director the Activity Details.
  • Remind staff about interviews they are assigned to conduct.
  • Notify the person who scheduled an activity that it has been completed.
  • Send thank-you notes to people who met with you.

docs.title: Using scheduled reminders for contributions
docs.text:
You can send emails to contributors based on the page they donated through or the contribution/financial type of their donation. Options include:

  • Send to contacts who contributed through the selected contribution page(s), with any combination of contribution statuses.
  • Send to contacts who made a contribution of the selected financial type(s), with any combination of contribution statuses.

docs.title: Using scheduled reminders for memberships
docs.text:
You can send messages to members based on membership characteristics, including membership type and status. For example, you could send current members renewal reminders 1 month before their membership end date, or “sorry you are leaving” emails 1 week after it. You could also send membership engagement letters 2 weeks after the membership start date to remind members of their benefits.

As well as sending emails based on memberships, you can send emails based on membership-related activities, such as Membership Signup. The payment reminder example below uses that activity.

docs.title: Renewal reminders
docs.text:
To email members 5 days before their membership expires:

  1. Set Entity Type to Membership.
  2. Select one or more Membership Types.
  3. If the selected membership types allow auto-renewal, you may want to send this reminder only for memberships that do NOT renew automatically.
  4. Set 'When' to 5 days before Membership End Date.
  5. Do not select Repeat.
  6. Check 'Send Email' and choose the Template, or create and save one.

What to include in a renewal email is discussed in Renewals in the CiviMember section.

Note

If a member renews, they will receive their next reminder 5 days before their new Membership End Date.

docs.title: Chasing members who have not sent membership payments
docs.text:
To remind contacts whose memberships are pending because payment has not been received:

  1. Create a smart group for contacts with a membership status of pending.
  2. In scheduled reminders, set Entity Type to Activity, Membership Signup, Completed. This uses the Activity entity, not the Membership entity.
  3. Restrict Recipients to the membership pending smart group. Without this restriction, all members—including those who have already paid—will receive the message.
