docs.title: Using scheduled reminders for events
docs.text:
Set up event reminders from the Scheduled Reminders administration screen or from the Schedule Reminders screen in the event configuration workflow. To reach the event screen, click the Schedule Reminders tab when setting up an Event, or Configure > Schedule Reminders next to your event on the Manage Events screen. The configuration steps are the same as on the administration screen.

A reminder set up from the event configuration screen applies only to that event. To send reminders for all events of a certain type—for example, evaluation forms after workshops—use the Scheduled Reminders administration screen.

Event-specific options include:

  • Send to participants in specific event(s) or in all events of given type(s), such as conferences or meetings.
  • Send to all participants in the chosen events or only those with specified participant statuses, such as registered and attended, or cancelled and no-show.
  • Send to all participant roles with the appropriate statuses or only specified roles, such as volunteer or host.

For example, you could:

  • Email volunteers for an annual fundraising dinner the day before the event to remind them when to arrive.
  • Send fundraising emails to attendees of all your training courses the day after the courses are held.
  • Ask event attendees for feedback.
  • Send a thank-you email to event speakers and hosts.
  • Email people who registered but did not show up to ask why.

docs.title: When scheduled reminders for events are or aren't sent
docs.text:
A reminder set for a specific date is sent only on that date. Contacts who registered before that date receive it the first time the Send Scheduled Reminders cron job runs on that date (likely shortly after midnight). Contacts who register on that date receive it shortly after registering. Contacts who register after that date do not receive it.

A reminder set relative to the event start or end—for example, 24 hours before the event start—will generally also be sent to contacts who register after that time. Specifically, a reminder set for any time before the event start or end is sent to all registrants who register before the event ends. A reminder set for any time after the event start or end is sent to any registrant, regardless of when they register.

Similarly, a reminder set before the registration start or end is sent to any contacts who register up to the registration end. Reminders set for after the registration start or end are not sent at all.

docs.title: Limiting or adding to your recipient list
docs.text:
You select recipients based on entity-specific characteristics, such as event type and participant status, membership type and auto-renew options, activity type and status, or an entry in a contact date field.

For activity reminders, you can further limit recipients using the Recipient field. Choose Activity Assignees, Activity Source, or Activity Targets; a predefined group using (Select a group); or contacts you specify using (Choose recipient(s)). Selected groups or contacts receive the reminder only if they meet all its other criteria.

For Event, Contact, and Membership reminders, you can limit recipients to a group, a participant role (Event reminders only), or manually selected contacts. Set Limit or Add Recipients to Limit to, then choose Select a group, Choose recipient(s), or Participant Role (Event reminders only) from the adjacent option list. For example, you could send birthday greetings only to members who are less than 12 years old.

As with activity reminders, groups, manual recipients, or roles selected with Limit to receive the reminder only if they meet all its other criteria.

To send a reminder to contacts who do not meet its general criteria, set Limit or Add Recipients to Also include. You can then select a group or an individual who will receive the reminder even if they do not meet the other criteria. For example, you could send an event reminder to registrants 2 days before the event and also send it to Bob Adams, your office manager, so he remembers to check the room configuration and equipment.

docs.title: What can cause scheduled reminders not to be sent?
docs.text:
First, use Find Activities to check whether the reminder was sent. Specify an Activity Type of Reminder Sent, or Membership Renewal Reminder for membership renewals.

If you find matching Activities for the contacts, another issue, such as email delivery, may explain why a contact did not receive the reminder.

If you find no Reminder Sent or Membership Renewal Reminder Activities, consider these conditions:

  1. The contact is deleted.
  2. The contact is deceased.
  3. The contact has Do not email enabled.
  4. The contact email address is On hold.
  5. For a Membership Renewal Reminder, the Membership Status Override? option is enabled. When Status Override is active, the selected status remains in force. No Membership Renewal Reminder is sent.
  6. The Send Scheduled Reminders Scheduled Job is not enabled or is not configured to run Always. This job must execute when the reminder criteria are met. If its execution is delayed, Scheduled Reminder criteria will be skipped.
  7. The Scheduled Reminder is disabled.
  8. The Scheduled Reminder has the Limit or Add Recipients Limit To option set, and it does not include the target contact.
  9. No Scheduled Reminders match the contact’s criteria.
  10. The Scheduled Reminder has a When (trigger date) that has past or otherwise has not been met.

docs.title: Scheduled reminders and privacy options, on hold
docs.text:
Scheduled reminders are still sent to contacts who have opted out of bulk emails. Sometimes this is appropriate: they may still want reminders about an event they registered for or an upcoming membership renewal. In other situations, it is not appropriate.

Scheduled reminders are not sent to contacts with the Do not email privacy option or an email address that is On hold.

To exclude contacts who have opted out of bulk emails from a scheduled reminder:

  1. Find all contacts who have not selected the privacy options "Do not email" or NO BULK EMAIL. You can use the Search Builder at Search > Search Builder, with the settings shown below.
  2. Create a smart group from the search results.
  3. Select that smart group as the Recipients of the scheduled reminder.

docs.title: Allow people to sign up for mailing lists online
docs.text:
CiviCRM makes it possible for people to sign themselves up for your mailing lists online.

To allow this, you must designate the group as a mailing list. If you didn't do this when you created the Group, go to Contacts > Manage Groups. Click Settings on the group that holds your mailing list recipients and check the Mailing List next to Group Type. You must also change the Visibility to Public Pages.

For this to work for users who don't have a log-in to your CiviCRM, you must ensure that anonymous users in Drupal have the following permission checked: "Access CiviMail subscribe/unsubscribe pages."

docs.title: Use the subscribe link
docs.text:
One way to allow users to subscribe to an email list online is by directing them to:

  • Drupal: example.org/civicrm/mailing/subscribe
  • Backdrop: example.org/civicrm/mailing/subscribe
  • WordPress with clean URLs: example.org/civicrm/mailing/subscribe?reset=1
  • WordPress without clean URLs (the default for CiviCRM instances installed before version 5.13): example.org/civicrm?page=CiviCRM&q=civicrm/mailing/subscribe&reset=1
  • Joomla: example.org/administrator/index2.php?option=com_civicrm&task=civicrm/mailing/subscribe&reset=1

You and anyone who accesses this link can subscribe to the available mailing list groups.

docs.title: Use a profile
docs.text:
Alternatively, you can use profiles to collect more information from people who sign up to your mailing list.

For example, you could create a new Profile called Newsletter Sign-up. Add to this profile the fields that you'd like website visitors who want to join your mailing list to fill out. Each of the fields in the profile must have its Visibility set to Public Pages.

For each field you include, you can choose whether it is required or optional for people filling out the public form. The one exception is that the profile must include an email field that is required. This is so that an email can be sent to the person to confirm that they wanted to sign up for the mailing list. Until they confirm, they will have a status of "Pending" in the mailing list group.

There are two ways to display the profile publicly:

  1. Share a link directly. Return to the listing of profiles (at Administer > Custom Data and Screens > Profiles) and click More to the far right of your profile. Click Use Profile-Create Mode. Your browser will open up the public page; you can publish this link to allow users to sign up for your mailing lists.
  2. Embed this set of fields as a form in your website. Return to the listing of profiles (at Administer > Custom Data and Screens > Profiles) and click More to the far right of your profile. Select HTML Form Snippet. This will open a window in your browser that has a box with HTML code in it. Copy and paste the contents of the box into a page on your website. Website visitors will be able to sign up to your mailing lists on this page.

Alternatively, for WordPress you can display the form publicly by using a shortcode. On any WordPress Page, click the CiviCRM button above the editor. For Page Type select Profile. On the next drop-down that appears, select the name of the profile that you have created. Select Edit on the radio button option just below the drop-downs, so that you give users access to edit data in your database (i.e. to add their email address and name to your database). Click Insert Form and the shortcode will be added to the editor.

docs.title: Use a Webform (Drupal)
docs.text:
Many Drupal site administrators prefer to use a webform instead of a profile to create their newsletter sign-up, because it provides additional features such as advanced spam control and flexible theming. For more information see:

http://wiki.civicrm.org/confluence/display/CRMDOC/Webform+CiviCRM+Integration

docs.title: Add people to your mailing list group by using a profile
docs.text:
To get a user automatically added to your mail list group(s) when they fill out your Newsletter Sign-up form (CiviCRM profile), you have two options:

Option A: On the profile, you can add a field for the mailing lists groups that you want users to be able to sign up for. Go to the profile's fields and click Add Field. For Field Name, select Contacts. When the possible selections load in the second field, select Group(s). In Field Label, you can leave "Group(s)" or you may want to change it to something more intuitive to your website visitors such as "Newsletter Sign-up." Visibility for this field must be set to Public Pages. When the profile displays publicly, this field will show check boxes for all Mailing List Groups that have their Visibility set to Public Pages. This way users can add themselves to all of your Mailing List Groups that they want to by putting a tick on the appropriate checkboxes.

Option B: Go to the profile settings. In the Advanced Settings section, select your desired Mailing List Group for Add new contacts to a Group?. Now when users fill out your form, they will be automatically added to this group.

docs.title: Mailing list confirmation workflow
docs.text:
For this to work, first make sure that you have put a tick on the desired Enable Double Opt-in options in Administer > Administration Console > CiviMail Component Settings.

After people subscribe to mailing list groups — via the subscribe link or a profile — CiviCRM will automatically send them an email asking them to confirm their subscription. Until they click the confirmation link in the email, their contact information will appear in CiviCRM with their group subscription set to Pending. When they confirm, CiviCRM will automatically change their group subscription status to Added and they will be sent a welcome message.

Note

When users subscribe to multiple groups at once, a confirmation email is sent for each group separately.

docs.title: Configure automated messages, headers, and footers
Automated messages and mailing list management
docs.text:
CiviCRM sends emails automatically when your participants take certain actions:

  • When someone signs up for a mailing list, they get a confirmation email with a link that they must click.
  • When they confirm, they get a welcome email.
  • When they unsubscribe, opt-out of all emails from your domain, or resubscribe to a list they have previously unsubscribed from, they get a confirmation email that does not require any action.
  • When they reply to a message you have sent through CiviMail, you can set up an autoresponse to their reply.

In CiviCRM, these are called Automated Messages, and you can edit them and add new ones at Mailings > Headers, Footers, and Automated Messages.

For more information on email list management see Maintaining healthy email lists which explores how CiviCRM handles unsubscribes, bounces and email holds.

docs.title: Create headers and footers
docs.text:
Headers and footers can be used only in mass mailings using CiviMail. They are not available unless CiviMail is enabled.

The header is the area at the top of the email; it should include elements that you want to be displayed before the main content body, such as the logo of your organization and the title of the newsletter.

The footer is always the last thing in the email. The footer is an ideal place for the compulsory unsubscribe tokens.

You can manage the content of headers and footers in Mailings > Headers, Footers, and Automated Messages. You can create different headers and footers for different purposes; for example, you might want to create a set of headers with different images and titles that can be used for different campaigns or programs. It is recommended to style them similarly, to present a coherent visual identity across all your messages.

After headers and footers are configured, staff who prepare a new mailing will be able to select them from available headers and footers. This helps staff create more standardized mailings with elements that help your readers identify the contents of the mailing or find information.

Like the Message Templates, headers and footers have both a text and an HTML version. Unlike Message Templates, however, the header and footer creation pages do not offer a WYSIWYG editor. You will need to write header and footer HTML directly or use another HTML editor to produce the HTML code.

docs.title: Test templates
docs.text:
Once your templates are ready, we strongly recommend that you test them in various email clients, such as Mozilla Thunderbird, MS Outlook, Mac Mail and web-based e-mail such as Gmail, Yahoo and Hotmail. An easy way to do this is to create a group that includes a test contact for each of those destinations and use it each time you create a new mailing.

Because email clients can display the HTML very differently from each other, we recommend that you keep the HTML as simple as possible and use only inline CSS or tables for formatting. Include as much of the layout as possible in the templates so that each new mailing will not require too much reviewing, since the template will have already been tested.

docs.title: Auto-file email conversations in CiviCRM
docs.text:
It is possible to have emails sent to and from your regular email client automatically filed in CiviCRM. This is done by including a designated email address in the To, Cc, or Bcc field (Bcc is recommended, as it is invisible to the recipient.) Emails that include this designated email get filed as an activity for the contact(s) that match the other email addresses in the From, To, and Cc fields. If any of these email addresses are not already in the system, a new contact record will be created. (Technically, this can work for inbound emails as well; however, it does depend on the person sending the mail to you including the auto-filing address in the To, Cc, or Bcc field.)

For this, your administrator should have configured IMAP or other mail accounts and set them up in CiviMail (see Email System Configuration, especially Adding an incoming email account for handling bounces or auto filing to CiviMail, in Initial Set-Up for more details).

docs.title: Allow users to edit inbound e-mails
docs.text:
Activities created by CiviCRM as a result of email-to-activity processing are not editable by users, as there is a restriction enforced on the Inbound Email activity type. To allow users to be able to edit these activities, an administrator can enable the CiviCRM: edit inbound email basic information or the CiviCRM: edit inbound email basic information and content permissions for the roles that require it.

CiviCRM: edit inbound email basic information will allow users to edit every field of the activity, except the original message, stored in the activity's details.

CiviCRM: edit inbound email basic information and content will allow users to edit every field of the activity, including the original message's content.

docs.title: Set up CiviMail for mass mailings
docs.text: This page describes how to set up information such as From email addresses and Mailing List Groups. It assumes that the basic functionality necessary for your server to send and process emails has already been configured. See CiviMail Setup in the System Administrator Guide for details.

docs.title: Configure your organisation's contact information
docs.text:
To send mass emails, you must fill in your organisation's name, a short description, your email address, and your postal address. CiviMail requires that you include the sender's postal address along with unsubscribe/opt-out links in any mass mailing you send, in order to comply with privacy laws in many countries. This information is made available via tokens and must be included in any mail sent with CiviMail.

To configure this information, go to Administer > Communications > Organization Address and Contact Info.

docs.title: Mailing groups
docs.text:
CiviMail uses Groups to organise recipients of mass mailings. To create a group, go to Contacts > New Group. When you create and configure a Group for this purpose, make sure to check Mailing List under Group Type so that it is available as a Mailing List in CiviMail. You can then do a search and add contacts to the Group.

You can also create Smart Groups based on search results, which will update the Group with any contacts that fit the search criteria. For example, based on the results of Advanced Search you can create a Smart Group of contacts who have active memberships, or a Smart Group of contacts in a given city. As people become members or move to the city you've searched on, they will be automatically added to the Smart Group. This makes it possible to send mailings without having to first update the contacts in a group.

To create a Smart Group:

  1. Go to Advanced Search or Find Contact and run a search query based on the criteria for your group.
  2. On the search results page, click the radio button that selects all the records.
  3. From the Actions drop-down menu, select Group - create smart group.
  4. The next screen provides a review of the criteria chosen for the Smart Group. Give the Smart Group a name and (optionally) a description, and make the Smart Group a Mailing List.
  5. Click Save Smart Group.

Info

You can also create a Smart Group based on a Participant search. However, the Smart Group save page will not offer you the option to make this group a Mailing List. To make this Smart Group available to CiviMail, you must change its settings through Contacts > Manage Groups. This same thing happens if you use the Advanced Search and choose Event Participants under "Display results as."

You cannot create smart groups based on Membership, Contributions or Pledge searches, or based on results of an Advanced Search if the "Display results as" option is set to anything but Contacts.

docs.title: Scheduled jobs and cron jobs
docs.text:
After people have signed up on your mailing list(s), you will want to be able to send them mass mailings. You will also want to automatically handle any bounced email messages. These topics are dealt with in detail in the Everyday tasks and Maintaining Healthy Email Lists parts of this book, respectively. Here in this section we are going to look at some backend and server options that enable the sending of mass mailings and the bounce handling to happen.

Go to Administer > System Settings > Scheduled Jobs and you will see all scheduled jobs that CiviCRM uses to do certain tasks on a regular basis. One such task is the actual sending of mass mailings, which is handled by the Send Scheduled Mailings scheduled job. Another task is the processing of bounced emails, for which the Fetch Bounces scheduled job is responsible. You will need to enable these two scheduled jobs (and any others that you want to be run on a regular basis). Without these two, CiviMail will not be sending any mailings and will not be processing the bounces.

Now, CiviCRM's scheduled jobs cannot self-trigger themselves. Something on your server has to trigger them. The most common option for this is to set up a cron job on your server. This cron job can trigger one or more (or all) of the scheduled jobs. For more detailed explanations and examples of how to do this, see the Managing Scheduled Jobs wiki page.

docs.title: What is CiviMail?
docs.text:
CiviMail handles mass email campaigns. It can reliably deliver a high volume of email and provide detailed reports on the results and effectiveness of those emails. It can complement other CiviCRM components: for example, you can email non-members to encourage them to become members, or people who have not yet registered for an event.

CiviMail, like all of CiviCRM's mail features, interacts with your mail server. Configuring the mail server and properly setting up CiviMail are system administrator tasks, and you may require professional assistance. You also need to check that your web hosting provider meets the configuration requirements and find out whether they limit how many emails you can send per day.

A misconfigured mail server is a liability. If you do not know what you are doing, you could end up on a spam black list, which is much harder to get off than to get on. For more information about configuring your mail server, see the Email system configuration chapter in the Initial set up section.

docs.title: Scenario: managing email lists
docs.text:
St Ethelburga's Centre for Peace and Reconciliation uses CiviEvent to run a yearly event programme on different themes. They have set up a mailing list page where people can sign up to hear about events that interest them. They use CiviMail to email people based on those interests. When someone unsubscribes from an event theme mailing list, CiviCRM keeps a record of it.

St Ethelburga's also automatically subscribes anyone who has attended an event on a specific theme to receive emails about that theme. CiviCRM remembers who has unsubscribed from a thematic event mailing list and does not re-subscribe them.

From time to time, St. Ethelburga's sends other emails to a mailing list that includes nearly all contacts in their database. These contain personal messages from the centre director highlighting particular issues. To test which message formats are more effective, they often send two similar versions of an email to different groups. They send the first version to half the contacts in a particular group, then send the second version while excluding contacts who received the first.

docs.title: Scenario: mobilising with email
docs.text:
The Townsville Organisation For Tenants (TOFT) held a survey and petition to gather data and support for the campaign Demand Affordable Public Housing. Volunteers conducted the survey by visiting selected constituents in their homes. The petition was widely promoted to the public, who could sign it and answer questions online.

Early in the campaign, the TOFT volunteer coordinator searched for contacts in the group Volunteers and used the Send Email action to ask for help with the survey. A small group of those who said they were available were trained to conduct home visits and record survey responses.

After the online petition was created using tools in CiviCampaign, the TOFT communications officer created an email with text, images and links to promote the campaign and encourage people to complete the petition online. They sent it to the entire database using CiviMail and included a forwarding link so recipients could distribute the email through their own networks.

CiviMail enabled TOFT to track responses to the mass email. Reports showed that 89% of recipients clicked through to sign the petition, and 75% forwarded the email to others. TOFT compared this data with previous offline petition and survey efforts to demonstrate the campaign's increased reach through using CiviCRM.

docs.title: Popular extensions
docs.text:
These are widely used extensions in the relevant category of the official CiviCRM Extensions Directory. Usage is a popularity signal, not a compatibility or suitability guarantee.

  • Mosaico CiviCRM Integration — reported usage: 4,729
  • E-mail API — reported usage: 3,072
  • Fuzion Tokens — reported usage: 1,489
  • PDF Creation API — reported usage: 438
  • Mosaico Tweaks — reported usage: 253

All extensions for this component

Check development status, current CiviCRM compatibility, CMS requirements, and release notes before installation.
