docs.title: What you need to know
docs.text: This page outlines key concepts and questions for planning your use of CiviCRM's email capabilities. Read it before you start sending emails to contacts. Detailed information on carrying out the activities mentioned here is in the Everyday Tasks section.

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text:
Email plays a central role in CiviCRM. Broadly speaking, email is sent from CiviCRM in three situations:

  • To individuals and small groups via the Send Email action.
  • To a large group as a mass mailing via CiviMail.
  • To individuals who trigger an email through a workflow in another component, such as an event registration confirmation email.

An advantage of sending email through CiviCRM, rather than through an email client or a bulk email tool other than CiviMail, is that every email sent via the Send Email action or CiviMail is treated as an activity and stored in each recipient's activity history. For example, you can see that John Doe made a donation three days after receiving your April newsletter, or that your volunteer coordinator emailed Jane Smith to ask her to staff the information table at an upcoming event.

docs.title: Send Email versus CiviMail
docs.text:
CiviCRM offers two options for sending email to contacts:

  • Send Email sends an email as an activity for a contact. It is suitable for individuals and small groups.
  • CiviMail sends a mailing to a group. It is suited to mass mailings or scheduled emails to small groups.

To send mass emails, first set up CiviMail. The Send Email action is available even when the CiviMail component is disabled.

The options have important differences:

  • Emails sent via the Send Email action are limited to a maximum of 50 email addresses. There is no reporting other than an activity record for each recipient.
  • CiviMail emails have bounce processing and reporting.
  • CiviMail allows recipients to manage their own subscriptions.
  • CiviMail can be configured to automatically track replies.

CiviMail requires more work to configure and involves more steps, but enabling and configuring it provides additional mass email capabilities. Which method to use for a particular email might not be immediately apparent. Over time, you can establish and share practices among your users.

docs.title: When to use the Send Email action
docs.text:
As long as you are contacting fewer than 50 recipients and do not need to track whether they opened the email or clicked any links, the Send Email action is quicker and easier than sending a mass mailing in CiviMail.

The Send Email activity offers the functionality of sending through an email client: you can attach files, CC and BCC contacts, and use message templates.

CiviCRM records only the messages you send. Recipients' replies come to your email address and are not recorded in the database. For this reason, do not rely on the Send Email action for extended email exchanges. To record an email exchange, you could create an activity called Email Exchange and copy and paste the conversation into its body, as you would for a record of a telephone call.

You can also record emails sent through your email client using the autofiling outbound email option described below.

docs.title: When to use CiviMail
docs.text:
If you want to send mail to 50 or more contacts at once, you must use CiviMail.

Use CiviMail when you want statistics about the success of a mailing, including bounce statistics and click-throughs. For more information, see the Reports and analysis chapter.

CiviMail also enables people to sign up for your mailing lists on your website and automatically tracks their unsubscription or opt-out requests. It can file emails that recipients send as replies to a mailing and send an autoresponse to those replies.

docs.title: Choosing recipients
docs.text:
Send Email lets you choose recipients from a contact record or from search results.

CiviMail lets you choose recipients from search results or from Groups marked as Mailing Lists, which must be created before you set up the mailing. There is a complication with search results: all mail sent from CiviMail must have an unsubscribe link. If recipients are in a Group, an unsubscribe request removes them from that Group's mailing list. If they are not in a Group, they must be added to one when they unsubscribe so CiviCRM can record the request.

docs.title: Personalisation with tokens
docs.text: Emails sent with both Send Email and CiviMail can include personalised text, such as a person's name. This uses tokens: placeholders that CiviCRM replaces with an appropriate value when sending each message. Some tokens available in CiviMail are not available in the Send Email activity.

docs.title: From email addresses
docs.text: Both mass and regular email can be sent from your personal address, a general email address associated with your organisation, or another person's address. For example, an assistant can send official email messages under the name of his manager.

docs.title: Headers and footers
docs.text: In mass mailings only, you can include customised headers and footers. Configure them under Administer > CiviMail > Headers, Footers, and Automated Messages.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: Templates for entire emails or parts of emails, such as headers and footers, let you reuse content. You can create email templates beforehand or when you send an email, and edit them at any time.

docs.title: Reporting
docs.text: CiviMail can track mass mailings, helping you understand recipients' interests and gauge the effectiveness of your communications. You can track how many recipients opened an email and which links were popular.

docs.title: Mailing list sign-up and unsubscribing
docs.text: CiviCRM lets you publish a sign-up page or form, called a profile, where people can join your mailing list on your website. It requires that you allow recipients to unsubscribe from any mailing list and opt out of ever getting email from you. CiviCRM automatically tracks these requests. For more information, see the Set-Up chapter.

docs.title: Autofiling external emails in CiviCRM
docs.text: CiviCRM lets you automatically record email sent through your email client in contact records. Set up a special email address and include it in the BCC field of an email you send. The database reads the email and converts it into an activity, filed in the record of the contact whose email address matches. If that email address does not exist in your database, a new contact record is created. See the Email System Configuration chapter of the Intial set up section for details.

docs.title: Key questions
docs.text:
When planning your use of CiviCRM's email capabilities, consider:

  • Are there types of emails you send repeatedly and want to create templates for?
  • Is there content you want in the header or footer of every mailing?
  • Do you want a web page where people can sign up for your emails?
  • Which emails are important to store in recipients' contact records?

When planning a specific email, consider:

  • How many people are you sending it to?
  • Do you want to know who opens it and clicks its links?
  • Have you created a list—a Group or Smart Group—to send it to?
  • Do you want recipients to be able to view the mailing in a browser window if they have trouble viewing it from their email browser?
  • Who should be the sender: a generic organisation address or an address personalised with someone's name?

docs.title: Interaction with other tools
docs.text: Many CiviCRM components interact with email functionality and CiviMail, for example, to send confirmation, thank-you, and receipt emails. The sections of this book about each component include information about customising these emails. Read them alongside this section to understand email in the broader context of CiviCRM.

docs.title: Privacy issues
docs.text: Consider privacy issues when planning email. Different countries have different laws relating to email privacy, including opt out/unsubscribe options. CiviMail's tracking tools may also raise issues; for instance, you may wish to avoid tracking who has clicked on the "how to deal with drug issues" link in a specific mailing.

docs.title: Spam and email deliverability
docs.text: When you send mass emails, there is a risk they will be marked as spam. This affects delivery of both the current email and future emails sent from your server. Managing these issues is complex and outside the scope of this book. If your organisation does not have a system administrator, consultant, or email hosting service knowledgeable about them, you may want to seek expert advice.

docs.title: Email and template design/layout
docs.text:
The success of an email depends partly on its design and layout, as well as its content. A well-designed email is clean, organised, and adapts to the ways people read email, including on smart phones, tablets, laptops, desktops, browsers, and applications. Consider these design practices:

  • Create well-designed base templates and encourage or enforce their use. These might range from a single-column table layout with a header image and text footer to a series of progressively more structured layouts. A consistent look and feel matters for organisation and communication branding.
  • Responsive email design can be very challenging — in ways much more challenging than response web design — because email is read in many environments and applications. Email applications also lack a universally accepted set of standards for rendering designs, making consistent layouts across devices difficult. Consider acquiring a responsive base template rather than building one from scratch. Free email templates are available that have been well tested on commonly used devices and applications.
  • Keep layouts relatively simple. More complex structures are more likely to have problems on different devices. If you develop complex layouts, test them thoroughly or use an email testing service.
  • Use tables for layouts. Unlike on websites, where div tags are more appropriate for layout, tables are more universally and consistently rendered in email clients.
  • Use inline CSS. Many commonly used email clients do not support externally referenced CSS styles or styles defined in style blocks. To ensure styles are recognised, insert them inline with the element tags.
  • Research rendering differences. Tags or CSS styles may render differently between email applications, so you may need to find out why a style is ignored in a particular context.
  • Consider design and content together. Focusing on one while neglecting the other may compromise your message.

docs.title: Complex event fees
docs.text: The regular fees layout form outlined in the Creating an event chapter of this section lets a registrant select one fee option from a list. If that single-option format does not meet your event registration needs, you can use price sets and discounts to compose more complex pricing options.

docs.title: Price sets
docs.text:
Price Sets let you break event fees into smaller pieces and set a fee for each piece. For example, you can offer an optional post-conference dinner or a book at extra cost.

This example shows a price set for a Conference with optional pre-conference training sessions, meals and lodging:

docs.title: Create a new price set
docs.text:
1. Navigate to CiviEvent > New Price Sets.
  2. In the Price Set form, enter the name of your price set and check Used For > Event.
  3. Select the financial type to be used (in this case it will be Event Fee).
  4. You can add pre or post form help (help text for the user).
  5. Check the Is this price set active box.
  6. Press Save. A form appears for you to create the first field in your price set.

docs.title: Create a new price field
docs.text:
Begin by entering a name for the event item in the Field Label**.**

The Input Field Type has a structure similar to custom data fields, with some unique qualities and usage relevant to fee structures:

  • Text/Numeric Quantity: Lets you set a unit price. The registrant enters a quantity in a text box, and that quantity is multiplied by the unit value to calculate the fee.
  • Select: Displays a dropdown box from which the registrant selects one option.
  • Radio: Displays multiple options in a list, allowing the registrant to select one fee choice.
  • Checkbox: Displays fields in a list from which the registrant can select or unselect any number of options.

You can combine these field types to create virtually any fee structure.

Enter a number in the Participant Count field if you want to increment the number of registered participants per unit against the maximum number of participants allowed for the event. For example, if the price field is for a table at a fundraiser that seats eight people, set Participant Count to 8.

For Text/Numeric Quantity fields, enter an amount in the Price field. For Select, Radio and Checkbox types, enter a price for each option in the table of options shown in the screenshot above.

To display the price next to the event item, check the Display Amount? box.

As when creating other custom data, you can enter a description for the Field Help, decide whether the event item is required, select whether it is visible to the public or only to the administrator in the Visibility field, and indicate whether it is Active. These fields are described in the Custom fields chapter in Organising your data.

You can also choose the dates when the price field is active. For example, you can have price fields offering discounted rates for people who register very early, standard rates for people who register up to two weeks before the event, and premium rates for people who register in the last two weeks before the event.

Press Save to finish configuring the event item, or Save and New to create another price field for the price set.

docs.title: Add the price set to an event
docs.text:
Once you finish configuring the price set, add it to your event on the Fees tab. Select its name in the Price Set field, as shown below.

As with custom data fields, it is helpful to plan the structure of your registration fees and build the price set before creating the event. If you begin creating the event and then determine that you need a price set, you can complete the process, create the price set, and return to the event configuration page to assign it.

Price sets can be reused in multiple events. This is particularly helpful for organizations that run multiple events in a series, such as a regional training seminar program.

docs.title: Manage price sets
docs.text:
To manage existing CiviEvent price sets:

  • Navigate to Manage Price Sets and choose the Events link; or
  • Navigate to CiviEvent > Manage Price Sets and choose Administer.

docs.title: Discounts
docs.text:
CiviEvent also lets you offer early bird discounts determined by sign-up date if you use a simple fee structure. These discounts override regular event fees during the period you specify.

To set up an early bird discount, check the Discounts by sign up date box underneath your regular fees in the fees section of your event configuration. Create the discount set and add it to the fee table. A new fee table appears toward the bottom of the page, duplicating the original fee table shown in the screenshot below. Edit the labels and fees to correspond to the discounts offered for each original fee option.

You can create multiple date-based discount sets for an event. This may be useful if you have a series of early bird dates that progressively increase the cost of registration as the event gets closer.

Discount sets and discounts via price sets are out-of-the-box CiviCRM that allow you to do offer discounts based on sign up dates. For more sophisticated discounts, you can install the CiviDiscount extension. It allows a variety of discounts, including Discount codes and discounts based on membership status.

docs.title: Creating an event
docs.text:
This page covers how to create a new event and the options available during setup. If you're going to allow online registration, also read online event registration. If not, read manual event registration.

To get started, choose Events > New Event from the menu. If you can't see the events menu, make sure that you have enabled the Events component in Administer > System Settings > Components.

docs.title: Event information and settings
docs.text:
The first page you see when creating an event requests basic information online about the event. Click a blue question mark for help with a field. Where a pencil appears, clicking it takes you to a screen where you can edit the available options. Depending on your permissions, you may not be able to edit these options and therefore will not see the pencil.

  • From template lets you create an event from a template rather than from scratch. See the Event templates chapter in this section.
  • Event type lets you categorise the event.
  • If CiviCampaign is enabled, you can select a campaign for the event. See the Campaign section for more details.
  • Roles distinguish participants such as attendees, speakers and staff. The value in this field is assigned by default when users register online or when you import registrations, unless you include the field Participant Role with other values in your CSV import file. The most common value is Attendee.
  • Participant Listings can show support for an event and help generate interest within your constituent community. Decide whether users should see a list of participants and how much information to reveal. The options here only enable participant listings — to display one, you must create a menu item or link to the listing on your website. After you create the event, the participant listing link appears on the event configuration page. See Event management for information on participant listings and other ways to promote your events.
  • Event Title appears on event information pages, registration pages, event listings, and the Manage Events administrative page. Choose a meaningful title for your event.
  • Event Summary and Complete Description both appear on event information pages. Use the rich-text editor for the description field to include photo, images, and formatted text.
  • Start date/time and End date/time appear on the event information page and event listings.
  • Maximum number of participants lets you set a limit and define a message to display when it is reached.
  • To display a map of the event location, use either Google Maps or Open Street Maps. Configure your mapping solution through Administer > System Settings > Mapping and Geocoding.
  • Select Public Event to include the event in promotional listings such as RSS feeds, iCal files or feeds, and event listing pages.
  • Select Allow sharing through social media to include links for sharing the event on the Event Info page, Thank-you page, Tell-a-Friend page (if enabled), and in event confirmation emails.
  • An event can be active or inactive. If configuration will take some time, consider leaving it inactive until it is complete so it is not inadvertently listed on event listing feeds. You can activate it when you are ready to publicize it.
  • Select Show Calendar Links if you want CiviCRM to add links for downloading a calendar meeting invitation on the information page and in registration mails. These invites do not work well if participants are in different timezones than the server. Test thoroughly if you enable this.

After reviewing the details, click Continue >> to create the event and advance to the next step. On any subsequent page, you can interrupt configuration by clicking Save and Done, then return later to review and modify the settings.

To return to a saved event, go to Events > Manage Events and click Configure.

docs.title: Event location
docs.text:
Next, complete the event's location and contact details.

After entering a location, you can reuse it for subsequent events by clicking Use existing location and selecting it from the dropdown list. If you choose an existing location and edit it, the change updates that location for all events that use it.

You can list phone numbers and email addresses on the event information page so registrants can contact event organizers directly. If the event is off-site from your organization's primary location, you may also want to provide contact information for the meeting location.

You can also select whether or not the event location is showed on the registration and event information screens.

docs.title: Fees
docs.text:
If the event is free, set Paid Event to No, click Save, and skip to Online Registration. If the event is paid, click Yes to show the available options.

Contribution Type (financial type) determines what is assigned to paid registrations for the event. The most common value is Event Fee, but you can define multiple Financial Types and assign them to different events. See Set-Up in the Contributions section for details.

If you plan to accept credit card payments through the online registration form, configure a payment processor before creating the event. See Payment Processors in the Contributions section for more information.

To let registrants pay later by mailing a check, paying on-site with cash or credit card, or arranging another payment method, enable the Pay Later option and define a label and payment instructions. If you leave it unchecked, registrants must pay by credit card.

Regular Fees provide price levels from which a registrant must select one, such as an individual registration for $50 or a family registration for $100. Each fee amount has a label, and you can set a default fee. This approach works well for many events and is easy to set up. Here is an example:

For a more complex pricing structure, with more options or additional add-ons, you may wish to use price sets or discounts. See the Complex event fees chapter in this section.

docs.title: Online registration
docs.text:
Online registration lets people register themselves through your web site. It can be convenient for constituents and save staff time and resources.

If you do not need online registration, do not check Allow Online Registration; move to the next step. If you do want it, see Online event registration.

docs.title: Scheduled reminders
docs.text:
Scheduled reminders can automatically email event registrants at certain times before or after an event. For example:

  • A week before the event, remind them to check the conference schedule.
  • A day after the event, ask them to fill in the feedback form.
  • Two days before payment is due for a Pending from Pay Later registration, warn them that their registration will be cancelled if they do not provide payment details in the next 48 hours.

To set up a reminder for a specific event, click the scheduled reminders tab. It shows existing reminders for that event, if any. Click Add Reminder.

Fill in the form to send a message—for example, an email to all registered speakers 3 days before the event start date. You can limit recipients by status (registered, attended, etc.) and by role (speaker, attendee, volunteer, etc.). You can use a template or compose a message in the HTML format box.

You can also set up reminders for specific event types and add them to specific event templates. The approach is the same, but you access it through Administer > Communications > Scheduled reminders.

docs.title: Tell-A-Friend
docs.text:
The final event-creation page lets you enable "Tell-A-Friend" so constituents can share details about your organization and event with friends and colleagues. You can define the text and links included on that page and in the email sent from the tool.

Each time a participant sends mail to friends, a "Tell a friend" activity record is added to the participant's Activities tab. This lets you track your most active supporters and engage them further. People emailed through this feature are also automatically added to CiviCRM as contacts.

docs.title: Registration confirmation and receipting
docs.text:
You can send automated confirmation and receipt emails to participants who register online or are registered by staff or volunteers. Message templates control the content and layout of these emails. Both HTML and Text formats are provided. You can modify or add text, or add branding such as a logo to the HTML versions. To set up a from email address for confirmations and receipts, see Set-Up in the Email section.

Go to Administer > Communications > Message Templates and click the System Workflow Message tab to see the messages you can modify. Click Edit next to the "Events - Registration Confirmation and Receipt" rows to edit their content and layout.

These templates include both the text shown and necessary program logic. Take care not to modify the program logic. After making changes, test the workflow and review the emails sent. If changes cause problems, errors or missing information, you can revert to the system default for that workflow.

docs.title: Custom data for events
docs.text: You may want to collect extra information about events and their participants as part of the event management process. A general understanding of how custom data works in CiviCRM will help you use this page. The chapter on Custom fields in Organising Your Data provides that background.

docs.title: Choose where to store custom data
docs.text:
The key question is where the custom data should go. There are three typical places:

  • The participant record
  • The contact record
  • The event record

Putting data in the wrong place can cause problems later. For example:

  • Add dietary preference to the contact's record, since it is unlikely to change between events.
  • Add session preference to the participant record, since it is only of interest in the context of the event.

The event record should collect information about the event itself, not its participants.

docs.title: Custom data for events
docs.text:
Custom fields can be added to events. For example, an organisation that holds training workshops throughout the year could create a checkbox style field to track six common workshop topics. It could add the list of topic options as custom data for events of the type workshop. The field would then be available when creating an event of type Workshop.

You do not have to select a specific event type. Leaving the dropdown set to Any makes the field available to all events, regardless of type.

docs.title: Custom data for participants
docs.text:
There are several options for adding custom data to participants:

  • Participants: Adds the field to all participant records. Use this for information that applies to all participants.
  • Participants (Event Name): Works like Participants, but lets you assign a group of custom fields to a specific event. This is useful for complex registration data for one event without cluttering up all events.
  • Participants (Role): Makes fields available only for particular types of participants. For example, you could collect biographical profile details from speakers and record them with their event registration.

docs.title: Add custom data
docs.text:
Adding custom data requires the administrator permission. To add custom data for participants, add new custom fields through Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Custom Data. To create custom fields for events, first add the custom field set on the appropriate record, and then add the fields themselves.

Alternatively, you can create custom fields on the fly during the event creation process—see the chapter Creating an event.

docs.title: Event planning and management
docs.text: The decisions you make when planning an event affect how you set it up. Consider the questions in this chapter before you start.

docs.title: Planning your event
docs.text:
If you are new to CiviEvent, think about the structure of your events and how you want someone to experience registration. These questions can help you decide how to set up and configure an event:

  • What different types of events does your organization hold, and what type of event is this?
  • What different roles will participants have at the event?
  • What information do you want to collect about participants, such as food and lodging preferences?
  • Will you allow online registrations?
  • Is there a limit on the number of participants who can attend?
  • Do you want to approve registrations, or leave registration open to anyone?
  • Will there be a waitlist if the maximum number of registrations is exceeded?
  • Should one person be able to register multiple people?
  • Do you want to give registrants confirmation of registering?
  • Do you want to make the participant listing public?
  • Is this an event that repeats regularly with roughly the same details?
  • Will this be a paid event? If so:
    • What Financial Type will you consider the event fees to be?
    • What kind of fee structure will you need?
    • Will you charge multiple fees, such as fees for additional sessions or meals?
    • Will you offer discounts or early registration?

Assess what information you need to run your events effectively and what would be useful to collect during events and from participants. If you run similar recurring events, consider using event templates or the event copy features to make setup easier.

docs.title: Promoting your events
docs.text:
Think about whom you want to attend and where they get their information. This can help you decide how to promote the event:

  • What strategy and channels will you use to promote your event?
  • Will you post the event on your website and allow people to register online?
  • Is email a good way to reach your constituents to market the event?
  • Is the event “by invitation only”? Whom will you invite?
  • Have you planned a schedule from the initial announcement or invitation through event reminders?

Listing your event prominently on your organization’s website and public calendar is one way to promote it. You can also let people and organizations know about it and encourage participants to help promote it. See the Integrating events with your website sub-section of the Online event registration chapter in this section.

If you publicise your event on another website or organization’s calendar, make it clear how people should register. For example, some social networks have a built-in event registration system, such as Facebook events. Other organizations helping to publicise your event may have their own registration systems. Wherever you publicise the event, make the expected registration process clear.

docs.title: Following up after the event
docs.text:
Update each participant’s status during or soon after the event so that you have accurate information to evaluate it.

Consider emailing attendees after the event to thank them and provide links to any documentation you have online. You may want to send a different email to people who registered but did not attend. You might also use this opportunity to promote a new event, suggest that attendees join your organisation as members, or solicit donations for a specific campaign. To learn more, see Scheduled Reminders in the Email section.

docs.title: Event templates
docs.text:
If you need to set up a number of events with similar configurations, you can streamline the process using event templates. Creating a template is similar to creating an event, with two differences:

  • Assign a descriptive template title that identifies the type of event it is used for, such as Monthly community meetup with online registration.
  • The template form has no starting or ending dates. Those dates are specific to an actual event instance.

docs.title: Create an event template
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Events > Event Templates and click Add Event Template.
  2. Enter a template title and event type.
  3. Select a campaign if all events created from the template should be associated with a Campaign.
  4. Continue the normal event set-up process, using settings that will be constant across events created from the template. Common characteristics might include location, event fees, online registration settings, and tell-a-friend settings.

docs.title: Use an event template
docs.text: When you start to create a new event, select the template. The new event will be pre-filled with the saved configuration properties.

docs.title: Integrating events with your website
docs.text: You can promote events on your website or on other organisations' websites by linking to event pages, displaying event information, or sharing an RSS feed.

docs.title: Link to an event page
docs.text:
Navigate to Events > Manage Events and click Event Links. The menu includes links to the event info page and the event registration page. The registration page is also linked from the info page.

Copy the URL for the event page. You can link to this page from anywhere on your website.

docs.title: Add an event link in Joomla!
docs.text:
1. Go into the Joomla! control panel.
  2. Choose Menu Manager > Your menu name.
  3. Click New.
  4. Expand CiviCRM > CiviCRM Events and click the Event Info item.
  5. Choose the event from the Select an Event list on the right side of the page.
  6. Click Save.

docs.title: Display an event registration form in WordPress
docs.text: You can use the CiviCRM icon 'shortcode' to insert the event registration form into a Page or Post.

docs.title: Display upcoming events in Drupal
docs.text: The views module offers options for displaying lists of content, including an automatically updating list of upcoming events. See Integrating with Drupal in the Website integration chapter for more details.

docs.title: RSS feed for all upcoming events
docs.text:
Visitors can subscribe to all your events in the RSS feed reader of their choice. Many website management systems can also subscribe to an RSS feed and present its information within their layout.

  1. Navigate to Events > Manage Events.
  2. Click the orange and white square icon at the top right of the page.
  3. Copy the URL to share or embed into your website.

docs.title: Finding and administering event participants
docs.text: These tasks apply to existing event participants. For how to add participants, see the Manual event registration chapter.

docs.title: View participants for an upcoming event
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Events > Dashboard.
  2. Click the Counted: link to see all the contacts for an event.

If any count is zero, the associated text will not be a hyperlink. Some participant roles may not count for the event total, such as someone who is on clean-up duty.

docs.title: Find participants using search criteria
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Events > Find Participants.
  2. In the event name field, start typing to see a list of events. Click the event you want. Set additional search choices for the fields you want to see.
  3. Click Search.

When the search returns results, you can select all participants in the results or a subset and perform an action on them. Available Actions include:

  • Cancel registration for the selected participants.
  • Delete participants from event: Deleting participants does not delete the contact record; it deletes all transactions and activities associated with the participant for this event. This action cannot be undone.
  • Email - send now generates an email to your search result list. For example, you may want to send details about parking options or changes to the programme before the event.
  • Export participants: Export a predefined set of fields (export mapping), or create an export mapping that can be saved for reuse. The software exports to CSV format, which can be opened in standard spreadsheet software or used directly for mail merges.
  • Group - add contacts to an existing group or one you create during this action.
  • Group - create smart group: Smart groups are saved search results based on defined criteria, similar to a query. The system reruns the query using those criteria each time you open the smart group. This is helpful for complex searches you need to view regularly.
  • Name badges - print: Select the type of badge you require. A printable PDF is generated with the names of the selected participants (see Event Badges in this chapter).
  • PDF letter - print for participants
  • Participant status - change (emails sent) When using this feature, emails are sent to participants when their status changes from one in the pending class (eg Pending (pay later), Pending from approval) to Registered or Attended (positive class). Emails are also sent if the status changes to Expired or Cancelled.
  • Print selected rows prints what is shown on the screen for the rows you selected.
  • Update multiple participants: Edit multiple fields for multiple participants in a table grid layout. You must create the profile set you want to use before taking this action. If you are not familiar with Profiles, see the Profiles chapter in the Organising your Data section.

docs.title: List a participant's individual fees
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Search > Custom Searches.
  2. Click Event Aggregate.
  3. Choose your search criteria, and click Search.

docs.title: Change registration selections for an existing participant
docs.text:
An existing registration might need to change in any of these situations:

  • A volunteer registered online with a pay later option for the event fees. Back-office staff want to change the person's role from attendee to volunteer and select a zero fee option from an admin-only price field.
  • A conference participant no longer wants to attend the conference dinner and requests a refund of the dinner fee.
  • A participant decides after registering online that they want to attend the pre-conference workshop. They contact the registration office with the request and provide credit card details for the extra charge.
  • A child registered for a holiday program decides she wants to do archery rather than pottery one afternoon. Although the fees do not change, back-office staff need to update her registration so they know where she should be for that session.

Back-office staff can make these changes by editing the participant's event registration:

  1. Navigate to the participant's event registration. One way to do this is via Events > Find Participants.

  2. Select View or Edit towards the right of the event record.

  3. Click Change Selections.

  4. Make the required adjustments. The event fee will be adjusted appropriately, and the event status will be set to partially paid, registered or pending refund based on the difference between the new event fee and the contribution(s) already processed.

Additional payments (credit card or offline methods) or a refund (offline methods only) need to be entered via the record payment link associated with the event registration record, as described in the section on partial payments.

docs.title: Creating and printing event badges
docs.text:
You can create custom name badges for your event.

Navigate to Administer > CiviEvent > Event Badge Layout > New Badge Layout to see the set-up screen.

Consider these layout options:

Label format: Four options are available:

  • Avery 5395 - 2-1/3" x 3-3/8"
  • A6 Badge Portrait 150x106
  • Fattorini Name Badge 100x65
  • Hanging Badge 3-3/4''x4-3/4''

Image (top left) and/or Image (top right): Select an existing image or upload a new one. Images can be positioned on the right and left to include your logo and that of a major sponsor.

Elements - Rows: Most standard or custom contact, event and participant fields can be selected to provide up to 6 rows on the labels. You can also select spacer to improve the layout. Typical fields include display name, current employer, country and/or participant role. If you have set up the appropriate custom fields, you could also include the sessions a participant registered for and their selected meal option.

Barcode?: A linear barcode or QR code can be added at the bottom of the badge.

Enabled?: This needs to be ticked for people to use the badge layout. For a special layout used only at an annual conference, you could untick this box for most of the year to prevent accidental usage.

Reserved?: Select this option to ensure that admin users do not accidentally delete the badge layout.

Note

You will not be able to preview the badge layout unless at least one event has been created and at least one participant has been registered.

docs.title: Printing name badges
docs.text:
Once your list of event participants is finalised, print the name badges as follows:

  1. Go to Events > Find Participants.
  2. Select the relevant participants.
  3. Choose Print Event Name Badges from the drop-down list of actions and Click Go.
  4. Select the name badge layout for this event.
  5. Click Make Name Badges.

A PDF file will be created that you can print on the appropriate-sized labels.

docs.title: Keeping track of events and participants
docs.text: After creating your event and providing the registration form to web site visitors, you can manage participants through the CiviEvent administrative tools. The tasks vary depending on the type of event you are organising. This page describes how to view events and participants and find event management tools.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
The CiviEvent Dashboard (Events > Dashboard) brings events and participant information together in one place. Its Event Summary table shows up to ten scheduled and recent Events. Click the Event name to view the event as it will be displayed to site visitors. Click the Participants count to see a list of participants.

To run your own customized searches, click Find more event participants at the end of the page. You can search by Participant Name, Event, Date Range and Status.

From the Dashboard, you can also:

  • Click Manage Events to find and manage specific events.
  • Click New Event to create a new event page.
  • Use the icons for RSS feeds and calendars to use the data in external applications.

docs.title: Finding and viewing events
docs.text:
Another way to access your events is to navigate to Events > Manage Events. This screen lists all CiviEvents that have been created. Search filters at the top of the page let you search by event name, specific event type or date.

At the right hand side of the page, you have four links for each event:

  • Configure - access to amend the event settings, including Information and Settings, Location, Fees, Online Registration, Schedule Reminders and Tell a Friend
  • Participants - quick links to lists of participants who are registered or attending the event, or participants who are not attending
  • Event Links - quick links to Register Participant and the live event pages, including the event information page and the live online registration page

docs.title: Mass event registration
docs.text: You can register multiple contacts for an event at one time. For example, Arts in Action anticipates high attendance at a youth leadership workshop from participants at a previous workshop. Staff search for those participants and register them with Participant Status set to Pending. They can then call or email the pending contacts. If someone confirms they will attend, the event organizer can change their status from Pending to Registered.

docs.title: Register multiple contacts
docs.text:
1. Search for the contacts you want to register. In the Arts in Action example, staff would use Search > Find Participants to find participants at the previous workshop.
  2. On the search results page, choose All x records or put a check mark next to each contact you want to register.
  1. From the actions list above the search results, choose Register participants for event, then click Go.
  2. Choose the event. You cannot currently register participants en masse for past events.
  3. Complete the registration form, choosing the action choices for this set of people, such as Participant Status set to Pending. Your choices apply to all contacts in the set.
  4. Click Save.

docs.title: Limitations of mass registrations
docs.text:
The action choices you make (in Step 3) are applied uniformly to the entire set of selected contacts. To use different choices, perform mass registration several times with different sets of contacts. For example, you might give contacts you plan to call and invite a Participant Status of Pending, then register event leaders you know will attend with a Participant Status of Registered.

You cannot do mass registration of participants for events in the past.

You cannot apply contribution information, such as a pay later contribution or credit card transaction, in a batch action. Mass registration is therefore best for free events or contacts who are not required to pay a fee at this point. You can add payment details for individual contacts later.

docs.title: Import event registrations
docs.text: Importing registration information adds multiple registrations to an event from a comma-separated values (CSV) file. If most contacts are already in CiviCRM, mass registration may be faster.

docs.title: Match participants to contacts
docs.text:
The participant import tool is similar to the contact import tool, but the Individuals must already exist in the database as contacts. If they do not, run a contact import first, preferably including a unique external identifier, most often an ID assigned by the database or application from which you are importing records.

There are two ways to match a participant to a contact:

  • Include the contact's external ID in a column of the CSV file. If you have the IDs on record but did not import them with the contacts, you can run a second contact import to update this field before importing participants.
  • Match participants using your contact de-dupe rules, for example by including each individual's first name, last name and email address in the file. If a contact matches these three fields, the event participation is assigned to that contact.

docs.title: Prepare your data
docs.text:
Include the required fields in your CSV file. You need only one of the fields marked (Match to Contact), not all of them:

  • Contact ID (Match to Contact)
  • Email (Match to Contact)
  • Event ID
  • External Identifier (Match to Contact)
  • Participant Status

docs.title: Import registrations
docs.text:
1. From the navigation menu, go to Events > Import Participants.
  2. Browse to the data file on your local computer.
  3. Select the appropriate contact type, date format and other options, and click Continue.
  4. Match the fields of your CSV file to the CiviCRM fields.
  5. If you may repeat this import in the future, check the Save this field mapping box.
  6. Preview and Save.

docs.title: Manual event registration
docs.text: Office staff can register contacts through the admin interface, including people who register by phone or mail.

docs.title: Register a participant manually
docs.text:
For example, when someone calls the office to register:

  1. Enter the person's name in the Quick search box.
  2. Select the contact from the results.
  3. Click the Events tab on the caller's contact record.
  4. Add the person to the event.

The Events tab lists the contact's current and past event bookings and provides links to register the contact for a new event.

There are two registration options:

  • Add Event Registration: For people who pay later, such as by sending a check or paying when they arrive at the event.
  • Submit Credit Card Event Registration: For people paying immediately by credit card. This option is available only if a payment processor is configured that allows direct payments through your web site. If you are taking a registration over the phone, you can ask for the person's credit card information and enter it manually.

The forms are similar except for the fields that record payment details.

Sections of the form change to reflect your choices. For example, selecting an event and participant role automatically loads predefined custom data fields that pertain to those selections.

docs.title: Registration and payment records
docs.text:
For a paid event, the form shows the event fees section defined in the event configuration details and an option to record financial transaction details (Record Payment).

An event registration records a contact's participation in an event. A corresponding financial transaction records the monetary value associated with that participation. The records are independent but can be linked. For example, you can register a V.I.P., speaker, or someone participating in a limited way without creating an associated financial transaction if their fee is waived. CiviCRM records the registration under the Events tab and the financial record under the Contributions tab, then links the two records.

If the event is a paid event, click the Record Payment checkbox and enter information in the Payment Information section. This links the event registration and contribution record for the contact. After recording the registration, you can view the related contribution record at the bottom of the event registration record. If you do not select the Record Payment check box, only a registration record is created.

docs.title: Register a participant paying only a deposit (partial payment)
docs.text:
For a manual registration, you can enter a payment amount less than the event fees and make one or more additional payments later.

During registration, enter the amount being paid now in the Amount field in the Payment Information section and set Participant Status to Partially paid.

A Partially paid registration is included in the participant total in the same way as a Pending from pay later registration. Additional payments are expected until the full event fee is paid.

To make an additional payment:

  1. Go to the registrant's contact record.
  2. Click the Events tab.
  3. Click more on the far right of the partially paid event record.
  4. Select Record Payment or Submit Credit Card payment.

You can make more than one additional payment. When the event fee has been paid in full, Participant status automatically changes to Registered, unless you choose a different status when making the last payment. The linked contribution's status automatically changes to Completed.

From an accounting perspective, the event fee is added to accounts receivable when the registration is created. Each partial payment is added as a separate line item until the fee is paid in full.

The event registration and linked contribution always display the full event fee. To see how much is owed, choose to View the event registration. Select ›› view payments under Total Paid to see a summary of each payment.

Alternatively, click the arrow next to the Contribution record at the bottom to see the payments.

docs.title: Online event registration
docs.text:
Online registration lets constituents register for events at a convenient time and place while reducing administration for your organization. The standard registration flow is:

  1. Event information
  2. Event registration
  3. Confirmation
  4. Thank you

The event information lists the event date, location, map link, contact information, and description. It also includes a link to the registration page.

During event registration, the registrant completes the form, including event fees, profile fields, and credit card or pay later fields.

The confirmation details the event fee options and data fields completed by the registrant. It proceeds to the credit card transaction.

The thank you message informs the registrant that they will receive a receipt by email.

docs.title: Setting up online registration
docs.text:
To offer online registration, check Allow Online Registration in the Online Registration step of event creation. Use the options on that form to configure registration.

Users will overwrite their own contact record if they attempt to register someone else while logged in

When a logged-in user opens the registration form, CiviCRM pre-fills it with their own contact details. If the user is registering someone else and they overwrite the pre-filled fields with the other person's details instead of their own, CiviCRM saves those details onto the logged-in user's own contact, not a new one. On sites where the CMS user account is kept in sync with the contact record, this can also overwrite the logged-in user's CMS account email.

If you expect logged in users to be registering other people then provide them with a link ending in cid=0:

https://example.org/civicrm/event/register?reset=1&id=123&cid=0

Whenever cid=0 is present in the URL, CiviCRM skips the pre-fill entirely and shows a blank "you are completing this form on behalf of someone else" form from the start. It does not save the contact to the logged in user.

Define the text for the link from the event information page to the registration form, and set the starting and ending dates for registration. The link text appears on the event information page and is most commonly "Register Now" or similar.

The start and end dates define when web site visitors may register. The registration end date can differ from the event start date if you want to close registration early to prepare name tags or perform other administrative tasks.

Enabling Register multiple participants lets individuals register as many people as they choose and pay the fees in a single transaction. For example, an organisation may send multiple people to a conference, or an individual may register and pay for themselves and their partner. By default, this option requires a different name and email address for each person registered.

Checking Allow same email and multiple registrations? provides the same capabilities without requiring distinct email addresses for each registrant. In either case, CiviCRM uses a separate contact record for each individual registered: an existing record if the contact is already in the system, or a new record otherwise.

This setting also a contact to register multiple times for the same event. For example, if the person purchased a ticket to a concert, then wanted to purchase another ticket later on.

Information on the Duplicate matching rule is provided in the Contact matching and duplicate management sub-section of this chapter (below).

Pending participant expiration (hours) is the time for confirming or finishing registration by participants with any status classed as Pending. It works in conjunction with the scheduled job Update Participant Statuses (see Administer > System Setting > Scheduled jobs). If both are set, pending registration must be finalized within the set time. Otherwise, the registration will be cancelled and the would-be registrant notified by email.

This feature is useful with scheduled reminders for automatically managing Pending from pay later registrations if you have allowed that payment option on your online registration page. See the Email section for more details on scheduled reminders.

Allow self-service cancellation or transfer: When selected, event participants receive a "self-service" link in their confirmation email. By clicking it, they can opt to transfer and/or cancel their registration.

Cancellation or transfer time limit (hours): When set, self-service cancellations and transfers are disabled the selected number of hours before the event starts.

Next, define the text and fields that will appear on the online registration page.

The introductory text appears at the top of the page and the footer text at the bottom. Between them, some or all of the following appear in this order: profile, fee selection, credit card details, and additional profile(s).

docs.title: Collecting participant information with profiles
docs.text:
Alternative: use FormBuilder

FormBuilder provides a new way to build the booking form if the built in Profiles don't offer the flexibility you need.

To collect information during online registration, include one or more profiles in your event configuration. You can include one profile immediately after the introductory message and one or more profiles under any fees and payment details you need to collect. If you are not sure what a profile is or why you would use one, see the Profiles chapter of Organising you data.

By default, the "Your Registration Info" profile is selected as the 'top' profile when you create an online registration form. It has three fields: first name, last name, and email address. However, CiviCRM requires only either first name and last name or email address for each contact. You can modify 'Your Registration Info' or create a profile with fewer fields. If you choose not to collect email addresses, be sure to uncheck "Send confirmation email?" at the bottom.

Warning

If you modify an existing profile whilst configuring your Online Registration page, the changes apply everywhere that profile is used. Unless an existing profile exactly matches your requirements, copy it, then rename and edit the copy as required.

If the profile you need does not exist, you can create it without leaving the Online Registration configuration page. The drag-and-drop profile interface also lets you create custom fields for the profile. Custom fields can be created for all events or participants, or only specific Event Types or Participant Roles. See Custom data on events for more details on where to store custom data.

Each profile appears on the registration form as a fieldset with a legend header. The legend is the profile Public Title if set; otherwise, it is the Profile Name. Give profiles names that help you identify them in a list and public titles that work as form-section headers.

For example, you could copy the Your Registration Info profile to add fields for workshops, name the copy "Workshop Registration", and give it the Public Title "Your Registration Info". You could then identify it when setting up workshop registration forms while keeping the same form header as other registration forms.

Several Advanced Settings for profiles take effect when a profile is included in event online registration. You cannot edit these in the profile editing interface within online registration settings; you must use the main profile settings form:

  • Adding contacts to a group. Many registrants do not wish or expect to join a mailing list merely because they signed up for an event.
  • CMS User account registration options. A participant can be offered the option or required to log in or create a user account while registering.
  • Including ReCAPTCHA. A CAPTCHA can be added to make registration more difficult for bots and people.

Other advanced settings, such as what to do upon duplicate match, are ignored on contribution pages.

For more information, read Profiles.

docs.title: Registration confirmation
docs.text:
Once your registration page is configured, enter the text for the Confirmation page, Thank-you page, and emailed confirmations/receipts, if enabled.

For free events, the Confirmation step is skipped. For paid events, payment is processed between the Confirmation and Thank you pages.

For most events, you'll want to enable the Send Confirmation Email feature, shown below. For paid events, the confirmation email also acts as a receipt. Make sure the Confirm From Email address is a valid email account on your mail server.

The contents of the Text field are included in both TEXT and HTML versions of receipt emails, so HTML tags or formatting are not recommended here.

docs.title: Email alerts for event registrations
docs.text:
Add one or more staff email addresses to CC Confirmation To or BCC Confirmation To if you want real-time updates on registrations. Separate multiple addresses with commas.

Warning

Make sure that the email addresses entered into the CC Receipt To and BCC Receipt To fields are correct and do not bounce or return an error email. Any return emails received by CiviCRM will be interpreted as a bounce for the CiviCRM Contact that the receipt was sent too and not as a bounce for the CC/BCC email address. This can have the adverse impact that the CiviCRM Contact's email address is put On Hold and cause future emails to not be sent. For more details see this issue report.

docs.title: Optional event registration features
docs.text: The following features may be useful for your online event registration process.

docs.title: Waitlists
docs.text:
Your organization may have an attendance limit, such as 25 people for a training workshop or 200 for a fund-raising dinner. CiviEvent lets you set the maximum number of people who can register. When registrations reach that number, CiviEvent prevents further registrations and sends an automatic message: "The event is currently full." You can customize this message when creating an event and let people join a waitlist on a first-come-first-served basis.

The waiting list works as follows:

  • When space becomes available, for example after a cancellation, On waitlist participants move to 'Pending from waitlist' status. They receive an email with a link to complete registration, including payment of any event fees.
  • People remain pending for the time set in Pending participant expiration (hours). Set this in the Online registration tab under Pending participant expiration hours. You can set it to 0 for no limit.
  • After that period, they move to expired and other people on the waitlist have an opportunity to register.

To enable the Waitlist feature, first enable the participant statuses On waitlist and Pending from waitlist in Administer > CiviEvent > Participant statuses. Then check Offer Waitlist on the Info and settings tab and set the message displayed on the event information page when the event is full.

For status processing to happen, the Update Participant Statuses scheduled job must be running (see Administer > System Setting > Scheduled jobs).

docs.title: Participant approval
docs.text:
For events open only to specific people, you can review registrations and approve those invited. For example, an organization might invite volunteers who donated 100 or more volunteer hours to an appreciation dinner. Invitees might tell friends about the event or forward its information, so registrations may need review.

To enable 'Participant approval', first enable Awaiting approval, Pending from approval, and Rejected in Administer > CiviEvent > Participant Statuses. Then check Require participant approval? on the Online Registration tab and set the approval message. You can also limit how long approved participants have to complete registration by entering a time in hours in the Pending participant expiration field. For example, enter "72" to allow 3 days.

When someone registers, they receive this reply: "Your registration has been submitted. Once your registration has been reviewed, you will receive an email with a link to a web page where you can complete the registration process." You can customize the reply for your organisation.

Participants are placed in 'Awaiting Approval' status. To review and approve them, go to 'Find Participants' and select the 'Change Participant Status' task. Approved participants move to 'Pending from approval' status and receive an email with a link to complete registration, including payment of any event fees.

For status processing to happen, the Update Participant Statuses scheduled job must be running (see Administer > System Setting > Scheduled jobs).

docs.title: Personal campaign pages
docs.text:
If you enable Personal Campaign Pages (PCPs), completed event registrants can create and customize a page to:

  • Promote the event for which they registered.
  • Promote an online contribution page.

For more information, see Contributions > Personal Campaign Pages in this book. This is the last step in creating an event. Click Save and Done.

docs.title: Contact matching and duplicate management
docs.text:
Allowing people to interact with your database from outside it can create duplicate contacts. One way to address this is to require people to log in: remove the register for events permission from anonymous users and give it to logged-in users or a specific role. Depending on the event, that may reduce registrations. For a conference or AGM, for example, you may want as many people as possible to register.

If people do not have to log in, CiviCRM needs to determine whether a registrant matches an existing contact. For example, James Martin might already be in the database—or there might be two contacts named James Martin, one in London and one in Paris. Duplicate rules determine how contacts are matched.

For more general and detailed information, see the Deduping and merging chapter. This section covers matching and duplicate management in CiviEvent.

By default, CiviEvent uses the Unsupervised rule for matching. When configuring online registration, you can select a different duplicate matching rule for that event. The selected rule applies to the primary participant and any additional participants.

The Online Registration tab checks whether the included profiles have enough fields to match participants to existing contacts. It reviews the possible combinations of matching fields that satisfy the event's rule and checks whether any combination appears in the included profiles. "Duplicate Matching Impossible" appears if the rule cannot match duplicate contacts using those fields. "Duplicate Contacts Possible" appears if enough fields are present but not all are required.

docs.title: Registration permissions
docs.text:
If online event registration is enabled, review Drupal user permissions to ensure visitors can view event information and complete registration forms. Navigate to Administer > Users > Permissions.

Most organizations let anonymous users—those who have not logged in—view and register for events. To do so, assign these CiviCRM module permissions to the anonymous user role:

  • access all custom data — required if you collect information from registrants in custom fields
  • profile create — required if your online registration forms include profiles
  • register for events
  • view event info
  • view event participants — required if you want to display a listing of registered participants

To exclude anonymous visitors from viewing or registering online for events, assign these permissions to an authenticated user role.

CiviCRM also has an Access Control Lists (ACLs) permissioning system for controlling access to CiviCRM data. A CiviCRM ACL Role is not related to a Drupal Role. See the Permissions and access control chapter for more information.

To limit access to specific events, you can use Manage Access Control to assign access to specific groups of contacts.

docs.title: Testing the registration process
docs.text:
Test event registration before making your event public:

  1. Navigate to Events > Manage Events.
  2. From Event Links, select Test-drive to test the registration page. Test-drive mode uses your payment processor's sandbox options, if available, and creates a registrant record with a test indication so you can review and easily remove it.
  3. Fill out the registration form and complete the registration process.
  4. To find the new test participant record, navigate to Events > Find Participants.
  5. In the search criteria, check Find Test Participants.
  6. If you need to adjust event settings, navigate to Events > Manage Events and click Configure for the event.
  7. If you find elements to edit, select Configure to return to the list of event setting pages.
  8. If anonymous users register for your events, also test registration while not logged in. Refer to the Event Permissions information later in this chapter for details.

Once you are satisfied with the event information and registration form, it's time to display it on your website. The next section gives details of how to do this.

docs.title: Repeating events
docs.text: You can set an Event to repeat on a certain day and time with a specific end date, and include dates to exclude from the repetition.

docs.title: Set up a repeating event
docs.text:
1. Go to Manage Events. Under Configure, select Repeat from the dropdown.

  2. On the Repeat Event Screen, specify the Repeating intervals (in hours, days, weeks, months, or years), Event end date, and occurrence end date. It is also recommended that you specify the Repetition Start Date and Excluded Dates.

    Note

    If you would like your Scheduled Reminders to repeat, make sure you have setup Scheduled Reminders on the Event that you are repeating. You can edit this later. It is also recommended that you do not setup your reminders to repeat on specific days, but rather have them sent two weeks or a few days before the Event.

  3. Once you have filled out all the appropriate fields, click Save. A popup window will prompt you to Continue with your selection.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
There are several ways to report on and analyse events and participants.

The event dashboard gives a quick overview of upcoming events. For each event, it shows the number of registrations and their statuses: how many are registered, how many are counted, and how many are pending for different reasons. The dashboard is limited to 12 events scheduled to start at a date closest to today. This is most likely not to be sufficient to organizations with many scheduled events.

CiviCRM's search features and CiviReport provide more detailed and customised analysis. If you are interested in the financial aspects of events, you may also find the Reports and analysis chapter in Contributions useful.

docs.title: Searching based on participant data
docs.text:
CiviCRM distinguishes between contacts and event participants. Sometimes an event-related question is best answered in terms of contacts—for example, which contacts came to events in 2011. At other times, participants are more useful—for example, how many training sessions did we deliver as part of our sexual health education programme this year. Consider this distinction when searching for event attendees.

Find participants searches based on participant data and returns participant data. Advanced search searches based on most participant information, can combine it with other contact information, and returns contacts. You can also choose Participant from the Display Results As column to show participants rather than contacts.

These searches give you simple totals. You can also export the results as CSV for further analysis in spreadsheet software.

docs.title: Event and participant reports
docs.text:
Reports can do things that searches cannot. For instance, a search cannot aggregate data from multiple events at once or limit the date of registration very flexibly. Repeating the same searches can also be time consuming. Searches can be set as Smart Groups, but this leads to a proliferation of groups.

You can instead set up reports for an event or a collection of events. Reports can be automatically assigned to a designated submenu (e.g. under Events > Reports) or made available as dashlets for the main dashboard, as described below.

Out of the box, CiviCRM comes with four reports designed to help you analyse events:

  • Event Participants List displays participant and individual data, as well as all custom data. All of these can also be used as filters.
  • Attendee List provides a list of event attendees and can be filtered to show just one event. You add one blank column on the left of the list and tone, two or three at the right of the list and so create an event sign up sheet.
  • Event Income Detail and Event Income Summary work together to show details of revenue from events. The summary can show total income for a series of events, such as all of your conferences in 2011. Clicking on one of those events gives you more detail about its income breakdown per role and per status. It can also be displayed in graphical form as Pie Chart or Bar Chart.

docs.title: Create an event report from a template
docs.text: See Reporting Set-up for details.

docs.title: More analysis
docs.text: If you can't do what you want with a built in report or search, consider commissioning a new report or custom search. Read the CiviReport section for more information.

docs.title: Displaying an event report on CiviCRM's home dashboard
docs.text:
If you haven't already created any Event Reports, see the following chapter Reports and Analysis for instructions on how to create reports. Then make the report available for the dashboard:

  1. From the navigation menu, click Reports and select the report you wish to display.
  2. In the Report Settings area, check the Available for Dashboard? box.
  3. Click Update Report.

Once the report is available for the dashboard:

  1. Navigate to Home to view the dashboard.
  2. Click Configure Your Dashboard.
  3. Drag the desired report from the Available Dashlets area into either the Left Column or Right Column of the dashboard area, and click Done.
  4. You should now see your report on your home dashboard. To view the latest updated information for your report and any other items you've included on your dashboard, click Refresh Dashboard Data.

docs.title: What is CiviEvent?
docs.text:
CiviEvent provides tools for running events and reducing the administration involved. It supports both simple and complicated registration processes. Key features include:

  • Self-registration for participants, including online credit card payments
  • Tracking sign-ups, cancellations, and attendance
  • Promoting events on your website
  • Streamlining set-up for similar, recurring events with event templates and event copy functionality
  • Checking in participants on-site from any computer with an internet connection

docs.title: Scenario: Youth leadership workshop
docs.text:
Arts in Action, a community arts group, conducts leadership workshops for people under age 25 throughout the year. The group wants to attract new youth to its workshops and enlist past attendees to volunteer and teach. It invites youth from local schools and theater groups. Youth speakers, volunteers, and other speakers also take part in the training workshops.

Arts in Action communications staff use CiviEvent to manage each workshop from planning through evaluation. A staff member creates an event page with an online registration form. Because the workshops are regular events, a staff member has already created an event template that fills in much of the information needed during event set-up.

Registration has a flat fee, with additional fees for optional workshops. Attendees can select what they are registering for and pay online. The form also gathers participants' food and lodging preferences using a CiviCRM feature called a profile.

Staff draw a targeted list of youth and groups from existing contacts and send personalised invitations using CiviMail. The invitations also use a template, so information can be reused for future events. Each invitation links directly to the event page, allowing participants to reach online registration with a single click. Staff also announce the event on the Arts in Action website and enable the "Tell-a-friend" function so people can share it through their networks.

A designated staff person manages self-registration. They periodically check that payments are being made, manage the wait list when sign-ups exceed the maximum number of participants, and answer questions.

On the day of the event, organisers check in attendees on-site to track attendance and no-shows in real time. They can also ask participants with outstanding fees to pay. The database is updated immediately, freeing up spaces for those on the wait list and recording payments.

After each workshop, staff evaluate the event and use CiviEvent to generate reports, such as the number of attendees, total event fees paid, and total amount still due. They can update and save the event and mail templates for the next event.

docs.title: Some key concepts
docs.text: These concepts provide context for the step-by-step event tasks in the following chapters.

docs.title: Events, participants and contacts
docs.text: CiviCRM lets you create one or more events in which your contacts can participate. When a contact participates in an event, they are called a participant.

docs.title: Event types
docs.text:
CiviCRM lets you define Event Types, such as Conferences, Meetings and Fundraisers, according to your organization's needs.

Event Types are useful when different types of events have different requirements. For example, you can create custom fields to store and display additional data about an event based on its Event Type. See Custom data on events for more information.

You can also use Event Types to categorise and segment events and attendees. For example, you could find all contacts who attended one of your Workshops or Fundraising events.

docs.title: Participant default roles
docs.text:
Every contact who participates in an event is assigned a Participant Default Role. Attendee is a common role; others include Volunteer, Host and Speaker. Participant roles are fully customisable to match the events your organization conducts.

Roles let you segment participants by their involvement. For example, you could email Volunteers only or generate a list of past table captains for fundraisers. You can also create custom fields that apply only to specific roles, such as fields for collecting availability from Volunteers only.

docs.title: Participant statuses
docs.text:
Participant statuses, such as Registered, No-show, Attended and Cancelled, track a contact's stage in their 'event journey'. Statuses are fully customisable to match the way your organization handles event registration.

You can use statuses to segment participants by their behaviour with respect to an event—for example, to generate sign-in sheets, track how many people are likely to attend, or tailor emails to registrants.

docs.title: Other parts of CiviCRM that work with CiviEvent
docs.text:
CiviEvent works with other parts of CiviCRM. You can use CiviMail to promote an event to a targeted list and email participants before and after the event. For more information, see the Email section, particularly Set-up and Scheduled Reminders.

CiviEvent works with CiviContribute to accept event payments online. To do this, you must enable CiviContribute and set up a payment processor. See the Contributions section for more information.

docs.title: Popular extensions
docs.text:
These are widely used extensions in the relevant category of the official CiviCRM Extensions Directory. Usage is a popularity signal, not a compatibility or suitability guarantee.

  • CiviDiscount — reported usage: 1,834
  • no overwrite — reported usage: 918
  • Summary Fields — reported usage: 663
