docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
CiviCRM keeps an eye on changes that you make to contacts, memberships, and so on. Each contact has a change log tab, which is populated each time a contact is added or edited. The change log shows who changed the record and when the change was made. This light-weight logging is turned on by default, and many users find it detailed enough.

One key missing piece is information about what was changed. Detailed logging adds that information and provides other features.

docs.title: Detailed logging
docs.text:
When enabled, detailed logging tracks all changes made to data in CiviCRM. Each time something is updated, CiviCRM keeps a note of:

  • what the value was before
  • what the value is after
  • when the change was made
  • who made the change

When you turn on detailed logging, the screen will look something like the image below. Clicking on update on the left hand side will show details of the change.

This logging extends to almost all data that exists in CiviCRM, including contact, membership, and event data. It also covers the 'meta data' in your install, such as Activity Types, Case types, and Contribution Types.

With detailed logging turned on, any changes made to your data can be reverted. This means you can worry less about unwanted changes, whether they are made by administrative staff or by contacts interacting via your website—maliciously or accidentally.

Logging all changes to the database can collect quite a lot of data and have a small performance impact on your database. For this reason, detailed logging is turned off by default in CiviCRM, and people can turn it on if they require it. Before deciding whether to turn it on, consider other ways in which time-based logging happens in CiviCRM.

docs.title: Activities vs. logging
docs.text:
Activities can be a useful alternative to logging. Since each activity happens at a specific point in time, you can view the activity tab on a contact record as a log of changes to that contact over time.

This does not mean you should record an activity each time you change a contact in CiviCRM. In some use cases, the activity log provides a good enough record of changes over time. A couple of manually recorded activities may supplement it sufficiently for your logging needs.

docs.title: Membership logs
docs.text: Over time, a membership grows into a historical record, including any contributions that went toward that membership and any renewals, up-sells, and so on. This out-of-the-box logging might meet your needs without detailed logging.

docs.title: Reverting changes
docs.text:
One benefit of detailed logging is the ability to revert changes to your data. For many contact fields, a revert button at the bottom of the screen that shows details of the change makes this easy.

This screen is not available for all contact changes, but the data is still recorded behind the scenes. If you need to revert data that cannot be reverted via the user interface, contact your system administrator or get help from someone familiar with CiviCRM's detailed logging functionality.

docs.title: Customizing the user interface
docs.text:
CiviCRM is highly flexible and customizable. This page describes ways to change the interface to suit your needs and make it easier for your users.

Customizing the data you collect and track is covered in Organising Your Data and in the What you need to know and Set-up chapters for the different CiviCRM components. For example, the Events section covers customizing event types.

docs.title: Changing dropdown options
docs.text:
You can add, rename, disable, or remove options in dropdown fields on contact entry and editing forms at Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Dropdown Options. These include:

  • Gender
  • Individual prefixes and suffixes (e.g., Ms., Mr. and Jr., Sr.)
  • Phone types (e.g. Phone, Mobile, Pager)
  • Mobile phone providers (e.g. Sprint, Verizon and Cingular)
  • Instant messenger services (e.g., Yahoo, MSN, AIM, GTalk, Jabber and Skype)
  • Website types (e.g., Work, Facebook, Twitter)
  • Location types (e.g., Home, Work, Billing, Main). Billing location is assigned to Billing Addresses entered when constituents contribute or pay for event and membership fees online. Location type names may not contain spaces (e.g., Summer Home is not permitted; use SummerHome).

You can also change the Preferred Communication Methods choices (e.g., Phone, Email, Postal Mail, SMS) on the contact entry and editing form at Administer > Communications > Preferred Communications Methods.

Modifying dropdown options that define data—such as Activity Type, Relationship Type, and Contribution Status—is outside the scope of this page. See Organising Your Data and the sections on the different CiviCRM components.

docs.title: Changing display preferences
docs.text:
If you do not track certain activities or collect certain categories of data, you can hide their fields and tabs from users. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Display Preferences.

To change which tabs appear when viewing contact records, check or uncheck the boxes next to Viewing Contacts.

For example, if your organization does not use Cases or Grants, you can uncheck those boxes to hide the tabs. If you later decide to use them, check the boxes to display them again. Information stored in hidden tabs remains in your database and will appear when you display the tabs again.

To change which blocks appear when editing a contact, check or uncheck the boxes next to Editing Contacts.

For example, if your organization does not collect Demographics or Communication Preferences information, you can uncheck those boxes. Information in fields you hide remains in your database, and you can display it again by rechecking the boxes.

docs.title: Disabling popup forms
docs.text: CiviCRM uses popup dialog boxes for viewing and editing data. To disable them and use traditional browsing, deselect Enable Popup Forms in administer > customize data and screens > display preferences. CiviCRM will be slower with this feature disabled because every form will require a complete page load in the browser.

docs.title: Disabling activity assignee notifications
docs.text: By default, CiviCRM sends notifications to all activity assignees when an activity is created. To disable this, deselect Notify Activity Assignees in Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Display Preferences. You can also selectively disable email notifications for specific activity types by selecting them in the field below.

docs.title: Customizing search preferences
docs.text:
You can change CiviCRM's default search behavior at Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Search Preferences. Available options are:

  • Automatic Wildcard (choose Yes or No): If you choose Yes, wildcards are added to the beginning and end of the search term when users search for contacts by Name. For example, searching for "ada" returns names that include those letters, such as Adams, Janet and Nadal, Jorge. If disabled, a wildcard is still added to the end of the search term. Searching for "ada" then returns a last name that begins with those letters, such as Adams, Janet, but not Nadal, Jorge. You might disable this to speed up searching on a large database.
  • Include Email (choose Yes or No): If you choose Yes, email addresses are included when users search by Name. You might disable this to speed up searching on a large database.
  • Include Nickname (choose Yes or No): If you choose Yes, the contents of the Nickname field are included when users search by Name.
  • Include Alphabetical Pager (choose Yes or No): If you choose Yes, a bar appears at the top of search results so you can choose a letter of the alphabet. Clicking A, for example, takes you to a page displaying only contacts that begin with A. You might disable this to speed up searching on a large database.
  • Include Order By Clause (choose Yes or No): If you choose No, your search results will not be ordered.
  • Smart group cache timeout: Determines how often the smart group cache is refreshed. A value of 0 turns off caching. What works for your site may vary. More information is in the admin guide..
  • Autocomplete Contact Search: Checkboxes for basic contact fields (name, email, phone, etc). Checked fields appear in the autocomplete results list when you use the Quick Search bar at the top left of all screens.
  • Contact Reference Options: Checkboxes for basic contact fields (name, email, phone, etc). Checked fields appear in the autocomplete dropdown search results for 'Contact Reference' custom fields.
  • Autocomplete Results: Determines the maximum number of results displayed when typing in an autocomplete field.

If your database is large and searches are slow, consider disabling some of these options to increase speed.

There is another place to customize search settings: Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Display Preferences has a block of Contact Search settings.

These checkboxes affect the Search > Find Contacts and Search > Advanced Search screens. Uncheck a box to remove the corresponding type of field from those search screens.

docs.title: Customizing date preferences
docs.text:
The default display preference for dates is set at Administer > Localization > Date Formats.

You can override this default and define the range of allowed dates for specific field types at Administer > Customise Data and Screens > Date Preferences.

By default, CiviCRM provides ranges for input on specific date fields. For instance, the default range for Activity Dates extends from 20 years before the current year through 10 years beyond it. To track activities that occurred 25 years ago, you would need to update this range so users can log them.

docs.title: Customizing the navigation menu
docs.text:
You can add, delete, rename, and move items in the CiviCRM navigation bar. For example, you can:

  • Remove menu items you do not use.
  • Add items to support specific workflows (e.g. data entry Profiles).
  • Add links to non-CiviCRM web pages or apps.
  • Rename menu items to use terms familiar to your users.
  • Move menu items to better support your work.

To customize menu items, go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Navigation Menu. The menu items appear as folder icons in a file structure. Expand folders by clicking the small triangles to the left of their names.

  • To delete an item, right-click it and select Delete.
  • To rename an item, right-click it and select Rename.
  • To move an item, drag and drop it to the desired location in the tree structure.
  • To add an item:
  • Click Add Menu Item.
  • Enter the text you want to appear in the menu in the Title field.
  • Enter the link to your item in the Url field.
  • Select the location of the new item from the Parent dropdown menu. You can place it anywhere in the navigation, at any level. For a top-level item, leave this dropdown unselected.
  • Check Separator if you want a line below the new item to separate it from the item below.

docs.title: Making custom data entry forms
docs.text:
If staff or volunteers often enter batches of similar contacts manually, you can create a Profile containing only the fields they need.

  1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Profiles and click Add Profile.
  2. Give your Profile a clear name related to its purpose (e.g., Name and Address Data Entry Form).
  3. Check the Standalone Form or Directory box in the Used For field.
  4. Use Pre-form Help and Post-form Help to add text for people doing data entry.
  5. Click Save. This takes you to the Add Fields screen, where you can choose fields for your Profile.
  6. From Field Name, select the contact record type containing the field you want: Contact, Individual, Organization, Household, or a custom contact subtype you have created. Other record types on this menu will not work with data entry forms, so do not choose them. Fields that apply to more than one kind of contact record type, such as Phone or Email for both Individuals and Organizations, are found on the Contacts menu.
  7. From the dropdown menu that appears, choose the field you want.
  8. If the automatically populated Field Label is not what you want on the form, edit it.
  9. If every record entered through the form must have data in this field, check Required?.
  10. Use Field Pre Help and Field Post Help to add text for people doing data entry.
  11. Use Order to change where the field appears on the form. Lower numbers appear before higher numbers.
  12. Click Save and New to add more fields, and Save when you are finished.
  13. On the screen listing your fields and settings, click Preview (all fields) to check the form. Click Use (create mode) to go to the page containing the form. Copy its link and use it to create a navigation menu item (see Customizing the navigation menu).

docs.title: Customizing search views
docs.text:
1. Create or open a profile and mark it as used for Search Views (known as Search Results in 4.1 and previous).
  2. When adding fields to this profile, set their Visibility to Public Pages and check the Results Column box.

When conducting an advanced search, use the Search Views dropdown menu at the top right of the page to select your Profile.

docs.title: Using Word Replacement to change terminology
docs.text:
CiviCRM's Word Replacement setting lets you replace existing system text with text you choose. For example, if your organization calls monetary transactions "donations" rather than "contributions," you can define a replacement that changes the term throughout your CiviCRM instance.

To use Word Replacement:

  1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Word Replacements.
  2. Enter the original text in the Original column on the left and the replacement text in the Replacement column on the right.
  3. Check the Exact Match box on the right to replace only exact matches. For example, without Exact Match, replacing "Contribution" with "Donation" also replaces "Contributions" with "Donations"; with Exact Match, it does not.
  4. Check the Enabled box on the left to enable the replacement.
  5. Add additional rows using Add row.
  6. Click Save when you have entered the replacements.

Anticipate alternate forms of words and different ways your chosen word or phrase may appear in CiviCRM.

Note

If you're using CiviCRM in another language, word replacements only work if you enter the English words as the original text to replace, not the words in the language you are using.

docs.title: Date localization
docs.text: Date and time conventions often vary by country and language. To configure the conventions for your locale, use Administer > Localization > Date Formats. The page includes several sections.

docs.title: Date display
docs.text:
Dates display differently depending on the context. An accounting report may list 1,000 donations in a data-table; to conserve space, the data-table uses a short notation (eg 09/19/22). By contrast, an event registration form uses a long notation (eg September 19th, 2022) to maximize clarity.

CiviCRM defines ~7 common ways to format a date or time, and each one can be tuned to local preferences. For example, in the United States, a typical configuration might look like this:

Format Name Example Configuration Example Value "Complete Date and Time" %B %E%f, %Y %l:%M %P September 18th, 2022 11:58 PM "Complete Date" %B %E%f, %Y September 19th, 2022 "Short Date" %m/%d/%Y 09/18/2022 "Month and Year" %B %Y September 2022 "Time Only" %l:%M %P 1:34 PM "Year Only" %Y 2022 "Financial Batch" %m/%d/%Y 09/19/2022

For a full listing of formatting codes, see PHP Manual: strftime().

docs.title: Date input fields
docs.text: Some forms require the user to enter a date or time. Date Input Format and Time Input Format adjust the data-entry screens.

docs.title: Calendar
docs.text: Type in the day you want for the beginning of the week, and the month and day you want for the start of the fiscal year.

docs.title: Date preferences
docs.text:
By default, CiviCRM provides ranges for input on specific date fields. For instance, the default range for Activity Dates is 20 years prior to the current year through to 10 years beyond the current year. If you would like to track activities that occurred, say, 25 years ago, you need to update this range to enable your end users to log these activities.

To update these settings to the appropriate range, go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Date Preferences. If you leave these settings as the default, you will see an error such as this: Please enter a date between 01/01/1994 and 12/31/2024.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Administer » System Settings » Debugging and Error Handling

Debugging options are covered in the developer documentation.

docs.title: Fatal error settings
docs.text:
• Fatal Error Template - Enter the path and filename for a custom Smarty template if you want to define your own screen for displaying fatal errors.
  • Fatal Error Handler - Enter the path and class for a custom PHP error-handling function if you want to override built-in CiviCRM error handling for your site.

Click Save to save your action or Cancel to cancel it.

If successful you will see the message "Your changes have been saved."

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Once CiviCRM is installed, review the initial configuration tasks to customize it for your organization.

Log in to your CiviCRM site and navigate to Administer > Administration Console > Configuration Checklist. This page covers general tasks; component-specific configuration is covered in each component section.

Use the checklist to review and complete configuration tasks for your site. You will be redirected back to it after saving each setting. Settings you have not yet reviewed appear in red. After you visit a page, its link appears in green, although you may still need to revisit it to complete or update the settings.

docs.title: Language and region
docs.text:
Localization adapts CiviCRM for use in a specific country or language by translating on-screen text and setting region-specific formats for dates and money, including currency. By default, CiviCRM is localized for the United States. Review and update the values on this screen if you use CiviCRM in a different country, need to store contact addresses in countries other than the United States, or want to use another language.

CiviCRM has been translated into a number of languages. Translations contributed by community members are available to download when you download CiviCRM. If CiviCRM is not available in your language, you may wish to translate it. You can find a translation guide on the wiki.

You can also configure your site to support multiple languages. In this mode, users can choose from a list of available languages after logging in. You can create and store multi-language versions of text, including custom field labels, an online contribution page, campaign information and event descriptions.

  • Default Language - If the additional language files have been installed, this dropdown lets you select a language other than US English as the default. This affects all CiviCRM users.
  • Inherit CMS Language - By default, the language CiviCRM uses is independent of the CMS. If 'yes', CiviCRM uses the language in use in the CMS.
  • Available Languages - If 'Inherit CMS Language' is set to 'No', the 'Available Languages' option appears. It lets you make additional languages available to site users. If more than one language is selected, a language switcher block appears so users can select their interface language.
    • In multi-lingual mode, the list of 'Available languages' consists of those configured in the database.
  • Default Language for contacts - Controls the default 'preferred language' when creating a new contact. Preferred Language is used for some communications on multi-lingual sites.

Multiple Languages Support - If multi-lingual mode is enabled, database tables are modified to store multiple translations of certain fields. For example, with English and French configured, two fields are created for a field such as event title: one in English and one in French. This mode can be useful for organisations operating in multiple languages.

You may also wish to configure how currency is displayed. CiviCRM lets you configure the characters that separate numbers: for example, in the US you would see 1,000.00, but in Demark it might look like 1.000,00. These are configured as the 'thousands separator' and 'decimal delimiter' on the localization page. However, from 5.43 these settings are ignored if you add the line below to your civicrm.settings.php; the system decides based on the locale instead. Allowing the system to decide is likely to give better results if you communicate with people in more than one language.

define('IGNORE_SEPARATOR_CONFIG', TRUE);

docs.title: Organization address and contact info
docs.text:
Use this screen to enter identifying information for the organization or entity that "owns" this CiviCRM installation. The organization name and address identify your organization in CiviMail mailings when you include the {domain.name} and {domain.address} tokens.

Enter a valid email address belonging to your organization. It will be used as the From field in system-generated (automated) emails.

docs.title: Enable components
docs.text:
This screen lets you turn components on or off for your CiviCRM system.

When you first install CiviCRM, the most frequently used components—CiviContribute, CiviEvent, CiviMail, CiviMember and CiviReport—are already enabled. You can disable components you do not need. You can also enable any or all of CiviCampaign, CiviCase, CiviGrant and CiviPledge. You can return to this page at any time to enable more components.

You can disable a component you have already used. Its information is retained and will still be there if you re-enable it, although disabling a component you have used would be unusual. If you want to simplify the administration menu and advanced search page, using permissions may be a better approach.

docs.title: Display preferences
docs.text:
This screen lets you modify screen and form elements for the following tasks:

  • Viewing Contacts - Controls the tabs displayed when viewing a contact record. For example, if your organization does not track Relationships, deselect this option to simplify the display. Tabs for Contributions, Pledges, Memberships, Events, Grants and Cases are also hidden if the corresponding component is not enabled.
  • Viewing Smart Groups - Controls the display of the smart groups a contact belongs to.
  • Editing Contacts - Controls the sections included when adding or editing a contact record. For example, if your organization does not record Gender and Birth Date for individuals, deselect Demographics to simplify the form.
  • Contact Search - Controls the sections included in the Advanced Search form. For example, if you do not track Relationships, you will not search for that section, so you can deselect the option to simplify the form.
  • Check for Similar Contacts - Controls how new contacts are checked for similarity to existing contacts.
  • Notify Activity Assignees - If enabled, assignees of new activities receive an email with a copy of the activity. Emails can be suppressed for specific Activity Types by entering them in 'Do not notify assignees for'.
  • Contact Dashboard - Lets constituents view the groups they subscribe to, their contribution history, event registration information and more. You can control which sections appear. For example, deselect contribution history if you do not want constituents to view their own.
  • WYSIWYG Editor - Select CKEditor to help users enter text in fields that allow HTML formatting, such as the introductory section of an online contribution page. You can configure CKEditor (http://ckeditor.com/) to add or remove functionality and change the order of toolbar elements using its built-in configuration page. Click the Configure CKEditor button to access that page. Select Textarea if you do not want a WYSIWYG editor.
  • Enable Popup Forms - On by default. Uncheck it to return to opening a form by refreshing the page.
  • Individual Display Name - Display name format for individual contact display names.
  • Individual Sort Name - Sort Name format for individual contact sort names.
  • Menubar position - Choose whether the CiviCRM menu appears above, below or in place of the CMS menu, or hide the CiviCRM menu altogether.
  • Menubar color - Choose a background colour for the menubar. For accessibility, it is best practice to choose a colour that contrasts with the menubar font colour. Use a free online contrast ratio checker if you are unsure.
  • Backend Theme - If you have installed a theme through the Extension Manager, you can specify it here or turn off CSS theming with 'None (Unstyled)'. If left at 'Automatic', CiviCRM uses its default theme (Greenwich).
  • Frontend Theme - You can select a theme or remove theming for front-end pages.

docs.title: Address settings
docs.text:
At Localization > Address Settings, you can modify the default fields for adding and editing contact and event address data. You can also change the address field layout used on screens and mailing labels.

Review the out-of-the-box defaults by adding a new contact record and noting the address fields on the form. Save the record and note the order of fields on the Contact Summary screen. If you plan to generate mailing labels, review the label layout: select Mailing Labels from the -actions- drop-down after searching with the Find Contacts menu option.

After reviewing the default fields and layouts, review the Address Settings screen and make changes as needed.

Tip

CiviCRM uses tokens (e.g. {contact.street_address}) to reference specific fields in the database.

  • Mailing Labels - Controls mailing-label formatting. The default format is:

    {contact.addressee}
{contact.street_address}
{contact.supplemental_address_1}
{contact.supplemental_address_2}
{contact.city}{, }{contact.state_province}{ }{contact.postal_code}
{contact.country}

    You must include the {contact.addressee} token to include the addressee's name on labels. When generating labels from a list of contacts, users can select from label types corresponding to the label manufacturer code. Test your format with the label type and printer you plan to use to verify spacing.

  • Address Display - Controls the layout of contact and event location addresses displayed on CiviCRM screens. The default format is:

    {contact.address_name}
{contact.street_address}
{contact.supplemental_address_1}
{contact.supplemental_address_2}
{contact.city}{, }{contact.state_province}{ }{contact.postal_code}
{contact.country}

    This format also applies to event locations, despite using the contact record type in the layout. The {contact.address_name} token is particularly useful for events where you need to include a location name, such as "Smithson Hall".

  • Address Editing Fields - Modifies the available address editing fields. You can hide fields you do not plan to use to simplify forms. For example, if you do not plan to record latitude and longitude for contacts, you can deselect those fields.

    • Street Address Parsing - CiviCRM uses the US Postal Service's (USPS) Postal Addressing Standards to parse an address into Street Number, Street Name and Apt/Unit/Suite fields. Entering addresses that conform to those standards helps keep data consistent and makes the best use of Street Address Parsing. When parsing is on, you can edit and or view the parsed address by clicking Edit Address Elements while editing an address.

Learn more about USPS' Postal Addressing Standards at http://pe.usps.com/text/pub28/welcome.htm.

  • Address Standardization - CiviCRM includes an optional interface to the United States Postal Services (USPS) Address Standardization web service. You must register at https://www.usps.com/business/web-tools-apis/welcome.htm. If approved, you will receive a User ID and service URL. The URL provided by USPS will not be prefixed with "http://". When entering it in the CiviCRM settings field, you must prefix it with "http://".

docs.title: Mapping and geocoding
docs.text:
CiviCRM supports the Google and OpenStreetMap mapping services. These let users display contact addresses and event locations on a map. To enable mapping, select a mapping provider and obtain a key for your site from that provider.

You can also select a Geocoding Provider, which can be the same as or different from your mapping provider. Once enabled, the service automatically geocodes contact and event records as you add or edit address data: it calculates or retrieves latitude and longitude and inserts them.

Other mapping and geocoding services can be added by installing extensions.

docs.title: Search settings
docs.text:
These settings adjust search behaviors, including wildcard use and the data included in quick search results. Adjusting them can improve performance for large datasets.

A wildcard substitutes for other characters in a search. The percent character "%" substitutes for zero or more characters; the underscore character "_" substitutes for a single character. Wildcards can broaden search results. For example, 'Volunteer%' as an Activity Subject matches a subject starting with "Volunteer", such as "Volunteer for Open House" or "Volunteering Opportunities".

  • Automatic Wildcards - By default, when users search for contacts by Name, the Search interface treats the text as though it were surrounded by percent signs. For example, 'ada' returns names containing those letters, such as 'Adams, Janet' and 'Nadal, Jorge'. Disabling this feature significantly speeds up searches in large databases, but users must explicitly use "%" or "_" for partial name searches.
  • Include Email - By default, a Name search also searches email addresses. Disabling this feature significantly speeds up searches in large databases, but users must use Email search fields in Advanced Search, Search Builder or Profiles to find contacts by email address.
  • Include Nickname - By default, nicknames are not included in Name searches. Set this to Yes to include them.
  • Include Alphabetical Pager - Disabling this hides the alphabetical pager on search screens and improves search-result response time for large datasets.
  • Include Order By Clause - Disabling this leaves search results unordered and significantly improves search-result response time for large datasets.
  • Default Contact Search Profile - Select a Profile to override the default columns in Find Contacts search results.
  • Smart group cache timeout - Smart groups are saved searches. Their contact lists are cached in the database so the saved search does not run every time a smart group is accessed. This field sets the number of minutes before the cache is refreshed. The default, 0, empties the cache immediately when a contact is edited or added. If contact data changes frequently, a value of 5 minutes or longer may reduce server processing load. The drawback is that users may see old data for a few minutes after new data is added.
  • Autocomplete Contact Search - If enabled, selected fields appear in auto-complete dropdown lists and the "Quick Search" box on the navigation menu. The contact name is always included.

  • Contact Reference Options - Selected fields appear in autocomplete dropdown search results for 'Contact Reference' custom fields. Contact Name is always included.

    Note

    You must assign 'access contact reference fields' permission to the anonymous role to use custom contact reference fields in profiles on public pages. In most situations, use 'Limit List to Group' when configuring a contact reference field for a public form to prevent exposing your entire contact list.

  • Autocomplete Results - Sets the maximum number of contacts shown at a time when typing in an autocomplete field. The default is 10.

  • InnoDB Full Text Search - If you use MySQL 5.6+, you can enable InnoDB full-text search optimizations.

docs.title: Miscellaneous (undelete, PDFs, limits, logging, etc.)
docs.text:
Use the Miscellaneous Settings screen to configure these behaviors:

  • Dashboard Cache Timeout - Number of minutes to cache dashlet content on the dashboard.
  • Checksum Lifespan - Number of days before a personalized (hashed) link expires.
  • Contact Trash and Undelete - If enabled, deleted contacts move to the trash rather than being destroyed. Users with the proper permission can search for and restore them, or delete them permanently.
  • Logging - See Logging Settings in the System Administrator Guide.
  • Attach PDF copy to receipts - If enabled, CiviCRM attaches a PDF receipt during event sign-up or online contribution.
  • Path to wkhtmltopdf executable - wkhtmltopdf is an alternative PDF-generation utility that may perform better when generating many PDF letters or receipts. Your system administrator must download and install it, then enter its executable path here. WARNING: wkhtmltopdf is no longer under active development and its latest tagged release of 0.12.6 from June 2020 (https://github.com/wkhtmltopdf/wkhtmltopdf/tree/0.12.6) is insecure and should not be used (https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2022-35583).
  • New Version Alerts - If enabled, on-screen alerts appear for users with "Administer CiviCRM" permissions when a new CiviCRM version is available. This works only if "Version Check & Statistics Reporting" is enabled.
  • Version Checking and Statistics Reporting - Automatically checks for a newer stable CiviCRM version. New version alerts appear on the main CiviCRM Administration page. The following statistics are anonymously reported to the CiviCRM team to help prioritize development: CiviCRM version; PHP, MySQL and framework (Drupal/Joomla!/WordPress) versions; default language; and record counts, but no actual data. Set this field to No if you are not comfortable reporting this information for your site.
  • Display "empowered by CiviCRM" - If enabled, "empowered by CiviCRM" appears at the bottom of public forms. This helps increase awareness of CiviCRM.
  • Maximum Attachments - Increase or decrease the maximum number of files, such as documents and images, that can be attached to emails, activities and grant records. The default is 3.
  • Maximum File Size (in MB) - Maximum size of a file, such as a document or image, that can be attached to emails or activities. Your PHP configuration files, php.ini, should support a file size at least as large as the value specified here.
  • Allow second-degree relationship permissions - If enabled, contacts who can edit a related contact inherit that contact's permission to edit other related contacts. For example, this can let a class teacher edit the records of students in that class when both are linked to the class, set up as an organisation sub-type, through relationships.

docs.title: Contact types
docs.text: You can change the names of the built-in Contact Types (Individual, Household, Organizations) and create or modify "contact subtypes" for more specific uses, such as Student, Parent or Team.

docs.title: Outbound email
docs.text:
To send emails to contacts through CiviCRM, enter settings that let CiviCRM connect to your mail server. These emails include contributor receipts, event registration confirmations and CiviMail bulk mailings.

CiviCRM supports three methods of connecting to a mail server: mail (the built-in PHP mail function), SMTP (Simple Mail Transport Protocol) and Sendmail. Each requires specific settings. If you do not know which method or values to use, check with your system administrator, ISP or hosting provider.

Always send a test email after entering or changing the settings. Click "Save and Send Test Email", shown below. An email is sent to the address associated with your user login account. The From email address is the default From address configured in the previous section.

If CiviCRM cannot send the test email, a message on the screen gives the specific error and suggestions for trouble-shooting it.

Disable Outbound Email - If selected, no mails are sent. If you disable outbound email while using Online Contribution pages or online Event Registration, turn off automated receipting and registration confirmations, which are enabled by default. Otherwise, constituents will see errors after completing a contribution or registration.

Redirect to Database - If selected, all emails are recorded as archived mailings instead of being sent.

See Email System Configuration in the System Administration guide for more details.

docs.title: From email addresses
docs.text:
CiviCRM uses the default From address defined here for automated emails. If you have entered an email address on the Domain Information screen, it is listed here, as illustrated in the leftmost field below.

When users send an email through CiviCRM, their primary email address is the default From address. They can instead select one of the general email addresses defined here. To prevent users from sending from their own Primary address and restrict them to the "From Email Address Options", use the Outbound Mail settings at Administer › System Settings › Outbound Email(SMTP/Sendmail).

docs.title: Payment processors
docs.text:
Payment processors handle credit card transactions for merchants and non-profit organizations, then transfer funds to the organization's bank account. If you plan to accept online contributions, online membership sign-up and renewal, or online event registration through CiviCRM, select and configure a payment processor.

CiviCRM supports several processors, and third-party developers can add support for others based on their clients' needs. Processors differ in pricing and features. Investigate the options to find the best fit for your organization. See Payment Processors for factors to consider.

Configuration and testing steps differ by processor. See installing payment processors in the System Administrator Guide.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: See Permissions and access control for information on setting permissions.

docs.title: System workflow templates
docs.text:
CiviCRM includes system-generated emails, such as contribution receipts and event registration confirmations. These system workflow templates will be sent with your organization's name. Review them and customize their style and wording here.

Workflow messages contain both text AND necessary program logic. Edit carefully to avoid changing the program logic. After making changes, test the workflow and review the emails sent. If changes cause problems, errors or missing information, you can "Revert" to the system default for that workflow.

You should now have reviewed the basic configuration tasks. The remaining checklist tasks require an understanding of how to record and use contact data and are best left until you have read more in this book.

docs.title: System status
docs.text: The system status screen at Administer > Administration Console > System Status (or /civicrm/a/#/status) reports potential problems with your installation, configuration or server environment. See System Status in the System Administrator Guide for help interpreting the results and responding to reported problems.

docs.title: Installation and basic set-up
docs.text: This information is for technicians and may be difficult to understand if you have little or no experience setting up web applications. In that case, you may wish to seek help or point your organisation's technical staff to this material.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
CiviCRM must be installed on a computer with a web server (such as Apache or nginx), PHP and MySQL. Some prefer to try CiviCRM on their local computer before installing it on a dedicated web server. If you don't have these prerequisites, you can download packages from the Internet such as WAMP, XAMPP, MAMPP and LAMP. The first two packages are for Windows and the second two are for the Macintosh and Linux, respectively.

Consider where you host your CiviCRM instance. Discuss hosting with your System Administrator and review the Hosting information in the System Admin guide.

Before installation, decide which CMS (Content Management System: used for building and managing websites) you wish to integrate with. The open-source options are Drupal, WordPress and Joomla!, or you can use Standalone CiviCRM.

You can find full installation instructions in the System Administrator Guide.

docs.title: Internet vs. local installs
docs.text: Most organisations access CiviCRM over the internet. Some organizations that only want internal staff to have access, and are security conscious, choose to install CiviCRM on an internal network where it is accessible only internally. The downside of an installation that is not publicly available is that contacts cannot 'self serve' to update their data.

docs.title: Securing your system
docs.text: Once CiviCRM is installed, it is important to secure your system. The System Administrator Guide describes techniques for securing your server and website.

docs.title: Upgrades
docs.text:
New versions of CiviCRM are released every month. Although extensions are typically how you add major new features, you need to upgrade the CiviCRM core software periodically to keep your site secure and take advantage of smaller new features and improvements. Some upgrades contain security fixes that are crucial to apply in a timely manner.

Plan for the people and time needed to upgrade your site. Read release notes thoroughly to understand how an upgrade may change it. Test upgrades on a copy of your live site to make sure the process runs smoothly. Back up your site and database before upgrading your live site, even if you tested the process on a test site.

Because upgrades are important and technical, many organisations employ a CiviCRM expert service provider to carry them out.

docs.title: Mapping and geocoding
docs.text:
Visit Administer > System Settings > Mapping and Geocoding to configure mapping and geocoding providers.

Mapping Provider Select the service used to build and display the maps shown in the CiviCRM UI.

Mapping Provider Key Enter your API Key or Application ID for the selected mapping provider. For Google Maps, refer to developers.google.com for the latest information. For OpenStreetMaps, you now require an API key from CARTO.

API Key for OpenStreetMaps usage

Maps under OpenStreetMaps rely on images from CARTO, which requires an API key. Without a valid API key, your maps may be repeatedly overlaid with an "API KEY REQUIRED" watermark. See CARTO's documentation for information on API keys for CARTO.

Geocoding Provider Select the service used to look up latitude and longitude for contact addresses so they can be shown on maps.

Geo Provider Key Enter the API key as required by your GeoCoding provider.

Click Save to save your action or Cancel to cancel it. If successful, you will see the message "Your changes have been saved."

Internal Server and/or Firewall Issues

If CiviCRM is installed on a server that does not have access to the public internet, or a firewall prevents CiviCRM from communicating with your chosen web services, you will see one or more fatal errors when attempting to add or edit contact records. To resolve this, either disable Mapping and Geocoding or resolve the connectivity issue.

After enabling the mapping provider, configure the job.geocode scheduled job to geocode addresses without a latitude and longitude according to the configured options.

Usage Limits

Some providers have usage limits on their Mapping and Geocoding APIs. If you go over the limits, you may receive an overlimit error when trying to save an address.

docs.title: Alternative geocoding providers
docs.text: If you need an alternative Geocoding Provider, you may wish to evaluate this extension, which includes many improvements: https://civicrm.org/extensions/geocoder

docs.title: CMS permissions
docs.text: All CMS have the same set of CiviCRM permissions, but the permissions are found in different places and differ slightly in appearance.

docs.title: Permissions in Drupal
docs.text:
To access Drupal's permissions, go to the Drupal menu, choose People and click the Permissions tab in the top right corner of the pop-up window. The list shows possible operations or actions in CiviCRM and Drupal, with a column for each existing role type. Checking an option in a column grants that role the ability to perform the action.

You may create new roles and edit existing ones. To edit roles, click Roles toward the top right of the page while in the Permissions tab.

Roles can be assigned to users in either of these ways:

  • Open a user's contact record (a contact in CiviCRM with a user account), click Actions at the top and select User Record. On the next screen, click the Edit tab at the top right, then scroll to Roles to change their level of access.
  • As an administrator, select People from the Drupal menu. In the list of active users, click the user's name to open their Drupal user profile. Click the Edit tab at the top right, then scroll to Roles.

docs.title: Permissions in Joomla!
docs.text:
To find permissions in Joomla!:

  1. Log into the Joomla! administrative portal.
  2. Go to Components and select CiviCRM.
  3. In CiviCRM's menu, navigate to Administer > User and Permissions > Permissions (Access Control).
  4. Click Joomla Access Control at the top of the list.

Joomla! assigns permissions through user groups (roles). Each group is either a parent or child of another group; child groups lower in the table inherit permissions set for groups above them. When editing a user group's permissions, you can choose:

  • Inherited: if the group above has the permission, this group can also perform the action.
  • Allowed: users in this group can perform the operation.
  • Denied: users in this group cannot perform the action.

Joomla! has two additional permissions not used by Drupal or WordPress: Configure Joomla! ACL (the user can configure Joomla! ACLs and is assigned all CiviCRM permissions) and Show CiviCRM Component (the user can see CiviCRM in the Components list).

To assign a user group to a user or change their existing group, log in as an administrator and use either method:

  • In CiviCRM, open the user's contact record, click Action and select User Record. Change roles in Assigned User Groups.
  • In the Joomla! administrative portal, click User Manager under User. Click a name in the list of users to open their account settings, including user group.

docs.title: Access Control (Permissions) in WordPress
docs.text:
In CiviCRM, go to Administer > User and Permissions > Permissions (Access Control). Select WordPress Access Control. Here you can adjust the CiviCRM settings for each predefined User Role from WordPress.

Roles can be assigned to users in either of these ways:

  • Open a user's contact record (a contact in CiviCRM with a user account), click Actions at the top and select User Record. On the Edit User screen, change their Role to change their level of access.
  • In the WordPress Site Admin area, select Users to see all users. Click a name to open the Edit User screen, where you can change their Role.

docs.title: Financial Type Permissions
docs.text:
By default, access to Contribution data is controlled by access CiviContribute, edit contributions and delete in CiviContribute. These permissions apply to all contributions, regardless of financial type.

To set different permissions for contributions based on financial type:

  1. Begin with CiviCRM installed within Drupal, Backdrop, or WordPress. (This feature is not yet available for Joomla.)
  2. Go to Administer > CiviContribute > CiviContribute Component Settings.
  3. Check Enable Access Control by Financial Type.
  4. Edit your CMS permissions. CiviCRM has added a 'view', 'edit' and 'delete' permission for every financial type. Assign these permissions as needed.

Tip

You must grant the add and view permission for each financial type to the anonymous user role for visitors to be able to access your contribution pages.

For example, you may use this feature to let some users manage event payments without seeing donation data.

docs.title: Anonymous and Authenticated roles
docs.text:
You will encounter both role types when working with access controls. Their names may differ between CMSes, but the basic principle is the same.

The anonymous role (public in Joomla!) applies to visitors who have not logged in. It has the lowest level of permissions.

The default CiviCRM permissions for this role are listed below. Actual permissions may vary depending on your CMS and how you installed CiviCRM, so check that they are set up as you want them.

Permission Description CiviCRM: access all custom data View all custom fields - i.e. see/enter information in custom data fields in forms CiviCRM: access uploaded files View / download files including images and photos CiviCRM: profile create Add data in a profile form CiviCRM: profile edit Edit data in a profile form CiviCRM: profile view View data in a profile CiviEvent: register for events Register for events on your website CiviEvent: view event info View event information pages CiviEvent: view event participants View the participants that have signed up to an event CiviContribute: make online contributions Make payments or donations through your website CiviMail: access CiviMail subscribe/unsubscribe pages Subscribe/unsubscribe from mailing lists CiviMail: view public CiviMail content View mailings on your website CiviCampaign: sign CiviCRM Petition Sign petitions (if CiviCampaign is enabled)

The authenticated role (registered in Joomla, subscriber in WordPress) applies to visitors who have logged in. It is the default role for new user accounts and cannot be deleted. By default, its CiviCRM permissions are the same as those for the anonymous role.

You can alter permissions for anonymous and authenticated users. The following scenarios show when you might do so.

docs.title: Taking online contributions
docs.text: If you only want contributions from logged-in users, remove make online contributions from the "anonymous" or "public" role.

docs.title: Viewing event info and registering for events
docs.text:
If view event info and register for events are enabled for anonymous and authenticated roles, all visitors can register for any event. To let only specific users view or register for some events, use a CiviCRM ACL. Give a role "view" access if its users should only view event information, or "edit" permission if they can register. For this to work, disable the CMS register for events permission, which would otherwise override these settings.

For example, a charity holds public fundraising events and private evening dinners for some corporate donors. Any visitor can register for a fundraising event, but only some donors should have access to the dinners. CiviCRM ACLs can specify which events each group can access, unlike the CMS register for events permission.

docs.title: Editing profile data in online forms
docs.text:
Profiles are collections of default and custom fields. They can be used in online forms to collect information from visitors or to build searchable directories (see "Profiles").

If a standalone profile in an online form is used to search for and edit CiviCRM data—for example, if it is not part of an event registration page—only authenticated users may edit. You can give profile edit to the anonymous role, but visitors who are not logged in still cannot edit unless they have a checksum (a unique URL to one page where they may edit their own data; read "Everyday tasks" in the email section for more information). For checksum tokens to work, anonymous users must have profile edit.

docs.title: Collecting data from anonymous visitors using profiles
docs.text: To collect data from anonymous visitors through profiles in online forms, such as event registration pages, contribution pages and standalone profile forms, give profile create to the "anonymous" role. If the profile contains custom fields, an additional permission is needed depending on the circumstances. See "Accessing custom data" below.

docs.title: Creating searchable directories for the public
docs.text: Profiles can build searchable directories: search criteria that gather results from the database, such as organisations by location. To give a group of users access to search pages published on the website, check profile listings for that role or user group.

docs.title: Profile view
docs.text: When a profile is embedded in an online page—for example, to display an organisation's name, description and contact details from the database—a visitor needs profile view to see it.

docs.title: Using the "Profile listings and forms" permission
docs.text:
Caution

The "Profile listings and forms" permission is equivalent to granting profile_view, profile_create, profile_edit and profile_listing. This is a lot of permission and should be assigned carefully!

Assign this access right only to trusted roles. It grants access to:

  • Add data through profiles in online forms.
  • Edit data displayed in standalone profiles on public pages, if the option is given (for example, contact information).
  • Use public searchable directories.

Where possible, assign each access right separately rather than through this 'allow all actions' permission. "Profile listings and forms" is not enabled for the "anonymous" and "authenticated" roles by default.

If this role were given to anonymous users, a visitor would still need to be logged in or use a checksum token to edit data (see "Everyday tasks" in the section on email).

docs.title: Accessing custom data
docs.text:
If an online form or profile uses custom data fields, users cannot interact with them unless they have permission to view and/or edit custom data. There are two ways to assign access:

  1. Enable access all custom data for roles that need both view and edit access. For example, giving it to the "anonymous" role lets visitors view and edit all custom fields in online forms, including custom fields in a profile incorporated into an event registration page. This is an 'all or nothing' approach.
  2. Create CiviCRM ACLs to give roles access only to specific sets of custom data fields. For example, a team in Amsterdam might access only custom volunteer fields, while a head office in Scotland accesses both custom volunteer and custom donor fields. These ACLs will not function if access all custom data is assigned.

docs.title: Accessing uploaded files
docs.text: Enable access uploaded files for any role that needs to view images, photos and files attached to CiviCRM records and pages. Assign it to the "anonymous" role if visitors should see photos attached to contact records, personal campaign pages, documents intended for public consumption, and similar files.

docs.title: Giving users the ability to view their contact dashboard
docs.text: You can give authenticated (logged-in) users access to a screen where they can review their mailing group subscriptions, contributions, memberships and event registrations, where applicable. Assign access contact dashboard to roles whose users need this feature. Do not enable it for the "anonymous" role.

docs.title: Other CMS Roles
docs.text:
Each CMS has other predefined roles with varying levels of CiviCRM access. You can change their permissions, but always keep one role (Administrator/Super Users/Admin) that can administer CiviCRM, including managing access control.

You may also add roles for more graduated access to CiviCRM functionality.

More information on CiviCRM permissions (access control options), including permissions required for certain back-office functions, is available at http://wiki.civicrm.org/confluence/display/CRMDOC/Default+Permissions+and+Roles.

docs.title: Native CiviCRM ACLs
docs.text:
CiviCRM ACLs provide more granular access to records through contact groups assigned to ACL roles. CMS access controls can turn off visibility of entire CiviCRM sections and determine whether users can view, edit, delete or create data in different areas. They cannot subdivide those rules by record type.

A charity based in Chicago has three regional offices. Its fundraising staff need to create and edit contact records for prospective donors, but each office's fundraising department should access only its local contacts. The CMS (Drupal, Joomla! or WordPress) can grant add contacts to authenticated users. If view all contacts and edit all contacts were also assigned through the CMS, it could not differentiate between the three groups of donors by location. This requires a CiviCRM ACL.

To begin, go to Administer > User and Permissions > Permissions (Access Control). This screen links to the CMS access control list and the three steps for managing native CiviCRM ACLs.

docs.title: Manage Roles
docs.text:
Create ACL roles here. By default, you have "administrator" and "authenticated" (logged in). Only the administrator role can be edited: "authenticated" is a reserved role and core to the system.

Click "Add Acl Role" to create a role using these options:

  • Label: the role's name, visible to users.
  • Description: a description of the role that you can create and format.
  • Weight: a number determining the role's place in the list. For example, "1" places it near the top, while "20" might put it near the bottom; lower numbers appear before higher ones.
  • Enabled?: whether the role is active. Disabling it may cause functionality to stop working for some users.

docs.title: Assign Users to CiviCRM ACL Roles
docs.text:
Once roles are configured, assign them to users in two steps:

  1. Create an access control group for users who should have the same level of access. There are multiple ways to do this, outlined in the chapter "Groups and tags".
  2. Assign the ACL contact group to a role. On the access control menu screen, click "Assign Users to CiviCRM ACL Roles", then "Add Role Assignment". Complete these fields:
    • ACL Role: select an available ACL role.
    • Assigned To: choose a contact group to assign to the role.
    • Enabled?: whether the assignment is active.

docs.title: Manage ACLs
docs.text:
The third step is to create ACLs. For each ACL, decide:

  1. Which role can perform the action?
  2. What is the action or operation—such as view, edit, delete or create?
  3. On which set of data can the action be performed?

Return to the Access Control screen (Administer > User and Permissions > Permissions...) and click "manage ACLs". The list of existing controls will likely include one allowing administrators to edit all contacts in the database. Click "Add ACL" and complete:

  • Description: a clear description of what the ACL does.
  • Role: the role to assign the ACL to, selected from the drop-down list.
  • Operation: the action the role can perform, such as view, edit, create or delete.
  • Type of Data: the data type the operation relates to:
    • A group of contacts
    • A profile
    • A set of custom data fields
    • Events
  • Group/Profile/Custom Data/Event: this field's label depends on Type of Data. Select the specific group of contacts, profile, custom data or event for the ACL.
  • Enabled?: whether the ACL is active.

docs.title: Permissions and access control
docs.text:
Permissions and the related concept of access control lists (ACLs) are collections of rules that define access to areas of the system. You create roles for your site, give those roles permissions to do certain things, and assign the roles to people.

Permissions and ACLs allow you to grant access to:

  • Different areas of CiviCRM, such as CiviContribute, CiviCase and CiviMail, according to the tasks a user is responsible for.
  • Entities within the system, such as contacts and contributions, and ways to interact with them, such as viewing, editing and deleting.

Permissions define who can see and do what on your site. From a security perspective, it is important to understand them before checking a permissions box: badly configured permissions may inadvertently expose your contacts' data.

docs.title: The difference between CMS permissions and CiviCRM ACLs
docs.text:
Permissions and ACLs are defined in two places: the content management system (CMS) and CiviCRM itself. Many organisations can meet their needs with CMS permissions alone. Others need CiviCRM ACLs for more fine-grained access control.

CMS permissions grant or deny user roles access to entire sections of CiviCRM, such as CiviMail and CiviEvent. They also restrict whether users can view, edit, add and delete records such as contacts, events and contributions. This is an 'all or nothing' approach: for instance, you cannot differentiate between contacts in different groups.

Native CiviCRM ACLs offer finer-grained control. For example, you can limit access to view, edit, create, delete and search to:

  • groups of contacts
  • a profile (a collection of existing and/or custom fields; see "Profiles")
  • a set of custom fields
  • events (for example, a user may access one event but not others)

As a general rule, start with CMS permissions. If they cannot meet your needs, consider CiviCRM ACLs for more granular access rights.

These examples show when to use CiviCRM ACLs instead of access controls in Drupal, Joomla! or WordPress:

  1. An organisation has a head office and three regional offices. The event director at the central office must be able to view all events, while coordinators at each regional office should only view and edit their own events. A CMS access control list can restrict viewing, editing, adding or deleting all events or no events, but cannot distinguish events by office. A CiviCRM ACL is needed.
  2. A team in Paris manages volunteers using one set of custom fields, while a team in London collects donor information in another set. Each team should access only its own set. A CMS access control list could grant access to all custom information or none of it. In this case, disable any CMS rule controlling access to custom fields and use a CiviCRM ACL instead.

docs.title: Scheduled jobs
docs.text: CiviCRM relies on a number of scheduled jobs that run automatically on a regular basis. These jobs keep data up-to-date and perform other important tasks. For example, there is a job which sends scheduled reminders, a job which checks for CiviCRM software updates, and many other jobs too.

docs.title: How scheduled jobs are initiated
docs.text: An important characteristic of scheduled jobs is that they run automatically. However, CiviCRM (like most other web-based applications) actually can't initiate actions itself — it can only respond to actions that other systems initiate. For most of CiviCRM's functionality, it relies on people to initiate those actions. For example, when a person submits a form, CiviCRM creates a new contact record. Because scheduled jobs must run automatically, CiviCRM relies on a piece of external software called "cron" to initiate them.

docs.title: Understanding cron
docs.text:
"Cron" is a piece of software, separate from CiviCRM, which is typically installed on server systems to initiate tasks automatically. Here are some important points to understand about cron, as you configure your CiviCRM scheduled jobs:

  • Cron must be setup to initiate CiviCRM's scheduled jobs before those scheduled jobs will run automatically. That setup is outside the scope of this User Guide because it involves "system" level tasks that you can't do from within the CiviCRM user interface.

    Cron setup

    To setup cron, refer to the Cron setup page in the System Administrator Guide.

  • Cron can be configured in different ways.

    • Your system administrator will typically configure cron to run on a regular interval with a frequency between 5 and 60 minutes. Each time cron "runs", cron tells CiviCRM to execute whatever scheduled jobs CiviCRM deems necessary at that time. This means that the granularity available to configure specific scheduled jobs is limited by the cron job frequency. For example, if cron only runs once every day, then it will not be possible for a scheduled job to run every hour. So it's best to have your system administrator configure cron to run frequently enough to meet your needs.

    • Alternatively, system administrators can configure separate cron jobs to run specific CiviCRM scheduled jobs, although this type of setup is less common.

    • From within the CiviCRM user interface, there is no way to see how cron is configured.

docs.title: Configuring scheduled jobs
docs.text: To configure scheduled jobs, go to Administer > System Settings > Scheduled Jobs.

docs.title: Scheduled jobs vs API calls
docs.text:
CiviCRM has a subsystem called the "API" which allows developers and integrators to perform all sorts of useful tasks. (You can read the full API docs in the Developer Guide.) CiviCRM users typically don't need to understand anything about the API, but when interacting with scheduled jobs, some understanding is helpful.

An "API call" is basically an instruction for CiviCRM to do something. For example, the ContributionPage.create API call will create a new contribution page — and the person constructing the API call can add parameters to it in order to specify characteristics of that newly created contribution page, like its title and financial type. Each API call has an "entity" (ContributionPage in the above example), and an "action" (create in the above example).

A scheduled job is the combination of an API call and a schedule (e.g. "hourly"). When you add a new scheduled job, you can specify any API call. So, you could for example, use scheduled jobs to automatically create a new contribution page every day. Of course this example is not very useful. What makes scheduled jobs useful is the fact that the CiviCRM API provides many actions that site maintainers will commonly wish to perform on a regular schedule. For example, the API call Job.send_reminder will send scheduled reminders.

docs.title: Default scheduled jobs
docs.text:
A fresh install of CiviCRM comes with over a dozen scheduled jobs already partially configured. These "default" scheduled jobs offer a starting point for you to configure your own scheduled jobs. If you like, you can rename them or delete them. Then later on, you can refer to the specific jobs section of this page for all the necessary details to re-create any of these default scheduled jobs (and other jobs too).

Parameters needed

Some of the default scheduled jobs require parameters to be configured before they can run properly.

docs.title: Job frequency
docs.text:
Some jobs need to be run very frequently, for example the email send task should typically be run once every 5 or 10 minutes. Others need to be run less frequency, for example the membership update script can easily be run just once a day.

When adding or editing a scheduled job you can select a "Run frequency" as follows:

  • Yearly
  • Quarterly
  • Monthly
  • Weekly
  • Daily
  • Hourly
  • Every time cron job is run

Note

As described in the cron section above, your system administrator will need to configure cron to run at a specified interval. Every 5 minutes is a common frequency, but from within the CiviCRM user interface it's impossible to determine cron's schedule. Scheduled jobs cannot run more frequently than cron. So if cron is set to run weekly, then choosing the "daily" setting for a scheduled job will mean that it only gets run weekly.

docs.title: Job timing
docs.text:
Let's pretend you want to schedule a job to run monthly, but it's also important to you that the job be run on the 15th day of each month. Unfortunately the scheduled jobs system system does not allow you this level of control. When you set a job to run monthly, it will continue to run one month after the first time it is run.

If you need more control over your job timing, you can create separate cron jobs to execute specific CiviCRM API calls.

docs.title: Command parameters
docs.text:
When editing a scheduled job, CiviCRM gives you a "command parameters" field where you can specify input parameters which affect the way the job runs. Each job has its own parameters, and some jobs don't accept any parameters. The parameters for each job are documented in detail within the specific jobs section below.

Example

Let's look at an example of how you use these parameters to fill out the "command parameters" field...

The Job.mail_report job documents the following parameters:

  • instanceId (required): ID of report instance to send
  • format (optional)
    • pdf (default)
    • csv to output the report as a CSV file instead of default PDF format
    • print output the report as printer-friendly HTML
  • sendmail (optional):
    • 1 send email
    • 0 don't email the report. Use this in combination with print or csv format to write report to stdout so you can save it to a disk file.

So for example, you might choose to fill out the "command parameters" field as follows:

instanceId=7
format=csv

As you can see in the example above, you'll need to use the following process to fill out the "command parameters" field:

  • Use one parameter per line
  • Use an equals sign = between the parameter and its value
  • Don't use any spaces
  • Don't use any quotes

docs.title: Manually executing a scheduled job
docs.text: You can also run scheduled jobs on a one-off basis by clicking the More > Execute Now link for the given job on the Scheduled Jobs page. This is useful for some of the scheduled jobs that are designed to be run less frequently, including the geo-coding job and the greetings and addressees job.

docs.title: Viewing the job log
docs.text:
From the Scheduled Jobs screen, you can click View Log (all jobs) or View Job Log for a specific scheduled job. Viewing this log is useful for troubleshooting purposes. You can make sure the jobs are running and examine any errors that the jobs output.

Note

The log displays separate entries for the time when a job begins and the time when it finishes. You can examine the time difference between these entries to see how long the job took to complete. Error messages are only displayed in the log entry for the job completion.

docs.title: Job.cleanup
docs.text:
Removes temporary data and files, and clears old data from cache tables. Recommend running this job every hour to help prevent database and file system bloat.

  • Name of scheduled job created by default: Clean-up Temporary Data and Files
  • Recommended frequency: hourly
  • Parameters:
    • session (optional)
      • 1 (default) clean up session cache
      • 0 skip
    • tempTables (optional)
      • 1 (default) clean up tempTables cache
      • 0 skip

Multisite installs

docs.text:
Retrieves geocodes (lat and long) and / or parses street addresses (populates street number, street name, etc.)

Note

Geocoding provider must be configured (Administer > System Settings > Mapping and Geocoding). Street Address Parsing must be enabled (Administer > Localization > Address Settings).

docs.title: Job.group_cache_flush
docs.text:
This job purges aged smart group cache data (based on the timeout value). Sites can decide whether they want this job and / or the group cache rebuild job to run. Generally performance is better when old caches are cleared out prior to any attempt to rebuild them (whether on demand or otherwise).

  • Name of scheduled job created by default: (none)
  • Recommended frequency: always
  • Parameters: (none)

docs.title: Job.group_rebuild
docs.text:
Rebuilds the smart group cache. This builds the cache for any smart groups for whom it is empty. If you do not run this it will build groups on demand. Building on demand is more efficient except for 2 operations; viewing the count on manage groups page for all groups and being able to expand the smart groups tab on an individual contact record. If these are important to you then enable this job but expect it to have performance impacts unless you have only a few small smart groups.

Note

You can disable the ability to expand the smart group tab on the contact record and this is recommended for medium sized site (e.g 50k contacts) and larger.

  • Name of scheduled job created by default: Rebuild Smart Group Cache
  • Recommended frequency: never
  • Parameters:
    • limit (optional): specify a number to limit the number of smart groups that will be rebuilt

docs.title: Job.mail_report
docs.text:

    • sendmail (optional):
