They are now able to identify newsletter subscribers and send the newsletter to them via CiviCRM. They couldn't be happier!

The AFSC currently has nine CiviCRM sites and the IT Department is now recommending CiviCRM as the "database of choice" for all of its offices. Support from the CiviCRM community is excellent and CiviCRM itself is improving every day, as more and more functionality is being added. AFSC staff are now able to access their data from any place that has internet access, run complex searches, manage online event registrations and send online newsletters and postal mailings. CiviCRM has enabled them to better manage their constituents. This makes their life easier and in turn, is of great benefit to AFSC.

docs.title: A CRM education
docs.text:
]

Schoolhouse Supplies (SHS) is a Portland, Oregon, USA-based non-profit organisation which gathers and distributes school supplies to students and teachers.

Prior to implementing CiviCRM, SHS used a combination of software programmes including Exceed, EROI, Constant Contact, Salesforce, Auction Pay (for online contributions) and, of course, hundreds of spreadsheets. In addition, SHS had a custom web application for managing its online store inventory and processing in-kind donations.

docs.title: What they did
docs.text:
By moving to CiviCRM, SHS has centralised their operations and the management of all their constituent data, and been able to unify and coordinate several of their core business processes.

All data from each source has been migrated to CiviCRM Standalone (an installation that is not integrated with either Drupal or Joomla! CMS). CiviContact and CiviContribute have replaced Exceed and Auction Pay. CiviMail has replaced EROI and Constant Contact. Salesforce data was moved into CiviCRM and the custom e-commerce application it supported was integrated with CiviCRM. Lastly, the inventory and in-kind management system was integrated with CiviCRM. Spreadsheets have been imported.

docs.title: The results
docs.text: Each business process at SHS can now take advantage of their full constituent database and business activities are easily coordinated. More importantly, SHS is now in the process of taking manual business processes (such as volunteer coordination) and moving them to CiviCRM. New campaigns are now being planned and executed which would previously have been impossible or prohibitively expensive.

docs.title: Growing satisfaction
docs.text:
The New York State Nursery Landscape Association (NYSNLA) is a member-based association providing resources and advocacy support for nursery and landscape professionals throughout New York State. The organisation seeks to advance the interests of New York State's nursery and landscape businesses and professionals by promoting sound business practices, expanding state and local markets, and exercising leadership in the development of sustainable communities.

Prior to migrating to CiviCRM the Association went through several iterations of member-management solutions, beginning with a series of spreadsheet documents and later moving to a Microsoft Access database. The move to CiviCRM was prompted by the desire to consolidate data, provide members real-time access to contact details, and to create a searchable member directory to website visitors who may be looking for a nursery or landscape professional.

docs.title: What they did
docs.text:
Working with a CiviCRM consultant, NYSNLA began the process of analysing the structure and content of their existing database and mapping the various functions to CiviCRM structures. They determined that they would use CiviMember, CiviEvent, CiviContribute, and CiviMail to address their core database needs, and would consider using CiviPledge at some point in the future for soliciting contributions to their associated non-profit, the Nurserymen's Foundation.

One data area that required particular attention was their Certified Nursery Landscape Professional program (CNLP). CNLP is an intensive, on-going educational programme designed to increase the skills of garden and landscape employees. The programme was designed by members of the nursery and landscape industry with assistance from Cornell University. Interested individuals must apply to the programme and successfully pass a test. Certification lasts two years, after which time the individual must recertify.

NYSNLA used CiviCRM's membership functionality to track the status of CNLPs. The ability to define a rolling-period membership and to gauge when they are nearing expiration perfectly met their management needs. The initial application process, which also must be carefully tracked, was handled through CiviEvent, as an application to the programme is essentially a registration to attend one of the bi-annual test events.

The Association also took advantage of CiviCRM's open source platform to make some interface customisations that improved the way they view contact records. Because of the importance of the CNLP programme, they wanted to be able to look at all employees for a certain nursery/landscape company and quickly know if any of them are CNLPs or Lifetime CNLPs. They also needed to easily find out which employees are authorised to manage the company's records.

docs.title: The results
docs.text: The Association has worked hard to communicate to the public the importance of using a qualified landscape professional. Essential to this effort was the inclusion of a searchable member directory on their website. Using CiviCRM, they were able to create a search page that included geographic segmentation (the Association divides members into 8 regions state-wide) and a list of services provided by members (using CiviCRM's tags feature). The resulting search tool, because it is directly connected with their contact data, ensures website visitors are always looking at current information. The Association is also able to provide members direct access to their own contact details so they can update and maintain their list of services provided and other information.

docs.title: Campaigning for efficiency
docs.text:
The Green Party has been the third largest party in New Zealand politics for most of the last decade, with strong roots in the Values Party (the world's first national Green party) of the early 1970s. They achieved parliamentary representation in 1996 and after the 2008 election had 9 Members of Parliament, 5,000 financial members and some 50,000 contacts. The Party has more than 50 branches around the country and contest elections across all 67 electorates in the last election.

Prior to adopting CiviCRM, the Party and its parliamentary units employed a range of systems for managing members, donations, contacts, campaigning, media and advocacy.

The Green Party policy states:

  • Development of IT must be socially responsible and sustainable.
  • The use of free and open source software should be encouraged.

docs.title: What they did
docs.text:
CiviCRM was adopted by the Party in 2007 (version 1.7), with a switch to Drupal as a parallel project. This was inspired in part by work done by the Canadian Greens on developing a voter canvassing module for Drupal. A Party database was set up using CiviCRM and online donations, memberships and event registrations were instigated.

The Greens have over 100 different issues that they generate media releases about. These were reconstructed as a check-box custom data field, and Smart Groups were built for each of these, for use when sending out media releases via CiviMail.

The highly complex access control requirements of the party necessitated the development of an alternative approach to the use of ACLs (Access Control Lists) in order to provide a more easily managed, highly granular system. This approach has now been incorporated as a hook (something that can be utilised by developers to extend CiviCRM) into the core code.

For the 2008 election campaign, a look-up function was developed so that when new contacts were added to the database, addresses were checked against a table containing the Electoral Roll, and links were created where matches were made. "Soft" matches were also recorded.

docs.title: The results
docs.text:
In the 2008 election campaign, the Party made extensive use of online fundraising and greatly exceeded previous online income. Membership renewal has been streamlined with more online renewals occurring.

As of May 2009, the Party was still using CiviCRM v2.0 on Drupal 5 and therefore had not yet benefited from the many features that became available through the 2.1 and 2.2 releases. An upgrade was in progress at the time.

In a complex organisation such as the Green Party, training can be a limiting factor, as well as the need to nurture more in-house super-users. New features in CiviCRM have led to some rethinking about the Party's usage of custom data fields, particularly with regard to the use of CiviMail for media releases. New options for both nested groups and Drupal Organic Groups suggest that a more time effective approach may soon be possible.

docs.title: Quest for success
docs.text: QuestBridge is dedicated to helping bright, motivated low-income high school students get accepted to and able to pay for college. QuestBridge recruits high school juniors throughout the USA and invites them to fill out the QuestBridge application online. QuestBridge also partners with the USA's most selective colleges and universities with the aim to increase the socio-economic diversity of their student bodies. QuestBridge's college partners accept the QuestBridge application in lieu of their own admissions application.

docs.title: What they did
docs.text: QuestBridge has built most of its business processes around CiviCRM. They wrote their online admission application using CiviCRM and extended it using the PHP scripting language. CiviCRM is used to store biographical and application information and communication histories about the students.

docs.title: The results
docs.text:
In the 2008-9 school year, QuestBridge helped more than 1200 students get accepted and pay for college at its 25 partner schools. They accomplished their goals in a very efficient manner, in part thanks to their effective implementation of CiviCRM. QuestBridge is currently planning to upgrade to the latest version of CiviCRM in order to take full advantage of the new email features.

If Questbridge were to start over they would have invested more in training on CiviCRM up-front.

docs.title: Changing with the times
docs.text: The San Francisco School (SFS), is a Preschool through 8th grade coeducational school with a diverse student body of about 270 students. Like all schools, communication between the school and families is very important. Whether it's updating a home phone number, email address or allergy, it is essential in meeting the needs of the students. The head of school was a strong supporter of the project from the beginning which led the staff and parents to be able to make a strong commitment to help the project move forward.

docs.title: What they did
docs.text:
They used CiviCRM to create a Parent Portal to:

  • required parents to log in to view their contact information and their child's school information
  • had an automated system to schedule parent teacher conferences
  • used a computer to record after school class sign in and sign out
  • managed after school class registration (example: music, cooking, sports) and view their child's after school fees

To ease the transition of the school community, each of the above features were shown gradually rather than all at the same time.

docs.title: The results
docs.text: Enabling parents/guardians to view their contact information meant that they could confirm what the school sees and hence notify the school of any changes. Also, they could view their child's after school fees and view a record of what classes their child is signed up for. Online sign ups allow parents the flexibility to schedule parent/teacher conferences and after school classes on their own time. Changing the existing school systems to an online system allowed both parents and staff to work together, view the Parent Portal so that contact information is current, parent teacher conferences are scheduled in a timely manner, and that access to the information is widely accessible.

docs.title: What is CiviCRM?
docs.text:
CiviCRM is a web-based constituent relationship management (CRM) system built by and for nonprofit organizations and NGOs. It helps organizations record and manage information about the people and organizations they interact with. More than an address book, it brings donations, events, memberships, activities, cases, campaigns, mailings, and other interactions into a single system that integrates with open source content management systems (CMS).

CiviCRM focuses on the needs of nonprofits, NGOs, and civic sector organizations, supporting communications, community engagement, activism, outreach, and donor management.

As of 2019, over 11,000 non-profits use CiviCRM. CiviCRM currently manages over 303,000,000 contacts, 265,000,000 donations, and 42,000,000 event registrations.

CiviCRM is Free/Open Source software. There are no license costs or user fees for downloading, installing, or using it. You can view and modify its source code and distribute copies of the original source to any person or organization.

Because CiviCRM is web-based, many users can access it at the same time from different locations. It was developed with the international community in mind and supports translations and multi-language options.

docs.title: Thinking of CiviCRM as an address book
docs.text:
One way to understand a CRM is to imagine a personal address book with more capabilities. Each time you call someone, it could record the call and a brief description of the conversation. It could decide whether to ask that person for a particular favor based on whether they did it for you a week ago, then schedule a follow-up meeting. Later, you could ask, “What were my interactions with Ji Lao?” or “How many people helped me this month?” and see the history.

Now imagine organizing a dinner party for everyone you met during the previous year. You could write an invitation and have your address book email it. It could handle guests’ RSVPs, record who is vegetarian, and tell you two nights before the event how many people to expect.

Organizations need this kind of help even more. Meetings, phone calls, and other contact can be hard to remember over time. Knowing more about the people and organizations you interact with helps you target messages to groups interested in particular topics, observe their reactions, and adjust future interactions.

docs.title: What CiviCRM can do
docs.text:
CiviCRM is modular. In the simplest set-up, you can:

  • Record basic contact information, such as name, home or postal address, email address, and phone number.
  • Define relationships between your contacts.
  • Send emails.
  • Keep a record of your interactions with your contacts.

Components and extensions let you do more, such as sign up members for your organization, take event registrations, receive donations, or distribute grants. See the Components and Extensions chapters for more information.

docs.title: Working with a website
docs.text:
CiviCRM works with a content management system (CMS), a tool for creating and managing websites. Most websites these days are based on a CMS.

CiviCRM integrates with Backdrop, Drupal, Joomla and WordPress. Through this integration, website visitors can renew their membership, sign up for events, request email updates, and donate money. You can also share parts of your CRM data, such as event information, with website visitors. Read more in the Website Integration section.

docs.title: Who is CiviCRM?
docs.text:
CiviCRM has a diverse community centred on developing, using, and documenting the software. It includes the CiviCRM core team; people at non-profits that use CiviCRM; consultants working with non-profit organizations; programmers and developers; power users; volunteers; and community organizers. The community is also closely related to many other open source projects.

People interact with CiviCRM in different ways, improving both the software and how the community organizes itself. This diversity, and the ease with which someone can join, helps the community keep changing and improving, sometimes in unexpected ways.

Your place in the community grows through your interactions. Treat others well, have some fun, and help others, and you can find the community rewarding. Complaining, using a disrespectful tone, or treating the community only as a resource rather than as a group of generous and knowledgeable people is unlikely to get much of a response.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
CiviCRM started in 2004 by Dave Greenberg, Donald Lobo and Michal Mach. The founders had a lot of previous experience working with non-profit organizations and tools. The group was influenced very early by Zack Rosen and Neil Drumm, who convinced them to use Drupal as a fundamental cornerstone for CiviCRM. This decision has meant that the developers have been able to leverage a lot of the functionality that Drupal provides, freeing the team up to focus on building the features necessary to make a great CRM.

In 2005 the first version of CiviCRM was released with two of the core modules in place: CiviMail and CiviContribute (you can read more about these later). Since those early days CiviCRM has become the leading open source CRM for nonprofits. It has built a large community of users and contributors (as of early 2019, there were over 11,000 installed sites), has added more components to the software (there are now 8 core modules and additional third party components), and has broadened its integration with other popular CMS's including Backdrop, Joomla! and WordPress.

CiviCRM includes a large ecosystem of free software contributors around the project and high-profile non-profit organisations such as Amnesty International, Creative Commons, Electronic Frontier Foundation, Free Software Foundation, and Wikimedia Foundation use CiviCRM.

Currently, CiviCRM operates using a group based structure focused on various aspects of the project including development, maintenance, marketing, etc. CiviCRM continues to be coordinated by a Core Team.

docs.title: It's good to talk
docs.text:
CiviCRM is an open, learning community where people are ready to hear your ideas. If you have an idea, nothing stops you from carrying it out, but talking about it is a good place to start.

If you are unsure where to begin, try CiviCRM's Mattermost, which offers live discussion in chat rooms and direct messages. Ask what others think. Someone may have tried something similar before, and collaboration is a guiding philosophy of the community.

Depending on your idea, people may direct you to a next step: an article on the blog (http://civicrm.org/blog/), CiviCRM's GitLab, a teleconference, or an in-person meeting with another community member.

docs.title: Be the change
docs.text: An idea needs an action plan and someone to implement it. The CiviCRM community is friendly and supportive, and people will want to be involved and kept up to date, but you will need to drive your project. Consider how to gather resources and fit the work around your day job. Finding a way to meet your own objectives while benefiting the CiviCRM community can help you get things done.

docs.title: And finally...
docs.text: If you use CiviCRM and have an ongoing relationship with a consultant, you can still be an active community member. The community benefits from direct feedback from end users. Your consultant is one person or organization; asking on the forums opens your question to help and input from the wider community.

docs.title: Cancelling and expiring memberships
docs.text:
If a contact resigns or cancels their membership, change its status to Cancelled or another status that is not considered current rather than deleting it. This retains the contact's membership history and any contribution records attached to the membership.

If a contact's membership is in a grace period and you know they will not continue for another period, you can manually change its status to Expired rather than Cancelled, since they completed the membership period.

To cancel or manually expire a membership:

  1. Search for the contact, click the Membership tab, then click Edit next to the membership record.
  2. On the membership edit screen, check the Status Override box and select the appropriate Membership Status, such as Cancelled or Expired.

Manually expiring memberships may not be necessary. Depending on how the membership status rules are set up under Administer > CiviMember > Membership Status Rules, memberships automatically expire based on timeline criteria.

docs.title: Deleting memberships
docs.text:
Delete a membership only if it was entered in error. For example, if you made Jo Smith a member instead of Joe Smith, you would remove Jo Smith's incorrect membership and any linked contribution record.

Deleting a membership completely removes it and any linked contributions from the database. This action cannot be undone, so give permission to delete memberships only to trusted staff.

You can delete membership records in either of these ways:

  • Search for the contact, click the Membership tab, click More next to the membership record, then click Delete.
  • Click Memberships > Find Members >, enter your criteria, then select the membership records from the "Find Members" results screen and click Delete.

docs.title: Membership status rules
docs.text: Membership status rules define the stages contacts move through during their membership. The rules use the membership's join, start, or end date.

docs.title: Membership dates
docs.text:
Memberships have three primary dates:

  • Join date: The date the contact first signed up for a membership with your organisation. Unless changed manually, it retains that first value.
  • Start date: The date the current continuous period of membership began.
  • End date: The last day of the current membership.

docs.title: Default membership statuses
docs.text:
By default, members move through these statuses:

  • Pending: Someone has requested membership but has not paid. You cannot change this status manually to New; you must update the associated contribution record. For example, if Joe Smith signs up using the pay later option, his membership status will not change to New until you change the contribution status of his related payment to Completed.
  • New: The member has just signed up, or a pending payment has arrived. By default, this status lasts until three months after the membership start date.
  • Current: New members move to this status after the New period. Current lasts until the membership end date.
  • Grace: The membership period has ended without a renewal. The contact remains in this status for a period of time and is still counted as a member.
  • Expired: The grace period has ended, and the contact is no longer counted as a member.
  • Cancelled: An administrator has manually cancelled the membership, perhaps due to misbehaviour.
  • Deceased: The deceased contact's record remains in the system, but the contact is removed from further communications. This status is set automatically from the contact's deceased flag.

docs.title: How rules and overrides determine a status
docs.text:
You can force a status by selecting membership override on a membership record and choosing a status. A membership with an override stays at that status rather than being updated according to the status rules.

Go to Administer > CiviMember > Membership Status Rules to see a summary of the existing rules.

CiviCRM checks for a status override first. If there is none, it checks the statuses in order from the top of the Status Rules page. For each status, it checks whether today's date falls between that status's start and end dates. It applies the first matching status.

docs.title: Adding or editing a status
docs.text:
When you edit or add a membership status, this form appears:

You can add statuses and edit existing statuses, except Pending and Deceased. For a new status, specify when it starts and stops relative to a membership event: the join date, start date, or end date. For example, 'one month after the membership start date' would use 'start date' and '1 month'; 'five days before the membership end date' would use 'end date' and '-5 days'.

Use the 'Current membership' tick box to specify whether contacts with the status are considered members. This produces Yes or No in the Member column of the status rules summary page.

For renewing contacts whose status defines them as members, the existing membership end date is extended by the duration of the renewal. Renewing contacts whose status defines them as non-members receive a new start date and an end date based on that start date.

docs.title: Keeping membership statuses updated
docs.text:
When a membership is added or renewed, its status is set automatically from the status rules. For example, a newly created membership is assigned "New" by default.

If statuses are not updating automatically, make sure the Update Membership Statuses scheduled job is enabled and runs at least once a day. See the Scheduled Jobs chapter for configuration details, and consult your system administrator if appropriate.

docs.title: Defining membership types
docs.text:
Membership types are a basic building block for membership management in CiviCRM. An organisation will typically set up a type for each membership it offers. One type may be enough for a simple membership structure; a more complex structure may need more. For example, an organisation might have 'regular', 'student', and 'honorary' memberships, or use membership types as subscriptions to free or paid publications.

The options on the membership type form can help you decide how many types your organisation needs and how to configure them. This page covers the most common set-up. Organisations with more complex requirements may need membership price sets, which are covered in Membership price sets.

If you have trouble modelling your membership structure in CiviCRM, ask about the problem on Mattermost or Stack Exchange (see Finding the Community Online). There may be other ways to model your data or simple changes you can make to CiviCRM's behaviour.

docs.title: Membership type options
docs.text:
To open the membership type form:

  1. Go to Administer > CiviMember > Membership Types.
  2. Select Add Membership Type.

  • Name: The name appears on public and backend pages, so choose one appropriate for both audiences. You can change it later, although you may also need to update membership receipts if they have been customised based on membership names.

  • Description: This is optional. You can describe the membership and the types of contacts it is aimed at.

  • Membership organisation: Specify the organisation that the contact will become a member of. CiviCRM can manage memberships for more than one organisation in a single instance—for example, the memberships of a tennis club, a football club, and a hockey club. Each organisation must already exist as a CiviCRM organisation contact. If you manage memberships for only your own organisation, you can choose the default organisation.

    Some organisations want contacts to hold two or more concurrent memberships of the same organisation. For example, an organisation focused on child health might offer parents a membership that includes a parenting magazine and health professionals a membership that includes a peer-reviewed journal and training-event discounts. A parent who is also a health professional might want both.

    CiviCRM's Membership Up-Sell feature expects a contact to have only one active membership with a single organization at any given time. A 'workaround' is to create 'dummy' organisations for the possible concurrent memberships. In the example above, you would create an extra organisation for health professionals. You do not have to expose the dummy organisation to members on the website; it is for administrative purposes only.

  • Minimum fee: Enter 0 (zero) for a free membership. Otherwise, enter the minimum amount that must be paid for this membership type. It is a minimum because you can encourage people to pay more if they want to.

  • Financial type: The default financial type is Member Dues, which is appropriate for many organisations. For more complex accounting needs, you can specify different financial types to account for membership payments in different ways. For finer-grained control, you can use Membership Price Sets.

    You can override the financial type on specific public membership sign-up pages or when recording a membership in the back end.

    CiviCRM handles paid memberships by linking membership records to contribution records. The membership record documents a contact's relationship with the organisation; the corresponding financial transaction records the membership's monetary value.

    The membership record is stored under the membership tab, the financial record under the Contributions tab, and a link is created between them.

  • Auto-renew: Auto-renew automatically submits a repeat transaction to the payment processor when the current membership expires. It is not available for all payment processors, so check whether yours is configured for recurring payments before selecting an auto-renew option. For information on payment processors, see http://wiki.civicrm.org/confluence/display/CRMDOC/Payment+Processors.

    You can offer or require auto-renewal, but only for memberships with a Duration of one year or less. Free memberships never auto-renew because auto-renewal relies on confirmation from a payment processor. For similar functionality, you can set a free membership's Duration to Lifetime and use a scheduled reminder to email those members, for example, annually.

  • Duration: Enter the number of days, months, or years that the membership lasts each time someone signs up or renews.

  • Period type: Rolling memberships start on the day the member signs up. Fixed memberships start on the calendar date you specify. Selecting a fixed period displays additional fields according to the Duration.

    For a Duration in years, two additional fields appear:

    • Fixed Period Start Date is the calendar date on which all memberships start, such as January 1st or April 15th.
    • Fixed Period Rollover Date determines the end date when someone signs up partway through the membership year. For a one-year membership with a Fixed Period Start Date of January 1 and a Fixed Period Rollover Date of September 1:
      • Someone signing up between 1 January 2018 and 31 August 2018 has a membership end date of 31 December 2018.
      • Someone signing up on or after 1 September 2018 has a membership end date of 31 December 2019—up to 15 months of membership for the one-year price.

    For a Duration in months, one additional field appears:

    • Fixed Period Rollover Date determines whether the membership duration starts at the beginning of the current calendar month or the next one. For a six-month membership with Fixed Period Rollover Date set to 15:
      • Someone signing up on days 1–14 January has a membership end date of 30 June.
      • Someone signing up on days 15–31 January has a membership end date of 31 July.

    For example, if Duration = 12 months, Period type = Fixed, and Fixed Period Rollover Date = 1, anyone joining during August 2018 has an expiry date of 31 August 2019.

  • Relationship Type: A membership can be inherited from one contact to another. For example, a professional trade organisation might sign up a company as the primary member and extend membership benefits to its employees.

    Select the relationship type along which the membership inherits. The pop-up help screen gives examples of relationship types to select. Then enter a number in Max related to limit the inherited memberships linked to each primary member. In the company example, you could limit membership through employment to 10 employees.

    With inherited memberships, the primary member is distinguished from the members who inherit membership through their relationship with that member.

  • Visibility: Choose Public to make the membership type available for inclusion on online membership sign-up forms. Choose Admin for types handled manually by an administrator, such as honorary and lifetime memberships.

  • Order: Determines where the type appears in a drop-down list of membership types and on membership sign-up pages.

  • Enabled: Untick this box for a membership type that is no longer offered or not yet available. This removes the type from the user interface without deleting membership data. You can re-enable it later.

docs.title: Collecting additional information about members
docs.text: You can create one or more custom field sets to collect additional information about members. A set can apply to all memberships or to specific membership types. If the information varies by type, create more than one set and link each to the relevant membership type or types. See Creating Custom Fields for details.

docs.title: Finding and viewing memberships
docs.text: You can view recent memberships on the membership dashboard, view an individual contact's membership records, or search based on membership data.

docs.title: The membership dashboard
docs.text:
For a snapshot of recent memberships, go to Memberships > Dashboard. The dashboard shows a summary of memberships by type and date range, and a list of recent member activity.

Click a summary number to view a list of members who have joined or renewed over the last two months or the year-to-date, or who are considered current according to the membership status definitions. From the list, you can take actions such as Delete, Edit, Export, and Send Email to Contacts.

docs.title: Viewing a contact's membership records
docs.text:
Find the contact you want to manage, then click the Membership tab to view a summary of their membership records.

Note

If a contact's membership is "pending", the membership will show up when the tab is clicked but it will NOT be counted in the number on the tab.

Membership records appear with active memberships (those with a current status) first, followed by expired or canceled memberships.

You can edit existing membership records, renew a membership, or create a new membership record. If you have configured an online credit card payment processor for use in CiviCRM, you will see two options for creating or renewing a membership: one for handling an offline record (no real-time transaction taking place), and one for handling an online record (using a real-time credit card transaction). The online option can also be used to set up auto-renew if the processor supports this. The interfaces are similar, except that the credit card option includes payment processing and recording options.

If you are viewing the primary member contact record for a membership type that has inherited membership, you will see a list of the contacts who have inherited the membership.

In this case, a maximum of two inherited memberships are allowed for people who are employees of the primary membership organisation. If an available inherited membership is assigned to the wrong employee, click Delete for that contact. This frees up an inherited membership to assign by selecting Create.

docs.title: Searching based on membership data
docs.text:
CiviCRM distinguishes between contacts and memberships. For example, “How many members do we have?” could mean “How many contacts are members?” or “How many memberships have we granted to contacts?” If one contact has more than one membership, the counts differ: there are two memberships but one contact. Which count to use depends on what you need to know.

Find members searches based on membership data and returns membership data:

  1. Click Memberships > Find Members and enter your criteria.
  2. Click Search.

Advanced search can search based on limited membership information combined with other contact information and return contacts. You can also choose membership from the Display Results As column to show members rather than contacts. For more information, see the Searching chapter.

  1. Click Search > Advanced Search.
  2. In the Display Settings For Results accordion, set Display Results As to Memberships and enter your criteria.
  3. Click Search.

The search results show some membership details. To take further action on all results or a smaller subset of selected records, use the Actions dropdown menu. Actions include Email - send now and Export members.

docs.title: Sending email to members
docs.text:
After searching your records, you can email selected contacts and include data field tokens to personalize the message.

  1. Click Memberships > Find Members and enter your criteria.
  2. On the "Find Members" search results screen, select the records you want to import.
  3. In the -actions- drop down, select Send Email to Contacts.

docs.title: Making member-only websites
docs.text:
CiviMember can be used with your CMS to create a members-only section of your website. Each CMS has its own integration module(s) that can be used to do this.

In a typical workflow, a contact creates an account on your site and becomes a member of your organisation using a CiviMember membership sign up page. When they log in to your site, they get access to member-only content. This content could come from your CMS or from your CRM—for example, a detailed members directory or a list of private events that are only available to members.

For more information, see the section on your CMS in the Integration chapter of the System Adminstrator Guide, or ask questions in the CiviCRM Community.

docs.title: Importing memberships
docs.text:
Use Importing Memberships for a large set of membership records from outside CiviCRM or to update large numbers of existing memberships with new information.

See also

The Importing Data page explains the import process generally and has a section specifically on importing memberships.

Before importing:

  • Contact records must exist. If the contacts are not yet in CiviCRM, first import the Contact data. Make sure it has an External ID that you can include with the membership data to associate the records. For existing contacts, use the Internal Contact ID or the fields from your Unsupervised Duplicate Matching Rule to associate the membership data with the correct contact.
  • The membership import file MUST contain both Membership Type and Start Date. Membership types must exactly match those set up by your CiviCRM Administrator, and the start date must use the date format specified for your CiviCRM installation. Without these fields, you cannot import the file.
  • Import membership data for different contact types separately; files with more than one contact type will not work. Import new memberships and renewals separately as well.

To import the membership data:

  1. Navigate to Memberships > Import Memberships.
  2. On the Upload Data screen:
    • Select your import data file. It must be a CSV file.
    • Select the checkbox if your source data contains column headers.
    • Specify the contact type you are importing.
    • Indicate what date format you are using.
    • Click Continue >>.
  3. On the Match Fields screen, map your membership data to the appropriate CiviCRM fields under the Matching CiviCRM Field column. You can Save this field mapping for future imports.
  4. On the Preview screen, review the table showing Total Rows in the uploaded file, rows with errors, and valid rows. If you continue, rows with errors will be skipped. You can download a file containing just the problem records, continue with the import, correct those records, and import them again. Alternatively, correct your original CSV file and restart the import.
  5. If there are no errors or you do not want to correct the errors found, click Import Now>>. You will see the import progress and, when it is complete, a summary of the activity and results.

docs.title: Manual entry of memberships
docs.text: Contacts can become members through self-service on a website, but memberships can also be processed manually. Appropriately permissioned users can create memberships one at a time, enter batches of membership payments, or import memberships.

docs.title: CiviMember access control
docs.text:
Use Administer > User & Permissions > Permissions to control access to CiviMember features:

  • To find and view memberships, assign access CiviMember and view contact permissions for the associated record. If payments are involved, also assign view contributions.
  • To create or edit membership records, assign edit memberships and edit contact permissions for the associated contact record. If payments are involved, also assign edit contributions.

More details on permissions can be found at http://wiki.civicrm.org/confluence/display/CRMDOC/Default+Permissions+and+Roles.

docs.title: Creating a new membership record
docs.text: You can create a membership from an existing contact's record or through the Memberships menu. The menu lets you create a new contact while adding the membership. From an existing contact's record, you can use Submit Credit Card Membership to process payment immediately if you have set up a payment processor that allows credit card transactions directly on your site. The Memberships menu does not offer that option, but you can record other types of payments, such as checks and cash.

docs.title: Via an existing contact record
docs.text:
From the contact's record, click the Memberships tab, then click Add Membership. If you have set up a payment processor that allows credit card transactions directly on your site, you can select Submit Credit Card Membership and process the payment immediately.

Many fields on the "New Membership" form will be auto-completed if left blank:

  • Membership Organization and Type: Select the organization the contact has a membership with and the type of membership.
  • Choose Price Set: If you have various fee structures for different classes of memberships, you can use Membership Price Sets by selecting Choose Price Set rather than Membership Organization and Type.
  • Number of Terms: Enter the number of membership periods or terms. The membership end date will be set for that number of terms. This option is hidden when using membership price sets.
  • Source: If left blank, the system will complete details about the record, including whether it was an offline or online transaction and who completed the record.
  • Campaign: If the membership is connected with a larger campaign, select the campaign name. To learn more, see the Campaign section.
  • Member Since: The date the membership record was created is auto-filled but can be overridden.
  • Start Date: For a rolling membership, the current date is auto-filled. For a fixed-period membership, CiviCRM determines the start date from the membership type configuration. The date can be overridden.
  • End Date: This is automatically calculated from the start date and membership type settings but can be overridden.
  • Auto-renew: This field is shown only if you have chosen a Membership Type with auto-renew functionality set in the Membership Type and are using Submit Credit Card Membership to create the Membership.

  • Status Override?: Check this box to manually define a status instead of the automatically provided status.

    Caution

    This setting will stop the status from automatically updating based on the membership status rules you have set up when defining your memberships.

  • Record Membership Payment?: Check this box and complete the transaction fields to record the money paid. This creates a contribution record as well as the membership record. After recording the membership, you can see the related contribution record at the bottom of the membership record.

    • Record Payment from a Different Contact?: This is often used for gift memberships.
    • Financial Type: Select the appropriate financial type for the payment.
    • Amount: Enter the membership payment amount.
    • Received Date and Time: Enter when the payment was received.
    • Paid By: Select the payment instrument, such as cash or check. You can learn more about configuring Payment Instruments in the Contributions section.
    • Check Number: If the payment was received by check, enter its number.
    • Transaction ID: If you have a payment processor, CiviCRM stores an auto-generated transaction id. For manual transactions, you can enter a bank transfer ID or other identifier as applicable.
    • Payment Status: Select the status of the membership payment received. You can learn more about configuring Payment Instruments in the Contributions section.

  • Send Confirmation and Receipt?: Check this box to email the contact confirmation of their membership.

    • Receipt From: Select the email address the confirmation receipt is from. If the address is not listed, you can add it under Mailings > From Email Addresses.
    • Receipt Message: Enter a special message for the member, or leave it blank to use the default confirmation and receipt message.

docs.title: Auto-renew memberships via a contact record
docs.text:
To manually create a membership that will auto-renew, go to the contact's summary screen, select the Memberships tab, and click Submit Credit Card Membership. If you select a Membership Type set up for recurring, a checkbox labelled Membership renewed automatically will be shown.

If you check Auto-renew, a recurring payment (subscription) request will be submitted to the selected payment processor. If successful, the membership will automatically renew on the last day of the membership period until the recurring payment is cancelled. Membership payment receipt emails will include a link for the member to cancel auto-renewal.

docs.title: Via the Memberships menu
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Memberships > New Membership, then select the contact or create a new contact.

  2. Fill out the New Member form with the appropriate membership and payment information described under Via an existing contact record above.

docs.title: Gift memberships
docs.text:
When entering a membership manually, select Record Payment from a Different Contact? to record it as a gift. The person paying for the membership (gifter) can be an existing contact or a new contact created during the process.

The payment will be recorded on the gifter's record, with a soft credit for the membership on the gift recipient's record. The receipt will be sent to the gifter. You will need to send a separate email or letter to tell the gift recipient about their membership.

docs.title: Entering batches of membership payments
docs.text:
The Batch Data Entry feature in the Memberships menu can be used to enter batches of membership payments received on paper forms or similar. It works for new and existing contacts and includes verification of the total amount and item count against the payments recorded on your deposit slip(s).

Its batch entry grid has a copy feature for setting all fields to the same value. You can also create new contacts without leaving the batch entry screen.

Several CiviCRM reserved profiles determine which fields appear in the batch entry input grid. To collect information not currently included in those profiles, alter the profiles to reflect the fields you want to display.

You can read more about the [Batch Entry of Contributions or Membership Payments](../contributions/manual-entry-of-contributions.md#batch-entry-of-contribution-membership-or-pledge-payments.

docs.title: Membership price sets
docs.text:
Membership price sets let contacts:

  • Sign up for multiple membership terms at the same time.
  • Sign up for more than one membership in a single transaction, such as national and local memberships.
  • Select non-membership options, such as information booklets, when they sign up for a membership.

Here is an example of a membership price set offering all these options:

The Donwell Swim Club price set consists of five price fields: National Association Fees, Annual Club membership, Club Gear, raffle tickets and donation.

It offers two membership types:

Define these membership types before creating the price set. See Defining Memberships. You must also define all the financial types you will need before creating the price set.

Membership price sets can be used on online join-up or renewal pages, or for new member sign-ups processed manually through the CiviCRM back office system. They cannot be used for renewals processed manually. Each membership must be renewed individually (see the Renewals chapter). You may also need to create a contribution price set for the non-membership items you offer.

You cannot combine memberships that can be auto-renewed with memberships that do not offer auto-renewal or with non-membership items.

Price sets can be configured in many ways. Test a price set thoroughly before using it on your live site to make sure it fits your situation.

docs.title: Create a price set
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Memberships > New Price Set or Administer > CiviMember > New Price Set.
  2. Enter the price set name. It appears both to the public as part of the price set and to admin staff choosing between price sets, so make it descriptive for both.
  3. Tick Membership.
  4. Set the Default Financial Type. This choice has accounting implications; refer to the Contributions section for more information.
  5. Add pre- or post-form help text if you want to.
  6. Make sure the price set is active and Save.

You will be taken to a form to create the first price field for your price set.

docs.title: Create a price field
docs.text:
1. Enter a name in Field Label. This name appears to the public.
  2. Select the Input Field Type. Four input types are available:
  3. Text/Numeric Quantity: Set a unit Price. The price set displays a text box for a quantity; the quantity entered is multiplied by the unit price to calculate the amount.
  4. Select: Displays a dropdown box from which one option can be selected.
  5. Radio: Displays options in a list; up to one option can be selected.
  6. Checkbox: Displays options in a list; multiple selections are allowed.

Each input type is used in an example below.

  1. Financial Type is set to the Default Financial Type chosen when the price set was created. You can override it if required.
  2. Display Amount? displays an option’s price next to its label. If the field label includes the option price, you can untick it. Otherwise, leave it ticked.
  3. Order, Field Help, Required and Active are either self-explanatory or have help on the form.
  4. Active On and Expire On can make a price field invisible until the Active On date, invisible after the Expire On date, or visible only between those dates. For example you could use these fields to bring in a price rise at 12:00am on 1 January 2019 by setting the price field with the old prices to Expire On 1/12/2019 12:00am and the price field with the new prices to be Active On 1/12/2019 12:00am.
  5. Set Visibility to Public (visible on your website to those who can see the membership sign-up page) or Admin (visible only through the back end, and only to users with appropriate permissions).

docs.title: Multiple membership terms
docs.text:
The National Membership price field illustrates how to let contacts sign up for multiple membership terms at the same time using the Radio input field type.

In Membership Type, select an option from the dropdown list of configured membership types. Selecting a membership type fills Number of terms with 1 and fills Label, Amount and Financial Type from that membership type’s definition. You can change all these values.

The National Association Fees membership type has a duration of 1 year and a minimum fee of $100. Setting number of terms to 2 gives 2 years of membership. If you have more than one option, change the Label so each option has a different label. You can increase the Amount to any value, allowing concession and standard fees for the same number of terms.

Because the price of each option is not included in its Label, Display Amount? needs to be ticked.

This configuration reduces the number of membership types you need: this price field needs only a 1 year National Association membership type with a minimum fee of $100, instead of three membership types. Members cannot auto-renew with this type of multi-term configuration.

docs.title: Membership of more than one organisation
docs.text:
In addition to National Association Fees, contacts must sign up for a membership with the swim club. This field uses the Select input field type.

Selecting a membership type from the dropdown list fills Number of terms with 1 and fills Label, Amount and Financial Type from that membership type’s definition. You can change any of these values.

Because the price of each option is not included in its Label, Display Amount? needs to be ticked.

Together, these two price fields let someone sign up for a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 2 memberships. The memberships must be linked to two different organisations: a contact can have only one active membership with a specific organisation. See Defining Memberships for more information.

docs.title: Non-membership price fields
docs.text:
You can configure price set fields to offer additional services, subscriptions or other non-membership options.

The example has three non-membership price fields. The first offers club-branded swimming gear. The Checkbox field type lets people choose more than one item.

Because these are products rather than memberships, leave Membership Type and Number of Terms empty. Set Label, Amount and Financial Type for each option. Because the price of each option is not included in its Label, Display Amount? needs to be ticked.

The three price fields discussed so far contain the same fields, despite using different input field types. Radio and Select are interchangeable: both allow one option and can be used for membership or non-membership options. Use Checkbox when contacts can choose more than one option from a single price field. It can also be used for either membership or non-membership options.

The fourth input field type, Text/Numeric Quantity, can only be used for non-membership options. Usually, include the unit price in the field label, as in this example, or in the field help. In that case, Display Amount? should not be ticked.

This displays as:

This price field is visible only between the Active On and Expire On dates, so raffle tickets can be purchased only during the selling period authorised by the relevant licensing authority.

The final price field allows people to give a donation. Its unit price is 1. The unit price is not included in the field label, although the currency symbol is, and Display Amount? is not ticked. This is the best configuration for "any amount" donations.

Here is how all the fields look on the final screen:

docs.title: Create a membership report
docs.text:
Use a membership template to create and save a report with criteria different from those offered by the built-in membership reports.

  1. Click on Reports > Membership Reports > click the New Member Report button.
  2. On the Create New Report Template screen, click one of the membership report templates and enter your criteria.

  1. Click Preview Report to check your results.
  2. If you like what you see, click Create Report, then enter the information you want to save this as a new membership report.

See Reporting to learn more about working with reports in general.

docs.title: Export membership records
docs.text:
You can export membership records for further analysis, document mail merges, or reports outside CiviCRM. You can export a default set of primary fields or choose fields specific to the membership record.

First, search for the specific membership records you would like to export.

  1. Click on Memberships > Find Members and enter your search criteria.
  2. On the "Find Members" search results screen, select the records you want to import. In the -actions- drop down, select Export Members.
  3. Select Export PRIMARY fields or Select fields for export, then click Continue.

  • If you selected Export PRIMARY fields, a file called CiviCRM_Member_Search.csv will be created containing the membership records based on your search criteria.
  • If you selected Select fields for export, include the fields you would like to export. Check Save this field mapping if you want to re-use this field mapping for a future export, then click Export. A file called CiviCRM_Member_Search.csv will be created containing the membership records based on your search criteria and the fields you selected to export.

docs.title: Membership reports
docs.text: There are several ways to report on and analyse memberships. The membership dashboard gives a quick summary of current memberships by membership type, including current member totals and totals for last month, this month, and the current year to date. You can also search for specific membership details using Advanced Search or Find Memberships.

docs.title: Viewing membership reports
docs.text:
CiviCRM comes with several membership reports:

The Membership Summary report groups information about members by a date frequency you specify, such as month, week, quarter, or year. For example, you can view the number of members who joined each month across a date range, membership types, or other custom data you collect about them.

Click a highlighted field to see the corresponding Membership Detail report for that row. For example, clicking May 2015 for membership type General shows:

The Membership Detail report shows information for each membership record based on your selected criteria.

The Lapsed Memberships report lists memberships that lapsed or will lapse before the date you specify.

The Contribution and Membership Details report displays details of contributions and contributions connected to membership records, based on your report criteria.

docs.title: Online membership sign up
docs.text:
This page explains how to create a membership sign up page, test it, and add it to your website. For background on concepts such as membership types and membership statuses, see Defining Memberships.

Alternative: use Contribution Forms

Contribution Forms provide a new way to take Contributions from visitors to your site. Contribution Forms are built with FormBuilder, which allows more flexibility to site admins to tailor forms to your specific needs. They also provide a number of more modern clientside payment integrations. At time of writing, only a few Payment Processors are supported.

docs.title: About membership sign up pages
docs.text:
A membership sign up page is an online contribution page with the ability to sign up for a membership. Membership sign up and contributing money have similar workflows, so membership pages can use contribution-page features such as premiums. Use a contribution page for online sign up even if the membership is free; see Free memberships below.

Contribution-page options are grouped into tabs. Follow the instructions in online contributions to create a contribution page. Once you give it a name, the tabs appear at the top of the page as you continue setting it up.

The tabs most relevant to memberships include Memberships, which contains most of the membership configuration, and Profiles, which lets you collect information about the people or organisations completing the form. For the full range of contribution-page options, see online contribution pages.

docs.title: The Title tab
docs.text:
The Title tab is the first page you see when creating a membership page. Set the page title and basic information, such as the Financial Type, that will be recorded for memberships made through this page.

You can also add an introductory message to the membership page. This text can include images and other simple HTML.

docs.title: Organisational memberships
docs.text: The Title tab has a check box that allows people to become members on behalf of an organisation. This is the recommended way to offer organisational memberships. When you enable it, you are prompted to select a profile to collect organisational information. Organisational sign up can be optional or required.

docs.title: The Amounts tab
docs.text:
The Amounts tab contains financial options, including the payment processor used on the page. You can select more than one payment processor to give people a choice.

Configure membership fees on the Memberships tab, not the Amounts tab. If you want to collect membership fees without soliciting extra contributions, leave Contribution Amounts section enabled unticked. To solicit contributions in addition to membership fees, tick the box and add suggested contribution options or configure a contribution price set.

docs.title: Free memberships
docs.text: For free memberships, leave the 'Execute real-time monetary transactions' box unticked and choose a membership type with a zero value minimum fee.

docs.title: The Memberships tab
docs.text:
Check Membership Section Enabled to use the contribution page for membership sign up and renewal.

The first few boxes let you add text for initial sign up and renewals. When a logged in user with a current or expired membership views the membership sign up page, CiviCRM automatically replaces it with a membership renewal page containing the text from the renewals box.

The options after the text boxes configure the membership types available on the form.

For a simple setup, select which membership types are available, which is the default, and which can be auto-renewed. Auto-renew requires membership types set up as auto-renew and a payment processor that supports automatic recurring payments.

If you enable auto-renew for a membership, users will see: "Please renew my membership automatically. (Your initial membership fee will be processed once you complete the confirmation step. You will be able to cancel automatic renewals at any time by logging in to your account or contacting us.)" Membership payment receipt emails will include a link for the member to cancel the auto-renewal.

You can make membership signup optional—for example, when you want to offer membership on a contribution page without requiring it. In that case, check "Contribution Amounts section enabled" on the Amounts tab. You can decide whether such payments are recorded separately from membership fee payments.

If the Membership Types table cannot provide what you need, use a Membership price set. For example, a price set can:

  • Allow users to sign up for multiple classes of membership, such as national and local memberships, at the same time.
  • Let people sign up for multiple membership terms at the same time.
  • Offer other options, such as a paid subscription in addition to membership signup.

docs.title: The Receipt tab
docs.text: After a visitor completes the membership signup or renewal form, they are redirected to a thank-you page and can have an email receipt generated and sent to them. The Receipt tab, the fourth step in the wizard, lets you configure these options. You can customise the message added to the membership receipt and the email address it comes from. To customise the receipt email template further, use Mailings > Message templates.

docs.title: Email alerts for memberships
docs.text:
For real-time updates about who has processed a membership, add one or more staff email addresses to CC Receipt To or BCC Receipt To. Separate multiple addresses with commas.

Warning

Make sure addresses in CC Receipt To and BCC Receipt To are correct and do not bounce or return an error email. CiviCRM interprets any return emails it receives as a bounce for the CiviCRM Contact who received the receipt, not for the CC/BCC address. This can put the Contact's email address On Hold and cause future emails to not be sent. For more details see this issue report.

docs.title: The Tell-A-Friend tab
docs.text: You can add a tell-a-friend feature to the thank-you page. Members can email friends a link and information about your organisation. Friends who are told about the membership sign up are added to CiviCRM if they do not already exist; their source field shows that they were added via tell-a-friend.

docs.title: Collecting information as part of membership sign up (the Profiles tab)
docs.text:
By default, contribution pages include only an email field. Add a profile to collect more information about members as they complete the sign up form, such as their address or interests. If the person signing up is logged in, CiviCRM populates their profile fields with available data. Don't add a membership profile: that information is collected automatically during online membership sign up.

On the Profiles tab, you can select an existing profile. If you have permission, you can also edit an existing profile or create a new one for the page.

Warning

If you edit an existing profile here, it will be changed in all places where that profile is used.

docs.title: Premiums tab
docs.text:
Premiums are thank-you gifts and incentives offered to people who donate to your organisation. They are commonly associated with tiered donation levels, such as a T-shirt for a $50 donation, but can also be used on membership pages. Before including premiums on a contribution page, configure them through Contributions > Premiums (Thank-you Gifts).

The Premiums tab controls introductory text, contact information, and other premium-related details.

docs.title: Testing membership sign up pages
docs.text:
After configuring the page, test the sign up process. Go to Contributions > Manage Contribution Pages, click Links next to your membership sign-up/renewal page, then click Test-drive. Membership data submitted in test mode is added to CiviCRM as test data. It is not included in membership stats or searches for members. To find and delete test memberships, click the is test check box in Find Memberships.

Go through the process several times as someone joining your organisation, using different combinations of fields. Check that the data appears as expected in CiviCRM. After testing and making any necessary changes, ask other staff or friends outside your organisation to test it.

When using the Test-drive Registration option, you see the same registration pages as a regular user, but the online payment isn't debited from your card. See Payment processors for information about dummy processors and card details for test transactions.

Periodically test and review the membership process. Members' use of the form can provide indirect feedback: if they do not enter data as intended, you may need to change it. You can also ask recent members how easy it was to join and how the form could be improved.

docs.title: Adding membership sign up pages to your website
docs.text:
Once you have made the contribution page, make it visible on your website using the method for your CMS.

Membership sign up pages inherit your website theme and should look reasonably nice out of the box. You can add images to the page's HTML text areas. Many organisations also improve the design of their membership pages to increase sign up rates. Design changes are outside the scope of this page, but a website designer familiar with your CMS and CiviCRM can help.

docs.title: In Drupal
docs.text: Go to Contributions > Manage Contribution Pages, click Links next to your membership sign-up/renewal page, then click Live Page to view the finished page. Copy the URL and include it in a content page or assign it to a menu item.

docs.title: In WordPress
docs.text:
Go to Contributions > Manage Contribution Pages, click Links next to your membership sign-up/renewal page, then click Live Page. Copy the URL and insert it into an HTML link or menu.

Alternatively, use a plugin such as Page Links To create a URL 'slug', or click the WordPress shortcode icon to insert a form into any page or post.

docs.title: In Joomla!
docs.text:
The most direct way to expose a membership signup/renewal page on the front of your Joomla! website is to create a menu item:

  1. Navigate to a menu and create a new CiviCRM item.
  2. From the list of menu options, choose Contributions.
  3. In the basic parameters section, select the contribution page you want to expose from the dropdown menu.
  4. Save the menu item and view the website to confirm the page's functionality.

docs.title: Permissions needed for online membership sign up/renewal.
docs.text:
Anonymous and Authenticated roles need the following CMS permissions to join or renew online:

  • Profile listings and forms: Lets you collect core contact information (name, address, etc.) when people sign up.
  • Access all custom data: Must be enabled to collect custom data.
  • Make online contributions: Must be granted unless memberships are free and you do not want to accept donations during sign up or renewal.

docs.title: Set a default online membership renewal page
docs.text:
When a membership is purchased using the online membership signup page (self-service), that user's Contact Dashboard will contain a "renew" link pointing to that page. However this link will not appear for members whose initial membership was entered manually unless you configure a Default Online Membership Renewal Page as follows:

  1. If it does not already exist, create a membership page that includes all currently available memberships. You may need to use a Membership price set for this if the membership fees need to be allocated to more than one financial type.
  2. Navigate to Administer > CiviMember > CiviMember Component Settings.
  3. For Default Online Membership Renewal Page choose the membership page containing all your membership types

A "renew" link pointing to that page will then be displayed on the Contact Dashboard for any memberships which were manually entered.

docs.title: Manually renewing a membership for a single contact
docs.text:
1. Go to the contact's summary page.
  2. Click on the Memberships tab
  3. Click MORE next to the membership record
  4. Select Renew to enter cash, cheque or EFT payment or Renew-Credit Card to process the renewal through your online payment processor.

docs.title: Update multiple memberships
docs.text:
You can use the Update multiple memberships feature (previously called Batch Update Members Via Profile) to update multiple existing membership records (don't confuse this with the Batch Data Entry feature that is used for adding new memberships and member payments).

To update multiple memberships, create and configure a Profile that contains fields pertaining to membership information that you want to display and update.

To use the Update multiple memberships feature:

  1. Find the memberships you would like to update by selecting Memberships > Find Members. Enter your search criteria and click Search.
  2. From the Find Members results screen, select the membership records and select Update multiple memberships from the -actions- dropdown box and click Go.
  3. From the Update multiple memberships screen, in Select Profile, select the profile you want to use from the dropdown box and click Continue >>.
  4. From the Update multiple memberships screen, you can update the information that is displayed based on the profile you selected. You can use the "auto-copy" icon at the top of a column to copy and paste the value from the field of the first record of that column to the rest of the fields below in the column. Once you are done updating, click Update Memberships.

Below is an example of an Update multiple memberships screen that is using a membership profile configured to display the Membership Type and the Membership Start Date fields for use with Update multiple memberships.

docs.title: Membership renewals
docs.text: Contacts can renew their memberships automatically or online. Office staff can enter renewals individually or in bulk via Batch Update of Memberships Via Profile. You can also let members know when their membership is due to be renewed.

docs.title: Renewal concepts
docs.text:
There is an important distinction between adding a new membership and renewing an existing membership. If someone is approaching their membership end date and wants to continue being a member, in most cases you will want to renew the existing membership using CiviMember's renewal workflow rather than creating a new membership.

Memberships have three primary dates. Member Since is not altered when a membership is renewed. Start date and End date may change depending what membership status is in effect when the renewal is processed.

  • If the renewal is processed when the membership status is one that has a Yes in the member column on Administer > CiviMember > Membership Status Rules then the Start date does not change and the end date is extended by the duration of the renewal.
  • If the renewal is processed when the membership status is one that has a No in the member column on Administer > CiviMember > Membership Status Rules then the Start date is changed to the current date and the End date is calculated from the new start date.

If applicable for the membership type, a contribution (financial) is recorded as part of the renewal process. This will create a contribution record that is linked to the membership record. Over time, and after a few renewals, the membership record will be a single membership record whose end date is extended, with multiple related financial transactions representing each renewal purchase.

docs.title: Membership up-sell
docs.text:
Membership up-sell allows contacts to change membership type as part of the renewal process. If a contact with a membership linked to an organisation renews under a different membership type belonging to the same organisation, the existing membership will be changed to that type and the associated membership history, including join date and contributions, will be preserved. The existing end date will be extended by the duration of the new membership type.

If this is not what you want then you will need to link your membership types to different organisations. (One can be a dummy organisation created purely for this purpose and invisible to the user. See the Membership types section of the Defining Memberships chapter for a more detailed explanation.)

If you are using CiviCRM to manage memberships for more than one organisation, note that a contact's membership type cannot be changed or up-sold to a type from another membership organization.

docs.title: Renewal reminders
docs.text: Letting a member know that their membership is about to end is the first step in the process of getting them to renew. CiviCRM facilitates communications with your members via email or via postal mail.

docs.title: Email reminders
docs.text:
One or more renewal reminder emails can be sent automatically using the Schedule Reminders feature (Administer > Communications > Schedule Reminders). This is particularly helpful for rolling membership types, where memberships could be ending at any time during the year. Refer to the Schedule Reminders page for the steps involved in sending out a scheduled reminder once you have composed your message.

Exactly what you want to say in your reminder email(s) will depend on what type of membership it is and when it is being sent in relation to the membership end date. For example, renewal reminders sent three months in advance to individuals who signed up on behalf of organisations (to give them enough time to arrange for a purchase order and payment through their accounts department) would be different from those sent one week after an individual's membership has ended.

Tip: Pre-filling the renewal form

If members are able to renew online, all renewal email reminders should contain a checksum token link to prefill the renewal form with any data that exists in their record.

As with all emails you send out you need to allow time to test renewal reminder templates, especially if you have complex membership structures and want to customise messages based on member types or other factors.

Remember that by default scheduled reminders will be sent to people who have opted out of bulk or all emails unless you specifically exclude those people. If people can elect to auto-renew their memberships then you should exclude members who have chosen that option from the scheduled reminders.

docs.title: Postal reminders
docs.text: You may also want to post out letters to all your members who are due to renew or just post letters to those without an email address and those who have opted out of bulk or all emails. Refer to Postal mail communications for ways to generate those letters.

docs.title: Automatically renewed memberships
docs.text: For members who have chosen this option when they first joined, on their renewal date the payment will be taken automatically from their pre-authorised credit card, their membership end date will be updated and they will receive appropriate thank-you and receipts from CiviCRM. (See Defining memberships, Online memberships sign up and Manual entry of memberships for details of how to set up auto-renewing memberships.)

docs.title: Online renewals
docs.text:
CiviCRM uses the same page for new memberships as it does for renewals. The only difference is that the page title and introductory message with the text you entered into the renewal fields on the memberships tab when you were configuring your online membership page. The renewal page is automatically displayed at the same URL as the membership join page when viewed by a logged in website visitor that has a valid current or expired membership.

When you are setting up membership sign up pages, it is worth remembering that current members will only see the renewal page if they are logged in. If they are not logged in, they will see the sign up page. If they fill that page in and, based on their contact information, CiviCRM can find their existing contact record then their membership will be renewed. If CiviCRM can't find their existing contact record (perhaps they have changed their email address) then a new contact record and membership will be created.

This is one source of duplicates in your database and you need to minimise the chances that this will happen. Two ways to do this are to always include a checksum token in renewal reminder emails and add text to the new member introductory message to remind people that they should log in before they renew.

docs.title: What is CiviMember
docs.text:
CiviMember is the CiviCRM component that supports and automates membership management. It allows you to:

  • Define membership types and pricing schemes that meet your needs.
  • Create self-service options for online membership sign-up and renewal, utilising CiviContribute.
  • Manage memberships manually through the administrative interface.
  • Create and schedule automated messages to welcome new members, remind them about upcoming renewal, and more.
  • Track and report on contacts through the membership cycle.
  • Grant additional website privileges for members.
