  1. Select the Group whose information you want to make publicly viewable or searchable. For a directory of active members, for example, create a Smart Group of members with a status of New, Current, or Grace.
  2. Choose that Smart Group in this field. Smart groups are dynamic: when new memberships are added, the corresponding contact will automatically be included in the directory.
  3. If you do not choose a Group, CiviCRM will, by default, allow a search to expose every record in your database. In most cases, you will not want website visitors to see who is in the whole database.

docs.title: Add new contacts to a group
docs.text:
Any new contacts who fill out the Profile will be added to the selected Group. For example, people who complete a volunteer sign-up form could be added to a Volunteers Group.

By default, contacts receive no confirmation that they have been added to the group and are not asked to validate their email address. To send an email to contacts who complete the form, go to Administer >> CiviMail >> CiviMail Component Settings and check "Enable Double Opt-in for Profiles which use the "Add to Group" setting". Contacts must respond (opt-in) before they are added to the group.

If you want to offer more than one group, consider using the groups profile field.

docs.title: Notify when profile form is submitted
docs.text: For a Profile used as a sign-up form, enter an email address to receive a notification whenever the form is submitted. For example, a volunteer coordinator could receive an email for each volunteer sign-up. Separate multiple addresses with commas.

docs.title: Redirect URL
docs.text: For a standalone Profile form, Redirect URL sends people to a specified web page after submission, such as a thank-you page. It does not apply when the Profile is embedded in an event sign-up or contribution form. If left blank, people are directed to a page displaying the information they entered.

docs.title: Cancel redirect URL
docs.text: This works like Redirect URL but applies when people cancel their form submission.

docs.title: Include reCAPTCHA?
docs.text:
This applies when anonymous users fill in Profiles. CAPTCHA is spam-blocking software that asks a visitor to enter text displayed in a graphic, preventing automated web-crawling spiders from completing the form. The source highly recommends including it.

To use this feature, set up a free reCAPTCHA account and enter configuration information in CiviCRM. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > reCAPTCHA Settings; that page includes sign-up instructions.

docs.title: Drupal user account registration option
docs.text: For Profiles used on public pages, this setting determines whether people can or must sign up for a website account in addition to submitting the form. It can be used when people become members or register for an event.

docs.title: WordPress user account registration option
docs.text: WordPress also allows CiviCRM Profiles to create accounts as described above. Within WordPress Settings > General, "Membership [ ] Anyone can register" must be clicked.

docs.title: What to do upon duplicate match
docs.text:
For Profiles used on public pages, this setting controls what happens when submitted contact data matches an existing record. You must choose an option; "Issue warning and do not save" is the default. Profile matching uses the Unsupervised deduplication rule. See Deduping and Merging in Working with Your Data for more about deduplication rules. If multiple contacts match, the first matching record is used.

  • "Issue warning and do not save" is ignored when a Profile is embedded in an online contribution, membership sign-up, or event registration form. In those cases, the transaction is linked to the matching contact. Otherwise, the user sees a message that a record already exists and cannot submit the form.
  • "Update the matching contact" adds new form information to the contact record and overwrites existing values in fields included on the form. For example, an address entered on the form replaces the address already in the database.
  • "Allow duplicate contact to be created" creates a new contact for every submitted form, regardless of potential matches. All submissions are saved without overwriting data, but duplicate records may need to be deduped later. See Deduping and Merging in Working with Your Data.

docs.title: Proximity search
docs.text: For a searchable directory, this adds a search block with a start address and a search radius. Choose None if it is irrelevant, Optional to offer it, or Required to make users enter both values.

docs.title: Enable mapping for this profile?
docs.text: For a searchable directory, this adds a map to the search results.

docs.title: Include profile edit links in search results?
docs.text: For a searchable directory, this adds a link in results listings to edit Profile fields in the returned contact records. Only users with permission to edit those contacts see the link.

docs.title: Include Drupal user account information links in search results?
docs.text:
For a searchable directory, this adds a link to a resulting contact’s Drupal user account information, such as their My Account page. The link appears only for contacts who have a website user account.

After saving the Profile settings, add its fields. If the form will use custom fields, make sure they have already been created.

docs.title: Add fields and choose field settings
docs.text:
Not every field setting applies to every use of a Profile.

  1. Click Add Field.
  2. For Field Name, choose the record type from the - select - dropdown, then choose the field from the secondary dropdown.
  3. For Field Label, use the prefilled default or rewrite it for your audience. For example, you might rename Postal Code to Zip Code. This label appears wherever the Profile is used.
  4. Check Required? to require the field whenever the Profile is used—for example, to require First Name, Last Name, or Email in a form submission. This is not relevant to Search Views usages [known as Search Results in 4.1 and previous].
  5. Check View Only? to let users view but not edit the field. Fields marked View Only are not included when the Profile exposes search results. This setting is not relevant when the Profile is used only to collect information.
  6. Set Visibility according to the Profile’s use:
  7. For a searchable directory, set fields you want on the search form to Public Pages or Public Pages and Listings.
  8. For sign-up forms, use User and User Admin only, so other visitors to the form cannot view database data.
  9. For Search Views, use Public Pages or Public Pages and Listings.

Either Public Page choice reveals two more settings: - Searchable? applies only to searchable directories. Check it to include the field on the search form. - Results Column? applies only to Search Views (known as Search Results in 4.1 and previous). Check it or the field will not appear in the Search View.

  1. Use Field Pre Help and Field Post Help to guide people completing forms. Field pre help appears inline. Field post help will create a small speech bubble which when clicked appear in yellow.
  2. Use Order to control the order of fields in the Profile. Lower numbers appear first.
  3. Leave Active? checked so the field appears when the Profile is used.
  4. Click Save and New to add another field, or Save when you are finished.

docs.title: Manage existing Profiles
docs.text: View and edit Profiles at Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Profiles. Use Fields to add fields or edit field settings, and Settings to change Profile settings. Under more, you can see how Profiles will appear, obtain links and embed code, or copy a Profile as the basis for another.

docs.title: Using Profiles
docs.text: These instructions cover the Profile uses described in the overview.

docs.title: Standalone forms with Profiles
docs.text:
In Drupal and Joomla!, you can use either of these methods after creating a Profile:

  • Link to the page CiviCRM creates. At Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Profiles, click more beside the Profile and choose Use Profile-Create Mode. You can publish the resulting link in an email, on a blog, or elsewhere.
  • Embed the form’s HTML. At Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Profiles, click more beside the Profile and choose HTML Form Snippet. Copy the code on the next screen and paste it into a page on your website.

WordPress offers a third method:

  1. When creating or editing a post, click the CiviCRM button to insert a CiviCRM shortcode.

  1. On the popup form, select Profile as the frontend element.

  1. Use the second select widget to choose the Profile. Select the form’s purpose—create, edit, or view—and click Insert Form.

docs.title: Multi-value fields in Profiles
docs.text:
Multi-value custom field sets hold more than one set of custom data per contact. Work experience is an example of repeating data. You can expose these fields through Profiles.

The screenshot shows a Profile collecting names and work experience. Its multi-value custom data is displayed in a way that supports adding, editing, and deleting multiple instances.

docs.title: Making directories with Profiles
docs.text:
1. Create a Profile. Consider these Advanced Settings for directory use:
  2. Enable mapping gives visitors the ability to map directory contacts using Google or Yahoo! maps and obtain directions to a record’s address dynamically. Mapping must already be enabled under Administer > System Settings > Mapping and Geocoding.
  3. Include profile edit links: adds a link in directory listings for editing data in the Profile’s fields. Only users with permission to edit the contact see it. It is not commonly needed for a membership directory.
  4. Include Drupal user information (Drupal only) adds a directory link to a contact’s Drupal user account information, such as their My Account page. The link appears only for contacts with a website user account.
  1. Add the directory’s fields. You control which fields are searchable, appear in search-result columns, and appear on the record detail View page.

Configure these field options:

  • Set Visibility for every directory field to Public Pages or Public Pages and Listings. With Public Pages and Listings, a field value in detail view is a link that runs a follow-up search for records with the same value. For example, clicking a City value searches for records in that city as though the visitor had selected it on the Profile search screen.
  • Searchable determines whether visitors can search by the field. In common directory uses, almost every field is searchable.
  • Results Column determines whether the field appears as a column in the results list. For example, selecting it for a website field puts that field in the results table. Without it, the field still appears in the record’s view mode. With it, the field appears both in the results column and in detail view.

The following images show the directory search form, the results listing with fields whose Results Column option is checked, and the detail page reached through a view link. The detail page shows all Profile fields.

docs.title: Linking to your directory
docs.text:
• Drupal: Link to the directory search page using http://www.myorganization.org/civicrm/profile?reset=1&gid=N, where N is the ID of the Profile directory.
  • Add &force=1 to that URL to show a result set directly.
  • Add &force=1&search=0 to hide the search criteria and show the result set directly.
  • Joomla!: In Menu Manager, create a front-end menu item. Select CiviCRM, choose the profile search option, and select the specific Profile in the parameters pane.
  • WordPress: This feature is not yet implemented.
  • Prepopulated searches: You can prepopulate search criteria in the URL. The options are described at http://wiki.civicrm.org/confluence/display/CRMDOC/Linking+Profiles.

docs.title: Updating multiple records at the same time
docs.text:
You can Update multiple memberships from a Find memberships search or from advanced search results when Display results as is set to Memberships. Use a Profile containing only membership fields.

Similarly, updating multiple contacts, contributions, activities, or participants requires search results of that record type and a Profile containing only fields of that type. The Update multiple ... functions can update up to 100 records at a time.

docs.title: Example: Update a diving skill field
docs.text:
Suppose you have a custom contact field called "Diving Skill Level". After an Intermediate Diving course, you want to set "Diving Skill level" to "Intermediate" for everyone who attended.

  1. On the Advanced Search screen, set the appropriate filters in the Event accordion. Leave Display Results As set to Contacts, because you are updating a contact custom field. Click Search.
  2. Go to the "Update multiple contacts" screen.

  1. Choose the Profile from the drop-down list and click Continue.
  2. On the next screen, update values as needed in the grid. Each row shows a contact’s name and the fields in the Profile.

  1. To give a field the same value in every row, enter it for the first contact. Then click the Copy icon—the image of two documents beside each column title—to copy the value to all displayed records.
  2. Click Update Contacts to save the changes, or Cancel to cancel them.

docs.title: Batch update limitations
docs.text:
• You cannot batch-update different Contact types, such as individuals and organisations, at the same time.
  • To update participant fields, start from a Find Participants search and include only participant fields in the Profile.
  • You can batch-update up to 100 records at a time. If a batch of 100 takes a long time, four batches of 25 may be quicker.

docs.title: View/edit user account /new user registration with Profiles
docs.text: For websites with logged-in users, a Profile can collect additional information during account registration. You can also invite or require people completing a Profile form to sign up for a user account.

docs.title: Include a Profile during user registration
docs.text:
1. Create a Profile used for User Registration.
  1. Add the fields people should complete during registration, using the field-adding process described on the creation page. Set field visibility to Public User Pages.

docs.title: Include Profiles in Drupal’s My Account screen
docs.text:
You can embed one or more CiviCRM Profiles in Drupal’s My Account screen so logged-in users can review and update their information there.

  1. Create a Profile, or open an existing Profile and click Settings.
  2. Select View/Edit User Account in Used For.
  3. Click Save.
  4. Add the fields people should be able to edit from their Drupal My Account page.

Warning

The Profile must include only fields related to the Individual contact type.

docs.title: Enable new account creation during Profile sign-up
docs.text:
To let constituents create a Drupal or Joomla! account while completing a Profile, use the "User account registration option" under Customize Data and Screens > Profiles: click Settings against a Profile. Anonymous users will then be invited or required to create an account; logged-in users see only the Profile fields.

The Profile must include a Primary Email Address field for this feature to function properly. The feature also works when the Profile is embedded in an online contribution or event registration page, so anonymous visitors can be invited or required to sign up for an account when registering for an event.

docs.title: Including Profiles in forms in CiviCRM components
docs.text: You may want to include selected fields on event registration and contribution pages. Profiles for those forms can include participant fields for event registrations or contribution fields for contribution pages. For instructions on including Profiles in contribution pages, event registration pages, and membership sign-up pages, see the Set-up chapters of Contributions, Events, and Memberships.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
A Profile is a collection of fields from your database. Profiles can collect data, such as on a sign-up form, or display data, such as in a member directory. They can be used internally to simplify data entry for staff and externally to display up-to-date information from the database.

You can add core and custom fields to a Profile, including multi-value custom fields. Two other available fields are Groups, which provides a set of checkboxes—one for each public group—and tags, which includes all public tags.

A Profile lets you select the fields relevant to a particular purpose. The diagram shows how existing fields become part of a Profile.

docs.title: Different uses for Profiles
docs.text: The following are ways to collect, display, and work with data using Profiles. Instructions for creating and using them are on the accompanying pages.

docs.title: Collecting information on public pages
docs.text:
A Profile can collect information from constituents on a standalone page or as part of a contribution, membership sign-up, or event registration page. You can add more than one Profile to a page, choose required fields, and add text to help people complete the form.

Examples include:

  • A volunteer sign-up form with predefined fields for first name, last name, and mailing address, plus a custom field for volunteer interests.
  • A Profile with custom fields for food preferences, added to registration pages for events where food will be served.

This Profile collects address information on a donation page.

docs.title: Displaying information on public pages
docs.text:
A Profile can display database information on public pages, so information need not be entered separately in the database and on the website.

For example, a membership-based organisation can provide a searchable membership directory that updates when a new member joins. An organization can also list donors’ names on a web page as contributions are made.

Native Americans in Philanthropy (NAP) wanted a membership directory that members could search to connect with each other. Previously, NAP created and mailed an expensive annual print directory; some information was already out of date when members received it. A searchable Profile on its website saved resources and gave members a way to connect.

docs.title: Customising your user interface
docs.text:
Profile forms can simplify manual data entry by showing volunteers or interns only the fields they need to complete. This can make entry easier and reduce errors.

A Profile can also select fields for advanced search results. For example, a Profile containing a phone number field and a custom volunteer interests field could provide an on-screen call list for a volunteer coordinator.

Details on this use are available in the Customizing the User Interface chapter in Initial Set-up.

docs.title: Updating multiple records at the same time
docs.text:
Profiles can supply fields for updating multiple records at once. After an event, for example, you might mark registrants as Attended or No-show. You might also update the Thank-You Sent field for a week’s donations.

Actions for updating multiple records are available from the Actions dropdown for most search results: Search, Advanced Search, Find Contributions, Find Memberships, Find Participants, and Find Activities. They are also available from event participant lists generated from the Manage Events screen.

Update multiple ... displays search results with the fields in your Profile, letting you change and save their values on one screen.

docs.title: Managing email lists
docs.text:
A Profile can provide a form for signing up to receive emails. Groups used to track different email lists can appear as checkboxes. When website visitors submit the form, they are added to the email lists they checked.

Details are in the Set-up chapter of the Email section of this book.

docs.title: Planning your Profiles
docs.text:
A Profile has settings for the Profile as a whole and for each field you add. Some Profile uses limit which fields you can include, and some combinations of fields are not allowed. Plan what the Profile is for and what it needs before creating it; you may also need some trial and error.

Use these guidelines when choosing fields:

  • Profiles used for Search Views can contain only fields from Contact records and the different Contact types, such as Individual.
  • Contact fields are available in all Profiles, but you cannot mix fields from different Contact types, such as Individual and Organization.
  • For fields such as Street Address or Email that apply to more than one Contact type, choose fields from Contacts rather than a specific type. The Organization field menu, for example, contains only fields that do not also apply to other Contact types.
  • Except in Search Results Profiles, you can combine Contact fields with fields from one and only one other record type: Activity, Participants, Contributions, or Membership.
  • If you combine fields from unsupported record types, you will get an error when you try to save the field.

docs.title: Other sources of information about Profiles
docs.text:
Read more about Profiles in these chapters:

  • Customizing the user interface in Intitial Set-up
  • Set-up in Email
  • Set-up in Contributions
  • Set-up in Events
  • Set-up in Memberships

docs.title: Alternatives to Profiles
docs.text: Other approaches may suit some Profile use cases. The available alternatives depend on your CMS and skills, and each has advantages and disadvantages.

docs.title: Drupal specific alternatives
docs.text:
• The Drupal Views module can make sophisticated displays of CiviCRM data, such as a list of members on a public website.
  • Drupal Webform-Integration can work with multiple contacts, events, memberships, and relationships. It also offers pagination, draft-saving, advanced spam-control, conditional fields, and flexibility in how forms are displayed. See the Drupal Integration chapter or the Webform CiviCRM Integration page.
  • You can add fields directly to Drupal user accounts without an embedded Profile. These fields will not be available in CiviCRM but will be more available in Drupal.

docs.title: The API
docs.text: With basic coding skills, you can use the API to display data flexibly on your website. See the Developer Documentation wiki for an introduction.

docs.title: Creating new relationship types
docs.text:
CiviCRM comes with a set of common relationship types that can be used to indicate relationships between contacts. If you need to track different types of relationships between your contacts, you can create your own custom relationship types.

Special Relationship Types

  • Employee <-> Employer relationship is created anytime the 'Current Employer' field is filled in, either in the Contact Summary form or via a Profile. When filled in, it will create an Organisation if one does not already exist with that name.
  • Household relationship enables household members to have the 'household address' applied to their record. Again, if a Household already exists then the individual will have a relationship created with it, if none exists then a new household will be created.
  1. In the navigation menu, go to: Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Relationship Types.
  2. Review the list of existing relationship types to ensure that you are not creating a duplicate.
  3. If the relationship type you need does not already exist, click the New Relationship Type button.
  4. Enter descriptive labels for the relationship type you are creating in the Relationship Label-A to B and Relationship Label-B to A fields. The Relationship Label-A to B field describes the relationship between Contact A and Contact B; the Relationship Label-B to A field describes the relationship between Contact B and Contact A.
  5. Some relationships can be described by the same label in both directions; in these cases you can enter the Relationship Label once in the Relationship Label-A to B field. For example, when describing the relationship between two domestic partners named Sylvia and Audre, you can say that Sylvia is the "Partner of" Audre and Audre is the "Partner of" Sylvia. Therefore you would enter the "Partner of" label only in Relationship Label-A to B field, leaving the Relationship Label-B to A field blank.
  6. In other situations one Relationship Label cannot be applied in both directions; in these cases you need to enter different Relationship Labels in each of the Relationship Label fields. For example, you can say that Kiyoshi is the "Grandparent of" Yuki but you cannot say that Yuki is the "Grandparent of" Kiyoshi. Therefore you would enter the "Grandparent of" label in the Relationship Label-A to B field and either "Grandchild of" or "Grandparent is" in the Relationship Label-B to A field.
  7. Use the Contact Type A and Contact Type B fields to designate which contact types are being linked by your relationship. Remember to check that the contact types you select for Contact A and Contact B make sense when corresponded to your Relationship Labels.
  8. Optionally enter Description for this relationship type. This is especially useful if the intended purpose of this relationship type may not be obvious to other users.
  9. Leave the Enabled box checked unless you intend to create this relationship type but not allow users to utilise it until a future date.
  10. Click Save. You will see a message telling you that the relationship type has been saved and you will see your new Relationship Type in the list below.

docs.title: Creating custom fields on relationships
docs.text: CiviCRM provides a number of standard relationship fields, described above. You may decide there is other information you want to store, either on all relationships, or just on given relationship types. Additionally, custom fields can be used as a tool to further distinguish relationships without creating inordinate numbers of types (e.g. you could track which department an employee works in using a custom field, rather than creating a new relationship type for each). You can add custom fields that display on the relationship types of your choosing. See creating custom fields for detailed instructions.

docs.title: Disabling or deleting unneeded relationship types
docs.text:
If an existing relationship type is no longer useful or relevant for your organisation, you can either disable or delete it so it is no longer presented as an option for new relationships. Disabling rather than deleting the relationship type has two significant advantages: you will still be able to see existing data on relationships of this type, and you can easily enable the relationship type again should you find you need it later.

  1. In the navigation menu, go to: Administer > Option Lists > Relationship Types.
  2. Click the More link in the row of the relationship type that you'd like to disable or delete.
  3. Select either Disable or Delete from the pop-up menu.
  4. If you select Disable, a pop-up confirmation bubble will appear. If you select Delete, you will be directed to an additional screen that provides a more serious warning and requests confirmation. Review the information provided in either confirmation message and if you are sure you'd like to complete this action, click the Delete button otherwise Cancel.
  5. If you have chosen to disable the relationship type it will appear in red in the Relationship Types list and relationships of this type will still be visible when viewing contacts. If you have chosen to delete the relationship type it will no longer appear in the Relationship Types list or in contact relationships data. In either case users will no longer be able to create new relationships of this type.
  6. To enable a previously disabled relationship type, follow steps 1 and 2 above and select Enable from the more pop-up menu.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
CiviCRM allows you to represent connections between contacts by creating relationships. For example, if a mother and son are both in your database, you can look at either record and see that they are related.

You can also track relationships between organisations, or between individuals and organisations. Entering an organisation in the Current Employer field of an individual contact's record automatically creates an "Employee of" relationship from the individual to the organisation, and an "Employer of" relationship from the organisation to the individual.

docs.title: Creating relationships between contacts
docs.text:
1. Navigate to one of the records that you want to relate.
  2. Click Add Relationship from the Actions button on the contact summary, or from the Relationships tab.
  3. Select the Relationship Type. In this case it would be "Sibling of".
  4. Begin to type the last name of the related person(s). If you discover that a contact you want to connect is not yet in the database, you can create a new contact from this screen.
  5. Optionally enter further information:
  6. Start Date and End Date if the relationship is time limited.
  7. Description — short text that shows on the relationship summary screen.
  8. Notes — longer text shown when viewing the relationship.
  9. Permissions — allows other users of the database to view or update the related contact.
  10. Enabled — shows the relationship is active.
  11. When you have made the changes you want, click Save Relationship.

docs.title: Relationship permissions
docs.text:
If a relationship is created between two contacts User 1 and User 2 and the Permissions box is set to allow User 1 'View' access to User 2, then when User 1 is logged in they can view details about User 2 using a Profile in View mode. If the permission is set to 'View and Update', User 1 can also update details about User 2 with a profile in Edit mode.

This functionality can be extended using the Related Permissions extension.

docs.title: Connecting employees and employers
docs.text:
A quick way to connect employees (stored in CiviCRM as individuals) to employers (stored as organisations) is to use the Current Employer field within an individual's record. This sets the current employer field in the contact record and creates a relationship between the contacts.

  1. Navigate to the record of the individual who you want to connect to an organisation.
  2. Click the Edit button.
  3. Begin typing the organisation name into the Current Employer field. As you type, matching names of organisations that already exist as contacts in CiviCRM will appear in a dropdown autocomplete list below the Current Employer field. If the organisation is already a contact in CiviCRM, you can select it from the dropdown list by pressing the down arrow key or by clicking on it. If the organisation does not already exist as a CiviCRM contact, enter the full organisation name.
  4. After the organisation's full name is entered in the Current Employer field, either press the Enter key or click the Save button. If the organisation is a pre-existing contact, an Employee/Employer relationship will be created between the individual and the organisation. If the organisation does not already exist, a new organisation contact will be created and the relationship will be created between the individual and the organisation. You can click the Relationships tab to view your newly created relationship Employee of and see any existing relationships.

docs.title: Other ways employees and employers can be connected
docs.text:
Employees and employers can be connected using the Current Employer field on CiviCRM Profiles and CiviCRM Contribution Pages.

When the Current Employer field is shown, the user can enter the name of their Employer; it is not presented as a select list to preserve privacy.

When the form is processed, CiviCRM will check the Current Employer field and attempt to match an existing Organisation contact before creating a new one, thus reducing potential duplicates.

The first check is performed using the Deduplication Rule, Organisation Unsupervised. If a matching Organisation contact is found, this contact is used and no new contact is created.

The second check is to compare if the Individual contact has an existing Current Employer with the same name as provided on the form. If matching, this contact is used and no new contact is created.

Lastly, if no match is found, a new Organisation contact is created and the Employee Of Relationship created to link the Individual and the new Organisation contact.

docs.title: Adding contacts to organisations
docs.text:
1. Select the desired contacts from your search results as described above.
  2. Select Add relationship - to organization from the dropdown from the Actions menu.
  3. On the Add Contacts to Organization screen, select the Relationship Type from the dropdown menu.
  4. Enter part of the desired organisation name in the Find Target Organization field, then click Search.
  5. Organisations that match your search will appear in the Mark Target Contact(s) for this Relationship section below the Search and Cancel buttons. If the organisation you're looking for appears in this list, click the radio button next to that organisation and then click the Add to Organization button below. If the organisation you're looking for does not appear in this list, try entering something different into the Find Target Organization field and clicking Search again. If you are still unable to find your desired organisation it may not exist; click Cancel, add a new organisation, and try again.
  6. After you've successfully chosen an organisation and clicked the Add to Organization button, you should see a message stating that the number of participants that you selected have been added to the organisation.
  7. Click Done to return to your search results.

docs.title: Adding contacts to households
docs.text:
1. Select the desired contacts from your search results as described above.
  2. Select Add relationship - to household from the dropdown Actions menu.
  3. Select the Relationship Type from the dropdown menu. CiviCRM will not stop you from adding multiple contacts as Head of Household for a single household, but this may cause problems later on in any situation where you are expecting Head of Household to refer to only one individual per household. Therefore, the Household Member of option may be the better choice in most situations.
  4. Enter part of the name of the household to which you are adding contacts (such as a last name shared by household members) in the Find Target Household field, then click Search.
  5. Households that match your search will appear in the Mark Target Contact(s) for this Relationship section below the Search and Cancel buttons. If the household you're looking for appears in this list, click the radio button next to that household and then click the Add to Household button below. If the household you're looking for does not appear in this list, try entering something different into the Find Target Household field and clicking Search again. If you are still unable to find your desired household it may not exist; click the Cancel button, add a new household, and try again.
  6. After you've successfully chosen a household and clicked the Add to Household button, you should see a message stating that the number of participants that you selected have been added to the household.
  7. Click Done to return to your search results.

docs.title: Smart groups
docs.text:
Smart groups are 'saved searches'. They are useful for keeping track of contacts who meet certain criteria, such as 'all members based in Europe'. To create a smart group, search using your desired criteria and then choose 'Create smart group'. Once the smart group is created, each time you ask to see its contacts, CiviCRM will carry out a search and show you the contacts who meet the criteria you specified.

Smart groups can be useful in many situations. Consider how you might use them in your work.

docs.title: When might I use a smart group?
Smart groups and profiles: a membership directory
docs.text:
You could use a smart group with a profile to display a directory of members on your website. Create a smart group that includes members of your organization, then create a profile with the fields you want to display in the directory. Configure the profile to show only contacts in that smart group.

When a contact becomes a member—for example, by filling in your membership form and paying online—they will automatically be added to the smart group and published in your members directory.

docs.title: Smart groups as mailing lists: an events newsletter
docs.text:
Suppose anyone who has registered for or attended an event should receive an events newsletter. You can create a smart group that includes those people and designate it as a mailing list. The group will then be available in CiviMail for sending the newsletter.

As people register for or are marked as having attended an event, they will automatically be added to the smart group and subscribed to the newsletter. Smart groups respect people's subscription preferences: if people unsubscribe from the newsletter, they will be removed from the smart group.

docs.title: Creating smart groups
docs.text:
You can create smart groups from the search results generated by many of CiviCRM's search forms. For example, a smart group of donors who have not yet been sent a thank-you letter can help you manage the work of thanking donors. As you send letters, their recipients will automatically leave the group, keeping the list of people to write to up to date.

You can use advanced search to create this group. If you do not have contributions in your CiviCRM installation, you could try it on the demo site - http://demo.civicrm.org.

  1. Go to Search > Find Contacts > Advanced Search.
  2. Scroll down to the Contributions section.
  3. Check Thank-you date not set? and choose Donation from the financial type drop-down menu.
  4. Click Search at the bottom of the page.
  5. Select all records.
  6. From the Actions drop-down menu, select Group - create smart group.
  7. Give the smart group a name and description. Optionally, designate it as a mailing list and give it a parent group. Click Save Smart Group.

You can also create a smart group from SearchKit. From any search that returns contacts, click +Add on the left hand side and then select Smart Group.

Your smart group will appear in all the usual places where you see groups. Try editing a contact in the group so that they no longer match its criteria. You'll see that they are removed from the group. If the contact is not removed immediately, smart group caching may be turned on; see Smart group caching.

docs.title: Changing criteria for smart groups
docs.text:
You may want to refine the criteria that select contacts for a smart group. For example, you may want a group of all current members to include new members as well. You can do this from the Manage groups screen.

  1. Click Manage Groups. To edit a particular smart group's search criteria, click Settings next to that group.

  1. On the group settings screen, click Edit Smart Group Criteria at bottom left.

  1. On the screen showing the search results, click the bar at the top to display the criteria used to define the smart group. Update the criteria.
  2. Once you're happy with the results, select all records and choose Update Smart Group from the Actions list.

Your smart group is now based on the new criteria.

docs.title: Adding and removing smart group members manually
docs.text:
By default, smart group membership is determined by the criteria in the smart group settings. You can override those criteria by manually adding or removing contacts. To add contacts, use the same workflows you would use for a standard group.

The Groups tab on a contact record does not offer a Remove button for smart groups as it does for standard groups. To remove someone manually:

  1. Go to Contacts > Manage Groups.
  2. Select Contacts in the right-hand column of the chosen group to view its current contacts.
  3. Find and check the box next to the contact you want to remove.
  4. Use the Actions dropdown and select Group - remove contacts.
  5. Confirm the removal. The group record will now appear under Past Groups for that contact.

CiviCRM will override the smart group criteria based on manual additions or removals, even if a contact's eligibility under those criteria changes.

After a contact has been removed from a smart group, an option to Delete their smart group record appears under the Groups tab on their contact record. If you Delete the record, the contact will again be subject to inclusion based on the smart group's criteria.

docs.title: Smart group caching
docs.text:
For performance reasons, smart groups are often cached: the contacts who meet the criteria are saved in memory for a certain amount of time. This speeds things up because CiviCRM does not need to run the search each time you use the group. The improvement may be small for a simple query involving few contacts, but significant or even necessary for a complex query involving many contacts.

The downside is that you may need to wait up to 5 minutes for the query to be updated. Depending on how you use smart groups, this may not be an issue.

The default expiry time for a smart group in newer versions of CiviCRM is 5 minutes. You can adjust the smart group query cache 'timeout'—the amount of time the cache is considered a valid reflection of the smart group—in Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Search Preferences.

When a group is accessed, CiviCRM checks whether its cache is older than the timeout allows. If the timeout has passed, CiviCRM rebuilds the group and resets the timeout to now + cache timeout setting. Setting the timeout to 0 turns off the cache altogether.

docs.title: Everyday petition tasks
docs.text: This page describes everyday tasks for conducting and managing petitions.

docs.title: Manage your petitions
docs.text: To view, manage and edit your petitions, click Campaigns > Dashboard > Petitions.

docs.title: Send out a petition for signing
docs.text:
When your petition is ready, you will want to publicise the URL where people can sign it.

  1. Go to Campaigns > Dashboard > Petitions.
  2. Click More > Sign next to the name of your petition.
  3. You will see your petition; copy the URL and use this link to email to your existing contacts, or add to your web site for individuals to sign your petition.

docs.title: Collect responses online
docs.text:
Once you have publicised the URL for your petition, people will be able to complete the form, answer the questions and submit their response.

After completing the form and clicking Sign the Petition, they will see the following message prompting them to check their email and verify their email address:

docs.title: Collect signatures
docs.text:
To view who has signed the petition:

  1. Click Campaign > Dashboard > Petitions.
  2. Click More > Signatures next to the name of your petition.
  3. You can then choose to view the petition activity for an individual, or select contacts and perform activities such as sending an email to the contacts, or a batch update via profile.

docs.title: Review results with Activity Report
docs.text:
To review all or some of the results from a petition, use the Activity Report.

  1. Go to Reports > Create Reports from Templates > Activity Report.
  2. In the Display Column area, select any fields you would like to view on the report, such as Target Contact Email.
  3. Expand the Petition Questions area and select the criteria you want to see, such as specific responses to a petition question.
  4. Click Preview Report to view the results. You can also export the survey report information to a CSV file to do more detailed reporting of the results.

docs.title: Reports and analysis
docs.text: There are a couple of simple tools to report and analyse petitions.

docs.title: View signatories
docs.text:
To view who has signed the petition:

  1. Click Campaign > Dashboard > Petitions.
  2. Click More > Signatures next to the name of your petition.

docs.title: Review results with activity report
docs.text:
To review all or some of the results from a petition, use the Activity Report.

  1. Go to Reports > Create Reports from Templates > Activity Report.
  2. In Display Column area, select any fields you would like to view on the report, such as Target Contact Email.
  3. Expand the Petition Questions area and select the criteria you want to see, such as specific responses to a petition question.
  4. Click Preview Report to view the results. You can also export the survey report information to a CSV file to do more detailed reporting of the results

docs.title: Set up a petition
docs.text: The CiviCampaign component must be enabled before you can use Petition. See Campaign for information about this.

docs.title: Set CMS permissions
docs.text:
Set the appropriate CMS permissions for the roles that can sign the petition. If you plan to make the petition public, grant permission to anonymous users.

  1. Go to your Drupal, Joomla!, or WordPress Access Control page, which is linked from Administer > Users and Permissions > Permissions (Access Control).
  2. Grant Sign CiviCRM Petition, Profile Create, and Access all Custom Data to the roles you require. For a public petition, grant these permissions to anonymous users and authenticated users ("Guest" in Joomla! or "Subscriber" in WordPress).

docs.title: Create two custom profiles
docs.text:
To create a petition, you must create two custom profiles: one to capture signers' contact information and one to capture their responses to petition questions. The responses to the petition questions are recorded in the activity record of type Petition for each individual who signs the petition.

  1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Profiles and add a profile with the contact fields you want to collect, such as First Name, Last Name, and Email. You may want to make some fields required so you can communicate with signers later. You must collect at least an email address: the Petition feature sends signers an email prompting them to verify their email address, and only verified email addresses can be counted.
  2. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Custom Fields and add a set of custom fields for responses to the petition questions. From the Used For drop down menu, select Activities. For the Activity Type, select Petition Signature.
  3. Under Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Profiles, add a profile for petition responses. Select Activity from the Field Name drop down menu, then select from the custom fields you created.

For both profiles, you may want to select these options in the Advanced Setting area:

  • For Drupal user account registration option?, select No account create option if you do not want all petition signers to have a Drupal account created.
  • For What to do upon duplicate match, select Allow Duplicate Contact to be Created if you do not want anonymous users to update an existing contact record's information. You will then need to periodically dedupe records.

For more about custom field sets, see Creating Custom Fields in Organising Your Data. For more about custom profiles, see Profiles.

docs.title: Create a new petition
docs.text:
Once you have created the two profiles, create the petition:

  1. Go to Campaigns > New Petition and enter the following information:
  2. Petition Title (required): Enter the name of your petition.
  3. Introduction: Enter text describing what your petition is about. Potential signers will read this, so create a message that encourages them to sign.
  4. Campaign: If your petition is one strategy or activity of a campaign, select the name of the campaign.
  5. Contact Profile (required): Select the profile that will collect signers' contact information.
  6. Activity Profile: Select the activity profile that will collect petition responses.
  7. Is Active?: Check this box to make your petition active.
  8. Is Default?: Check this box to make your petition default.
  9. Click Save to save the petition information.

docs.title: What is CiviPetition?
docs.text:
CiviCampaign includes a function for creating petitions to publicly gather responses and information online.

A petition can collect signatures for a cause to present to an elected official or raise awareness of an issue. It can also serve as an online survey: an organization can ask questions, analyse the responses, and use what it learns to build support for its causes. A petition is particularly useful as an online survey when you do not know who will respond—for example, when anyone can submit responses through a petition on your website.

docs.title: Scenario: City Council petition
docs.text:
Townsville Organisation for Tenants (TOFT) wanted to show the Townsville City Council how satisfied or dissatisfied the public was with the Council’s work to provide safe public housing. TOFT created a petition that gathered answers to questions alongside signatures, then presented the results to the City Council.

A TOFT staff member used CiviCampaign to create the petition and emailed it to all existing contacts. She linked the petition to the organization’s web site so the community could respond online. She also worked with the Communications Director on strategies to encourage people to visit the web site and complete the petition.

Respondents could choose to receive ongoing email updates from TOFT about the campaign’s progress throughout the year.

After the petition drive, the staff member compiled the electronic signatures and responses and created reports to analyse the results. TOFT then communicated the results to the City Council. The organization also used the results to shape its messages and tell its story to build interest in the campaign.

docs.title: What you need to know
docs.text: These concepts and questions will help you plan a petition before creating and using it.

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text:
Petitions are a function within the CiviCampaign component of CiviCRM. When an individual responds to a petition, an activity record of the type Petition is created. The record contains the individual's responses to the petition questions.

Petitions are essentially online surveys.

docs.title: Petitions and campaigns
docs.text:
A petition does not have to be connected to a specific campaign. For example, if the Toft Organisation For Tenants (TOFT) used a petition to assess members' satisfaction with TOFT's web site, it probably would not need to connect it to a campaign.

The petition described in the scenario in the previous chapter, however, is part of TOFT's Demand for Better Housing campaign, which includes a survey and other activities. Connecting the petition to the campaign enabled staff to analyse petition responses in the context of the campaign's other strategies and activities.

docs.title: Profiles and custom fields
docs.text:
When a site visitor signs a petition, a contact is saved and an activity is created. Profiles display the fields for each.

The contact profile collects information about the signer, including their email address. Capturing email addresses is necessary to validate and accurately verify submissions and count signatures, especially when you do not want to count multiple submissions from one person. This profile is required and must include an email address field.

The activity profile may collect information specific to the petition signature.

Prepare custom fields to store any questions you want to ask on the petition. Then create the profiles and select them when you create the petition.

To learn more about custom field sets, see Creating Custom Fields in Organising Your Data. To learn how to create a custom profile, see Profiles in Organising your Data.

docs.title: CMS permissions
docs.text: Set permissions to allow specific roles to Sign CiviCRM Petitions. See Set-up for the permissions you'll need to allow.

docs.title: Key questions
docs.text:
Consider these questions about your online strategies before creating a petition:

  • Do you plan to send the petition via email?
  • Will you link to the petition on your website for people to sign?
  • Will you use other social media or offline strategies to drive people to your website to sign the petition?
  • How will you frame your message so that people will want to sign your petition?
  • What do you plan to do with the results from the petition?
  • What follow-up activities are you planning to continue communicating and building a relationship with petition signers?

docs.title: Recording payments
docs.text:
If a donor has chosen to use an offline payment method such as cash or cheque, you will need to manually record the receipt of payment within the pledge.

  1. Look up the Contact in CiviCRM (Search >> Find Contacts).
  2. Go to the Pledges tab within their contact record.
  3. Click the small (view payments) arrow on the far left of the "pledged table" to open up the scheduled pledge payments.
  4. Find the next scheduled Pledge Payment and record the payment as Completed.
  5. You can also Edit the Scheduled Payment to alter either when the payment is due or the amount of the payment.

docs.title: Batch entry of pledges
docs.text:
The Batch Data Entry feature speeds up data entry when you have a lot of pledge payments to record at one time. You enter payments using a grid input screen where you can use the ‘autocopy’ icons at the top of each column to quickly fill in field values. It also lets you verify the total amount and count of items in the batch against the payments recorded on your deposit slip(s).

During batch data entry, you can create new contacts on the fly. You can save the batch and return later to continue entering payments. If you have the appropriate permissions, you can also edit the total amount and count of items in the definition of the batch if needed.

docs.title: 1. Create a new data entry batch
docs.text:
Create a new batch to hold the multiple payments you want to record. From the menu, click on Contributions > Batch Data Entry then select New Data Entry Batch.

Enter the following information:

  • Batch Name: CiviCRM will create a default Batch Name ("Batch N" + open date), which you can edit (required field)
  • Type: Select Payment Type Pledge Payment. This selects the appropriate reserved profile to view in the batch entry grid screen. (not required)
  • Description: A Description of the batch (not required)
  • Number of Items: Total Number of Payment Items in the batch. (required field)
  • Total Amount: Total Amount of all the payment items in the batch. (required field)

You can Edit or Delete Batch information by going back to the Bulk Data Entry screen then clicking on Edit or Delete next to the batch you want.

docs.title: 2. Enter pledge payments (check, cash, EFT, etc.)
docs.text:
When you save information about the new batch, the batch data entry screen shown above will appear. Enter payments on each line as follows:

  • Contact: You can:

    • Start entering the name of an existing contact and CiviCRM will return a list of potential contact names for you to select, OR
    • Create a new contact by clicking the drop-down box for “-create new contact-“ and selecting the type of contact you want to create: New Individual, New Organization, or New Household and enter the information about the contact in the new window that opens.

    Note

    If contact information such as phone number or email address are included in the grid profile, those values will be populated for an existing contact and can be updated as needed.

  • Open Pledges: Click on the down arrow to see all open pledges for the contact. You can assign the payment to any of the open(pending) pledges.

  • Type: This is the Financial Type and pre-fills when an open pledge is selected.
  • Amount: This will pre-fill when you select an open pledge. If you have the appropriate permissions, you can also alter the amount or schedule for the pledge payment. (Click on adjust payment amount next to the Amount field.)
  • (Payment) Status: This defaults to Completed.
  • Received – Date and Time: This pre-fills with the current date but can be edited.
  • Source: Enter text that describes the source of the payment.
  • Paid by: Enter the payment instrument, e.g. cash, check, EFT, etc. (required field)
  • Check Number: fill in if paid by check.
  • Send Receipt: check the box if you want to send a receipt via email
  • Invoice ID
  • Soft Credit
  • Soft Credit Type

docs.title: 3. Validate and process the batch totals or save the batch
docs.text:
You can enter all transactions for the batch in one session, or save the batch and complete the data entry later. To continue entering information into this batch at a later time, click Save & Continue Later.

To find and add/edit more transactions into the batch later, from the menu, click on Contributions > Batch Data Entry then click on Enter Records next to the batch you want. Then continue entering more transactions in the batch.

Once you are finished entering payments into a batch, click Validate & Process the Batch. The status of the batch will be set to Closed and will be available for searches and reporting later.

If the total amount or count of items do not match the values you entered when you created the Batch, you will be alerted when closing if the count or total don't match. In this case, you can either:

  • Override the entered count and total by clicking Ignore Mismatch & Process the Batch? button, in which case the batch values are updated to match the transactions in the batch, and then the status of the batch will be set to Closed, OR
  • Continue entering or editing the payments for the batch, then Validate & Process the Batch again.

docs.title: Canceling pledges
docs.text: Some pledges will not come to fruition. To cancel a pledge, find it through a contact or the Find Pledges search tool, use the more link to the right side of the pledge and click Cancel.

docs.title: Pledge reports
docs.text:
CiviCRM comes with two reports for analysing pledges:

  • Pledge Detail Report shows information per contact, including amount pledged, pledge status, next payment date, balance due, and total amount paid. It is based on the Pledge Report template.
  • Pledged But not Paid lists pledges that are not completed and have a due date in the past. It is based on a template with the same name.

These reports are configured to display particular information. To suit your needs, you can create a new report from the relevant report template. See Reporting Set-up for details.

The Pledge Summary Report template can be used to create a report summarising total pledge amounts by, for example, city or month of initial pledge.

docs.title: Set up pledges on contribution pages
docs.text:
You can let constituents make pledges for future donations through an online CiviContribute donation form. Donors can choose how often to donate—for example, twice a year or twice a month for five months.

Some payment processors will not allow this kind of automation, and payments may arrive in a non-electronic form such as cheques. You can record future income against a current source, such as an event or email campaign, and manually change a payment’s status from 'Pending' to 'Complete' when it arrives if the payment method does not support this. Pledges also provide an automated way to remind donors of their commitment.

For more information about pledges, including how to create them internally on behalf of constituents rather than through an online form, see the chapter Pledges.

docs.title: Enable pledges
docs.text:
After creating a contribution page (see Creating Contribution Pages), edit its settings, go to the Amounts tab, and tick Pledges. The following options will appear.

  • Supported pledge frequencies: Choose whether donors can pledge daily, weekly, monthly or annual donations.
  • Allow frequency intervals: If checked, donors can specify a gap between payments, such as once every 5 days, 5 weeks, 5 months, or five years.
  • Send payment reminder: To send donors a reminder before a scheduled payment is due, enter the number of days beforehand to remind them, for example, via email.
  • Send up to: Specify the maximum number of reminders an individual will receive for one scheduled payment.
  • Send additional reminders: Set the interval between reminders in days, for example, 5 days before the next reminder is sent.
  • Allow other amounts: Check this box to let individuals pledge an amount of their choosing. You can also specify the minimum and maximum payment they can make.
  • Fixed Contribution Options: Use the table below to enter up to ten fixed contribution amounts. These appear as radio button options showing both the label and dollar amount.

When you have finished, choose Save, Save and Done, Save and Next or Cancel.

docs.title: Check pledges
docs.text: Once enabled, the option to make a pledge appears on the online form. Several reports and a dashboard are available to check and monitor current pledges. To access the dashboard, go to Contributions > Pledges > Dashboard.

docs.title: What is CiviPledge?
docs.text:
A pledge is a promise to give a donation at a pre-arranged time in the future, either in full or at regular intervals until a total goal is reached. For example, Sally pledges to give $3000 over five years in regular monthly payments of $50.

In CiviCRM, donors can make a pledge themselves through an online Contribution Form (see the Contributions section), or internal users can make one on their behalf. Payments are handled separately, either manually (e.g. cheque) or automatically through a Payment Processor. The pledge links the individual contributions together.

If a donor misses a payment, the status of the pledge can be updated accordingly. Email reminders can also be set for automatic delivery at specified intervals before payments are due.

docs.title: Enable CiviPledge
docs.text: Before using CiviPledge, you must enable it for your installation if you have not done so already. Go to Administer > System Settings > Enable CiviCRM Components, click the checkbox CiviPledge, and click Save.

docs.title: Create a pledge
docs.text:
To create a New Pledge on behalf of a constituent, navigate to Contributions > Pledges > New Pledge. An individual may also do this themselves through an online contribution form; see the Contributions section.

The options available are:

  • Pledge by Select contact: type the name of an existing contact, or create a new one before setting up the pledge (a new window will open)
  • Total Pledge Amount: enter the total amount to be donated
  • To be paid in: specify the number of instalments and time period for payment, if greater than one
  • Payments are due on the: choose the day on which a payment is due during that instalment cycle (e.g. the second day of the week/month/year)
  • Pledge Made: select the date on which the pledge was promised
  • Payments Start: set the date the scheduled payments will start
  • Send Acknowledgment?: if outgoing mail is configured, and an email address is available for that contact, check this box to send a notification email
  • Acknowledgement Date: the date the individual was notified of the pledge's creation (automatically populated if an email was sent)
  • Financial Type: choose the Financial Type of the contribution (e.g. Donation or Event Fee) to denote what the pledged money is meant for
  • Campaign: if available, you may assign the Pledge to a Campaign if the money is intended to go towards that fundraising effort
  • Self-service Payments Page: give donors the ability to make a payment online by selecting an online Contribution Form to collect the money through
  • Honoree information: you may also enter Honoree information if the individual elects to dedicate the pledge to someone, and set payment reminders

docs.title: Payment reminders
docs.text:
One or more payment reminders can be emailed to the donor before the scheduled payment date. If a 'Self-service Payments Page' has been selected (see below), the reminder will include a link for the contributor to make their payment online.

For reminders to be sent:

  1. The Process Pledges (process_pledge) scheduled job must be enabled to update pledge payment statuses and send payment reminders. Alternatively, a cron job can be scheduled to run this specific task apart from other scheduled jobs. Refer to the Scheduled Jobs chapter for more information.
  2. The donor must have a valid email address and must not have the "Do Not Email" flag checked.

Once these prerequisites have been met, you can choose the payment reminder schedule for an individual when creating a New Pledge. The settings are:

  • Send Initial Reminder: enter the number of days, prior to the payment date, that a reminder will be sent
  • Send up to: specify the maximum number of reminders an individual will receive for one scheduled payment
  • Send additional reminders: set the interval between reminders by the number of days, e.g. 5 days before the next reminder is sent

docs.title: Self-service payments
docs.text: A donor can be given the option to make a scheduled payment online if a Contribution Page (with Payment Processor) has been created. To do this, select a Contribution Page from the drop-down menu 'Self-service Payments Page' when creating a New Pledge. If reminders have been enabled for the pledge, a link to this page will be included in the body of the emails.

docs.title: Find pledges
docs.text:
To search for existing Pledges, go to Contributions > Pledges > Find Pledges. You may search by Pledger Name, Email Address, or any discrete feature of the Pledges themselves (e.g. Payment Start Date, Pledge Status and Honoree information).

The search results page displays a summary of the Pledges found. View, Edit and Delete options are available for each record at the end of the rows. If the Status of a Pledge is 'in progress' or 'Pending', there is also an option to Cancel the Pledge.

docs.title: View the pledges dashboard
docs.text: You can view a list of recent Pledges and a summary table of Pledges recorded over the current month and past year on the pledges dashboard. This can be reached through the Contributions menu: Contributions > Pledges > Dashboard.

docs.title: Everyday tasks
docs.text: This chapter assumes that CiviReport is already configured and you are a user wanting to access reports that have been configured for you. If you want to learn more about how to set up and configure reports, read the section on setting up CiviReport.

docs.title: Viewing reports
docs.text:
To view a report:

  1. Go to Reports.
  2. Select the relevant report type.
  3. Identify the report you wish to view. Click on View Results to view the report results using the preset criteria. Click on the report name to go to the criteria settings.

Reports can also be configured to be directly accessible from navigation menus. For example, an event report can be configured to appear in the Events menu.

When you open a report, it will appear on screen as a table. Some reports can also be viewed as a bar or pie chart. When this is the case, a dropdown menu will allow you to select the format you want.

The appropriate report should then be displayed.

As well as viewing reports on screen, you can create a PDF version of either tables or graphs, suitable for printing or emailing.

If you want to perform further calculations on your report data, you can output the data as comma separated variable (CSV) for import into a spreadsheet by clicking Export to CSV.

If you have the appropriate permissions, you will be able to adjust the report criteria and settings when you view the report. Read Set-up for detailed information about how to do this.

docs.title: Reports on your dashboard
docs.text:
Reports can be configured to appear on your dashboard (the first page you see when you log in to CiviCRM). You can configure this yourself, although not all reports may be available to put on your dashboard.

To display specific reports on your dashboard:

  1. From your dashboard, click on Configure Your Dashboard.
  2. Select a report from the list of available reports.
  3. Drag the report onto your dashboard.

docs.title: Adding report results to a group
docs.text: Sometimes it is useful to add contacts returned in a report to a group. This functionality isn't available in all reports but where it is, you can choose the group you want to add the contacts to from the dropdown menu as shown below.

docs.title: External reporting
docs.text:
Reporting within CiviCRM generally assumes that:

  • You want to report directly on your "production" CiviCRM database with real-time data.
  • You only want to report on data in CiviCRM, rather than data from other applications or combined data from many applications.

You can also create reports, dashboards, or data transformations outside CiviCRM using tools such as Metabase, Tableau, Power BI, RapidMiner, and Pentaho. These tools can access the CiviCRM database through a direct link to the MySQL or Maria database, or potentially through the CiviCRM API.

How to use these tools is outside the scope of this document. If your organization does not have the necessary skills, contact your CiviCRM experts or whoever supports you with CiviCRM or reporting.

docs.title: Set up CiviReports
docs.text:
This page describes how to create a report from a template and make it available to users. It assumes you understand why you want to use CiviReport and that a supplied CiviCRM report template can produce the report you need.

If the template you need does not exist, you or your developer should refer to creating custom reports in the Developer Guide for information about creating new templates.

docs.title: Choose a report template
docs.text:
Report templates are general reports that you can customise to create specific report instances. You can then make those instances available to users.

The Create new report from templates page is in the Administer > CiviReport menu. It lists available templates by component, with a brief description of each template’s intended scenario. If a template already has report instances, you’ll see a link to view Existing Reports.

Click a report template name to open its configuration screen. Configuring a report has two steps:

  1. Select your report criteria to decide what information the report displays.
  2. Define the report settings to choose a title, set permissions and add the report to a menu. The report settings tabs do not appear until you have previewed the report.

docs.title: Select report criteria
docs.text:
When you create a report, two or more tabs let you define the information it displays. The available tabs depend on the template. The most common are:

  • Columns (all reports)
  • Grouping (summary reports)
  • Sorting (detail reports)
  • Filters (all reports)

The options within these tabs vary by report.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Use the check boxes to select the data displayed for each record. In most reports, at least one display column is required and cannot be unselected. For example, Contact Name and Membership Type are required fields in the membership detail report.

docs.title: Grouping
docs.text:
Grouping is not available in every report. It is useful for summarising data instead of displaying each individual row, or for comparing different types of data. For example, you can compare donations per year.

You can specify more than one grouping criteria. Results will then be nested based on both groupings. Not all combinations will make sense for your data, so you may need to experiment with Group By Columns.

Some Groups By Columns interact with Display Columns and cannot be selected at the same time. The system will warn you if you make an invalid selection.

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text: Sorting is not available in every report, but can be useful in "detail" reports, as shown below.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text: Filters specify which records to include. For example, a Membership Detail report without filters shows all membership records. You could filter it to show members of a specific membership type who joined last year. Most filters are self-explanatory; the date range filter is described below.

docs.title: The date range filter
docs.text:
Most reports have a date range filter. You can use:

  • An absolute date range, such as "1st Jan 2010" to "31 July 2010".
  • A relative date range, such as "Previous Year".

Relative date ranges are useful for reports you run regularly:

  • This year gives all records from the start of the current year.
  • Previous quarter gives all records from the previous quarter.
  • Last 12 months gives all records between one year earlier than today's date and today.

The "Last ..." ranges are particularly useful with Group By Columns. Combining Ending Year with Group By Month gives a report that summarises data by month for the previous 12 months.

The report below shows the total amount of contributions received in the past 12 months, as well as each month's total.

Once you have selected your criteria, click Preview Report. The report settings tabs will then be visible. If the results are not what you wanted, return to the appropriate tab and modify the criteria. You may need to make several modifications.

docs.title: Define report settings
docs.text:
When you are happy with the criteria, save them as a new report so that it can be run again. You must preview the report before the settings tabs become visible.

  1. On the Title and Format tab, give the report a title and description that help others understand its use, such as "Student members joined so far this year".

A standard header and footer are included with each report and appear at the beginning and end of PDF or downloaded versions. They are written in HTML. To display the actual report title, replace "CiviCRM Report" between < title> and < /title>. You can include a logo by adding an < img> tag. You can also change the printed report’s appearance by including a custom CSS file instead of print.css.

  1. On the Email Delivery tab, fill in the Subject, To and CC fields in the Email Delivery Settings to have the report emailed to you or someone else regularly. You can enter one or more email addresses in the To and CC fields; separate multiple addresses with commas.

To send report emails, you must also enable the Mail Reports (mail_report) scheduled job. Alternatively, a cron job can run this task separately from other scheduled jobs. Specify the report instance and, optionally, its format in the scheduled job configuration. See Scheduled Jobs for more information.

  1. On the Access tab, choose where else the report appears in the navigation menu. All reports are included in Report > Report listing. Checking Include Report in Navigation Menu? displays the Parent Menu field, where you can select the parent menu for a second link to the report.

That link can open either "View Results" or "Show Criteria". "View Results" opens the results page and is appropriate, for example, for a report using a relative date filter such as "Number of new contributors last calendar month". "Show Criteria" lets you change the criteria before running the report.

You can also use the Access tab to set permissions to view or edit individual reports. This can simplify the interface for junior users and restrict sensitive reports. For example, you might select "access CiviContribute" for a contribution report so that only people who can see contribution data can access it.

Alternatively, you can limit access to particular ACL role(s). Refer to Permissions and Access Control in the Initial Set Up chapter.

A Reserved Report can only be altered by someone with the Administer Reserved Reports permission.

Checking Available for Dashboard? lets users with appropriate permissions add the report to their dashboard by clicking Configure Your Dashboard on their dashboard.

Once the criteria and settings are correct, click Create Report. The report will appear in Reports > All Reports and in any navigation menu you defined on the Access tab.

docs.title: Edit or copy an existing report
docs.text:
To permanently change an existing report’s criteria, open the report, make the changes and click Update Report.

You can also create reports with the same columns but different filters. For example, an events manager might need an Event Income Summary report for all events, while a fundraising manager might have access only to a report for Fundraiser events. Open the initial report, change its filtering criteria and click Save a Copy.... You will be prompted for a title and description for the new report.

docs.title: CiviReport permissions
docs.text:
Four permissions are specifically associated with reports:

  • CiviReport: access CiviReport — The user can view the CiviReport menu, but can view only reports set with the access CiviReport permission.
  • CiviReport: access Report Criteria — The user can change report search criteria.
  • CiviReport: administer reserved reports — The user can edit all reserved reports.
  • CiviReport: administer reports — The user can manage report templates.

docs.title: What is CiviReport?
docs.text:
Reporting helps your organisation evaluate its impact and achieve its mission. Funders or other stakeholders may require reports. CiviReport lets you create, run and schedule reports based on the data CiviCRM holds about your contacts and their interactions with your organisation.

Reports query the database using the criteria and fields available in a report template. You can view a report on the page when you run it, display it as a dashlet on the dashboard, or receive it by scheduled email. An emailed report can include a CSV file or PDF.

docs.title: Scenario: a simple report to help with fundraising
docs.text:
1two3, a support organisation for street workers, has launched a capital campaign to raise money for a new shelter. Anne, the development director, wants to contact donors who made a large donation last year but have not given this year.

Anne creates an instance of the LYBUNT report (“Last year but unfortunately not this”) and filters it to show people who gave more than €500 last year. She runs the report and uses the Add to Group button to put these donors in a new group. She can then email everyone in the group about the capital campaign.

She also adds the report to her CiviCRM Dashboard to review progress in getting these prior donors to contribute. Anyone who donates automatically drops off the list because they no longer meet the criteria. The people remaining in the dashlet can be contacted by phone or through other personalised follow-up.

docs.title: Scenario: a regular financial report
docs.text:
WAM is an academic membership organisation with about 1,500 members. Members renew online and pay either online by card or offline by direct debit. Mark, the finance officer, needs several reports to track incoming money. Automating these reports was a key reason for implementing CiviCRM.
