Mark receives the regular reports by email with CSV attachments. He imports the details into either the organisation’s accounting software or its online banking interface. WAM’s requirements were fairly complex, so some custom report templates were needed alongside the standard ones.

Every Monday morning, Mark receives a list of all completed online payments from the previous week to import into Sage. The report includes each payment’s amount and time, what it was for (membership or event), and a reference ID that links it back to the record in CiviCRM.

At the end of each month, he receives a list of members who pay by direct debit and whose memberships are due to expire the following month. He imports part of the list into the online banking interface to set up direct debit payments for those renewals.

These email reports save Mark several hours a month, allowing him to focus on other issues affecting the management of WAM’s financial resources.

docs.title: Scenario: determining total contributions for a household
docs.text:
A non-profit organisation in Ohio keeps records of individuals organised by household. For example, a husband may have attended several paid events while his wife has registered for other events and made separate donations.

Staff want to see the total contributions received from everyone in a household. If someone calls to ask about a donation or event payment made by another family member, staff can run the Donation Summary Report (Household) using the household’s name. The report gives them the contributions and related information they need to answer the caller’s questions.

docs.title: Popular extensions
docs.text:
These are widely used extensions in the relevant category of the official CiviCRM Extensions Directory. Usage is a popularity signal, not a compatibility or suitability guarantee.

  • Extended Reports — reported usage: 2,399
  • SearchKit Tokens — reported usage: 1,733
  • Chart Kit — reported usage: 1,187
  • Export to native Excel — reported usage: 959
  • Civisualize — reported usage: 718

All extensions for this component

Check development status, current CiviCRM compatibility, CMS requirements, and release notes before installation.

Usage snapshot reviewed: 2026-10-13.

docs.title: What you need to know about CiviReport
docs.text:
This page explains ideas that are useful when planning your use of CiviReport. System administrators should read it before configuring CiviReport for daily use. It is also useful for anyone who wants to understand the thinking behind CiviReport. If you only want to use reports already configured by your administrator, you can skip it.

CiviReport can support organisational planning and analysis of membership or donor development. It can produce tabular or graphical output, and reports can be set up to email specific people on a schedule.

The questions an organisation might ask about its data are almost unlimited. CiviCRM aims to cover 90% of scenarios while allowing administrators and developers to extend the system for the remaining 10%.

docs.title: Report templates
docs.text:
A report template is the basis for creating any number of reports. CiviCRM includes predefined report templates for creating specific reports. For example, the Membership Report(Detail) template can be used to create one report showing student members who joined your organisation in the past quarter and another showing memberships cancelled this year.

These templates address basic needs of non-profits and organisations, and future versions of CiviCRM are likely to include more. You can create templates for your organisation’s requirements and contribute them to the CiviCRM community for others with the same reporting needs. Writing a new report template requires PHP and SQL skills. See the Developer Guide for details.

docs.title: Reports vs. searches
docs.text:
CiviCRM’s inbuilt search functionality covers most scenarios. CiviReport helps users display complex information about their data and present answers to questions in accessible ways. It is useful when you need to ask the same question, or similar questions, repeatedly.

The current report interface does not support most common batch actions, such as Update via Batch Profile and Smart Group creation. If you want to perform an action against a result set, use search rather than a report.

Reports can be more flexible than searches in some cases, and each has its own features. For example, reports let you change the columns displayed. In summary reports, you can order by whichever display results you choose.

docs.title: Report options
docs.text:
• Run the report: Use Print Report to view it in a browser, generate a PDF, or Export to CSV. Each option runs the report once when you hit the button and lets you work with the result.
  • Dashlet: If you make a report Available for Dashboard, users with appropriate permissions can add it to their dashboard. This is useful for information they want to see regularly, such as new members or donations this month. The report runs every time the dashboard loads.
  • Email: Schedule a regular email of a report. For example, a finance office could receive a monthly report of event fees received, or a membership administrator could receive a weekly report of overdue renewals.

docs.title: Detail and summary reports
docs.text: Reports often come in pairs: one shows a summary and the other shows detail. They can be linked so users can see information at a glance and drill down into a report for more detail.

docs.title: Questions to consider
docs.text:
• Should you use CiviReport for this task, or would a search work better?
  • What reports are available? The list is constantly growing. For a complete list available in your version, with explanations of how to use them, see Create reports from templates in the Reports dropdown menu.
  • What do you want to ask about your data? For example, how many new members joined in a certain period, or how much money was collected during a fundraising campaign?
  • What fields do you need to include?
  • Does the report provide enough options, or will you need to analyse the results further in a spreadsheet?
  • Is this a one-off report, or will you run it regularly? Could you make a report template to streamline future reports?
  • Who needs to see the report? Does it contain sensitive information that should be available only to privileged users, or useful daily updates for everyone?

Details of available report templates and comparisons with searches appear for each component throughout the rest of this book. Refer to the relevant section for more about component-specific reports.

docs.title: Adding new relative date filters
docs.text:
The code for some of the patterns supports the addition of more filters (via the api or the URL civicrm/admin/options/relative_date_filters).

Making other patterns more flexible is generally 'patch-welcome'—the hardest part is the non-code part: figuring out what the definition is and how it relates to the other patterns.

docs.title: ending
docs.text:
The trick to the ending prefix is that it is a 'count backwards from now' type filter. If you are in the middle of a month and you use ending, it will start from the middle of the relevant month (if it's the 15th today then it would start from the 16th of the month).

Additional filters can be added with the syntax below, where 3 can be any number you choose:

  • ending_3.day - Last 3 days, including today
  • ending_3.week - Last 3 weeks, including today, equivalent to ending_21.day
  • ending_3.month - Last 3 months, including today, e.g if today is 25 Dec 2021 then from 26 Sep 2021)
  • ending_3.quarter - Last 3 quarters, including today - equivalent to ending_9.month
  • ending_3.year - Last 3 years, including today (e.g if today is 25 Dec 2021 then from 26 Dec 2018)

docs.title: this
docs.text:
The this term works in full date units—for example, this_3.year starts from 1 Jan and ends on 31 December. So if today is 25 December 2021 then this_3.year runs from 1 Jan 2019 to 31 December 2021.

  • this_3.day - Last 3 days, including today - equivalent to ending_3.day
  • this_3.week - From start of two weeks ago to end of this week (total of 3)
  • this_3.month - From start of two months ago to end of this month (total of 3)
  • this_3.quarter - From start of two quarters ago to end of this quarter (total of 3)
  • this_3.year - From start of two years ago to end of this year (total of 3)
  • this_3.fiscal_year - From start of 2 fiscal years ago to end of this fiscal year (total of 3 years)
