docs.title: Search result actions
docs.text:
You can take actions directly from search results. The available “Action” options depend on the type of information you searched for: a Contact search, for example, has different options from a Contribution search.

Whether you search for contacts or contact data using Quick Search, Advanced Search, SearchKit, or Find Contacts, you must select one or more results before options under “Action” become selectable.

docs.title: Contact search actions
docs.text:
The following “Action” options appear for Contact entity searches.

  • Add activity - Add an Activity to the selected contact records.
  • Communication preferences - alter - Modify preferences by adding or removing options. For example, if “No bulk emails (User Opt Out)” is selected, the contact will be automatically excluded from future email communications out of CiviCRM. Learn more about Communication Preferences.

  • Dedupe - Merge 2 Contacts - In addition to merging the contact data (address, phone, email) of two contacts, you may choose to move all or some of the related activity records (groups, contributions, memberships, etc.). This option will be grayed out and not selectable if more than two contacts are selected. Learn more about Deduping and Merging Contacts.
  • Delete Contacts - This will not permanently delete the contacts from CiviCRM. Should you delete contacts in error, they can be restored by searching for contacts in the trash via Advanced Search. Learn more about deleting and restoring contacts.
  • Download Spreadsheet - Select the file format of the data. The download includes the columns enabled in your Search.

  • Email - schedule/send via CiviMail - Compose and send a mass-mailing to the 2 or more selected contacts. You will be able to add or exclude additional groups of contacts in the next step. Learn more about CiviMail.
  • Email - send now (to 50 or less) - Emails will not be sent to contacts who have communication preferences set to “Do Not Email” or do not have a valid email address on file.
  • Email - unhold addresses - When an email is on Hold, no future emails will be sent to it unless someone fixes it and removes the hold. This action allows you to remove the Hold from email addresses in bulk.
  • Export Contacts - Export a predefined set of fields (export mapping), or create your own export mapping and save it for reuse. The software exports to CSV format, which can be easily opened in standard spreadsheet software or directly used for mail merges. Learn more about Exporting Contacts.
  • Group - add contacts - Add contacts to an existing group or create a new group. Learn more about Groups.
  • Group - remove contacts - Select from your list of existing groups to remove contacts in bulk.
  • Mailing labels - print - Select a label format from the dropdown list to generate labels for a bulk print communication directly from the system. Learn more about postal mailings in CiviCRM.
  • Print/merge document - Create merge letters directly from the interface. You can insert tokens representing fields in the database into your letter, optionally save it as a template, and output it to PDF, HTML, Word (.docx), or Open Document (.odt) format. Learn more about Print/Merge Documents.
  • Profile Update - To update multiple contacts, you must select contacts of the same basic type (e.g. all Individuals OR all Organizations...).
  • Tag - Add/Remove Tags - New tags cannot be created from this action. You can select from existing tags in the system. Learn more about Tags.
  • Update Contacts - Select the data field(s) you’d like to update for all contacts selected. These changes will apply to all contacts selected.

docs.title: Contribution search actions
docs.text:
The following “Action” options appear for Contribution entity searches.

  • Delete contributions - The delete operation cannot be undone and will delete all transactions and activity associated with the contributions selected.
  • Email - send now (to 50 or less) - As long as you are contacting fewer than 50 recipients and you don't need to track whether recipients opened the email or clicked on any links, the Send Email action is quicker and easier than sending a mass mailing in CiviMail. Learn more about small group emails.
  • Export contributions - Export a predefined set of fields (export mapping), or create your own export mapping and save it for reuse. The software exports to CSV format, which can be easily opened in standard spreadsheet software or directly used for mail merges.
  • Printing selected rows - You must have a printer connected to your device. This option prints the selected search results.
  • Receipts - print or email - You may choose to email receipts to contributors OR download a PDF file containing one receipt per page to your local computer by clicking Process Receipt(s).

  • Record payments for contributions - This option will only work if you select contributions with Pending status. If the selected contributions have a status other than Pending, an error message will appear in the upper-right of the screen.

  • Thank-you letters - print or email - Email thank you letters directly from CiviCRM or create pdf merge letters for the selected contacts. Learn more about Print/Merge Documents.
  • Update multiple contributions - You will need to create a Profile containing the Contribution fields you want to edit before you can use Update multiple contributions. Navigate to Administer CiviCRM > Customize Data and Screens > CiviCRM Profile to configure a Profile. Learn more about using Profiles for updating information.

docs.title: Participant search actions
docs.text:
The following “Action” options appear for Participant entity searches.

  • Cancel registration - Set the participant’s status to Canceled.
  • Delete participants from event - This delete operation cannot be undone and will delete all transactions and activity associated with the selected participations. This action will not delete the participant’s contact record.
  • Email - send now (to 50 or less) - As long as you are contacting fewer than 50 recipients and you don't need to track whether recipients opened the email or clicked on any links, the Send Email action is quicker and easier than sending a mass mailing in CiviMail. Learn more about small group emails.
  • Export participants - Export a predefined set of fields (export mapping), or create your own export mapping and save it for reuse. The software exports to CSV format, which can be easily opened in standard spreadsheet software or directly used for mail merges.
  • Group - add contacts - Add contacts to an existing group or create a new group. Learn more about Groups.
  • Group - create smart group - Smart groups are saved search results based on defined criteria, similar to a query. The system reruns the query using those criteria each time you open the smart group. This is particularly helpful for complex search criteria that you need to view regularly. Even if only a few contacts have been selected from the search results, all contacts that meet the criteria specified will be in the group. Learn more about Smart Groups.
  • Name badges print - Select the type of badge you require and a printable PDF will be generated with the names of the selected participants. Learn more about Event Badges.
  • PDF letter - print for participants - Create merge letters directly from the interface. You can insert tokens representing fields in the database into your letter, optionally save it as a template, and output it to PDF, HTML, Word (.docx), or Open Document (.odt) format. Learn more about Print/Merge documents.
  • Participant status - change - When using this feature emails will be sent to participants when the status is changed from one which belongs to the pending class (eg Pending (pay later), Pending from approval) to either Registered or Attended(positive class). Emails will also be sent if the status is changed to Expired or Canceled.
  • Print selected rows - Print what is shown on the screen for the rows you have selected.
  • Update multiple participants - Edit multiple fields for multiple participants in a table grid layout. You must create the profile set you wish to use before implementing this action. Learn more about using Profiles for updating information.

docs.title: Activities search actions
docs.text:
The following “Action” options appear for Activity entity searches.

  • Delete activities - This delete operation cannot be undone.
  • Email - send now (to 50 or less) - As long as you are contacting fewer than 50 recipients and you don't need to track whether recipients opened the email or clicked on any links, the Send Email action is quicker and easier than sending a mass mailing in CiviMail. Learn more about small group emails.
  • Export activities - Export a predefined set of fields (export mapping), or create your own export mapping and save it for reuse. The software exports to CSV format, which can be easily opened in standard spreadsheet software or directly used for mail merges.
  • Print selected rows - Print what is shown on the screen for the rows you have selected.
  • Print/merge Document - Create merge letters directly from the interface. You can insert tokens representing fields in the database into your letter, optionally save it as a template, and output it to PDF, HTML, Word (.docx), or Open Document (.odt) format. Learn more about Print/Merge documents.
  • Tag - add to activities - Add one or multiple tags to Activity records.
  • Tag - remove from activities - Remove one or more tags from Activity records.
  • Update multiple activities - To use this action, you will first need to create a Profile containing the Activity fields you want to edit. Learn more about using Profiles to update multiple activity records.

docs.title: Member search actions
docs.text:
The following “Action” options appear for Member entity searches.

  • Delete Memberships - This delete operation cannot be undone and will delete all transactions and activity associated with the memberships selected.
  • Email - send now (to 50 or less) - As long as you are contacting fewer than 50 recipients and you don't need to track whether recipients opened the email or clicked on any links, the Send Email action is quicker and easier than sending a mass mailing in CiviMail. Learn more about small group emails.
  • Export members - Export a predefined set of fields (export mapping), or create your own export mapping and save it for reuse. The software exports to CSV format, which can be easily opened in standard spreadsheet software or directly used for mail merges.
  • Group - create smart group - Create a saved search query that can be used for mailings or as a filter in future searches or reports. Even if only a few contacts have been selected from the search results, all contacts that meet the criteria specified will be in the group. Learn more about Smart Groups.
  • Mailing labels - print - Select a label format from the dropdown list to generate labels for a bulk print communication directly from the system. Learn more about postal mailings in CiviCRM.
  • Print selected rows - Print what is shown on the screen for the rows you have selected.
  • Print/merge document for memberships - Create merge letters directly from the interface. You can insert tokens representing fields in the database into your letter, optionally save it as a template, and output it to PDF, HTML, Word (.docx), or Open Document (.odt) format. Learn more about Print/Merge documents.
  • Update multiple memberships - To use this feature, you will first need to create a Profile containing the Membership fields you want to edit. Learn more about using Profiles to update membership information.

docs.title: URL filter support in searches
docs.text:
In some cases, you can bookmark search URLs with parameters to revisit searches quickly. This page covers Advanced Search and component searches, such as 'Find Contributions'. URL filtering for SearchKit is discussed on the SearchKit interface page. and the FormBuilder form page.

To construct a parameterised URL:

  1. Ensure the URL contains 'reset=1&force=1' after the question mark.
  2. Add supported parameters.

Date/Time Parameters

Date/time parameters require that, either, the time component is omitted entirely 20200101 or specified with a full six digit time 20200101235959

For example, the following URL works on Drupal (with Clean URL support) to find contributions made by a person with a name like Bob, a contribution source like dad, and a contribution date on or before 01 Jan 2018:

civicrm/contribute/search?reset=1&reset=1&force=1&sort_name=bob&receive_date_high=20180101&contribution_source=dad

The following parameters work in a standardised way for contribution searches:

Field Example Comments Min version (where known) sort_name sort_name=bob Sort name is like bob% or %bob% depending on your site config * contribution_source contribution_source=dad Contribution source like %dad% or 'dad%' * cancel_reason cancel_reason=dunno Contribution source like %dunno% or dunno% * invoice_number invoice_number_reason=xyz Invoice Number like %xyz% or xyz% * contribution_page_id contribution_page_id=1 5.21 PR receive_date_high receive_date_high=20180101132323 Contribution received on or before 01 Jan 2018, 1.23 pm receive_date_low receive_date_low=20161001 Contribution received on or after 01 Oct 2016 receive_date_relative receive_date_relative=this.year Contribution received this year contribution_cancel_date_high contribution_cancel_date_high=20180101132323 Contribution cancelled on or before 01 Jan 2018, 1.23 pm contribution_cancel_date_low contribution_cancel_date_low=20161001 Contribution cancelled on or after 01 Oct 2016 contribution_cancel_date_relative contribution_cancel_date_relative=this.year Contribution cancelled this year event_high event_high=20190101000000 Event end date on or before 1 January 2019 5.21 PR event_low event_low=20190101000000 Event Start date on or after 1 January 2019 5.21 PR event_relative event_relative=this.year Event Start Date on or after ths start of this year and the event end date on or before the end of the year 5.21 PR participant_registration_date_high participant_registration_date_high=20190101000000 Participant Registration Date on or before 1 January 2019 5.21 PR participant_registration_date_low participant_registration_date_low=20190101000000 Participant Registration date on or after 1 January 2019 5.21 PR participant_registration_date_relative participant_registration__date_relative=this.year Participant Registration Date on or after ths start of this year and the event end date on or before the end of the year 5.21 PR participant_status_id participant_status_id=1,2 Participant Status in Registered and Pending Pay Later 5.21 PR participant_role_id participant_role_id=1,2 Participant Role IN (Attendee, Host) 5.21 PR case_start_date_high case_start_date_high=20190101000000 Case Start Date on or before 1 January 2019 5.21 PR case_start_date_low case_start_date_low=20190101000000 Case Start Date on or after 1 January 2019 5.21 PR case_start_date_relative case_start_date_relative=this.year Case Start Date on or after the start of this year and on or before the end of the calendar year 5.21 PR case_end_date_high case_end_date_high=20190101000000 Case End Date on or before 1 January 2019 5.21 PR case_end_date_low case_end_date_low=20190101000000 Case End Date on or after 1 January 2019 5.21 PR case_end_date_relative case_end_date_relative=this.year Case End Date on or after the start of this year and on or before the end of the calendar year 5.21 PR case_type_id case_type_id=1,2 Case Type is one of Housing Support or Adult Care Support 5.21 PR case_status_id case_status_id=1 Case Status is Opened 5.21 PR case_subject case_subject=test Case subject like %test% 5.21 PR case_deleted case_deleted=1 Case is deleted 5.21 PR case_id case_id=1 Case id = 1 5.21 PR case_owner case_owner=2 Only My Cases 5.21 PR case_tags case_tags=1,2 Case Tags in (1,2) 5.21 PR

* Whether text fields search for LIKE %dad% or LIKE dad% depends on the site wide setting 'Automatic Wildcard' under Administer CiviCRM -> Customize Data and Screens -> Search Preferences. For large sites turning this off gives a significant performance improvement but it means that searching for 'dad' will return 'daddy' but not 'grandad'.

docs.title: Date formats
docs.text:
In general, there are two types of date formats to use:

  1. _high or _low fields take an 8- or 14-digit number representing Year, Month, Day and, optionally, Hour, Minute and Second. For example, 20180921235959 means 21 September 2018 at 23 hours, 59 minutes and 59 seconds. Leaving off 235959 means zero o’clock—that is, midnight.
  2. Relative date fields. See the list.

docs.title: Search for information in CiviCRM
docs.text: CiviCRM offers several ways to find information you have stored. Begin with Quick search, Advanced Search, and component searches. For more advanced searches, consider SearchKit reports and custom searches.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This page covers:

  • Quick search: Find contacts quickly.
  • Advanced search: Search contacts using a wide range of criteria.
  • Full-text search: Search text fields in the database.
  • Component searches: Search records associated with components, such as events, memberships, cases, and contributions.
  • Custom searches: Use searches supplied by CiviCRM core or by your extensions.
  • Search actions: Act on search results or, sometimes, report results. See Search Result Actions for the primary actions available for the selected entity.
  • The contact summary pop-up: View or change information shown when you hover over a contact icon in search results.
  • Wildcards: Use % or %_% in searches.
  • Case sensitivity: Understand how searches handle upper- and lowercase characters.
  • Default number of rows: See how many results appear and how to change that number.
  • SearchKit: Follow the link to SearchKit.

docs.title: Searching and reporting
docs.text:
There are three main reasons to search:

  • Find a specific contact. The Quick search box can find contacts by name, email address, or various other characteristics.
  • Find contacts who meet criteria so you can act on their records. For example, find advisory group contacts to invite to a meeting, contacts whose memberships have recently expired to send renewal reminders, or contacts under 25 in a specific location to email about a nearby event.
  • Produce an ad-hoc report.

Searching can be useful for ad-hoc reporting, but you cannot group results by particular criteria, summarize them, or easily produce graphs of them. For more advanced reporting, see CiviReport.

docs.title: Quick search
docs.text:
To find a specific contact, use the Quick search box in the navigation menu at the top left of the screen. You can search by several criteria. To modify the available criteria, go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Search Preferences. The Search Preferences page has options to hide basic contact fields that are not normally used in Quick search and to add custom field options.

Click in the Quick search box and start typing to use the default Name/Email search. Alternatively, click again to show other criteria in a dropdown list. Matching contacts appear below the box.

For example, if you search by Name/Email and have left automatic wildcard enabled in Search Preferences, entering “peter” finds:

  • People whose first or last name is Peter.
  • People with Peter elsewhere in their name, such as MaryPeterson.
  • People with Peter in their email address, such as bluepeter@gmail.com.
  • Organisations with Peter in their name, such as Alpeter Community Centre.

Often, the first few letters of a name are enough. If you do not see the contact, type more characters to refine the search, or press Return to convert it into an Advanced Search.

Quick search displays up to 10 results by default. To change this number, change Autocomplete Results on the Search Preferences screen.

CiviCRM also allows a nickname to be collected when entering a new contact. For example, “Joe” can be a nickname for “Joseph,” and “IBM” can be a nickname for “International Business Machines.” When you first install CiviCRM, searching for “Joe” will find “Joseph,” and searching for “IBM” will find “International Business Machines.”

You can change this behavior on the Search Preferences screen by changing Include Nickname to yes.

Note

If you search by phone, enter the digits without formatting. The phone search uses a field containing only digits, with all non-numeric characters stripped out.

Tip

To search by first and last name, use “Lastname, Firstname,” not “Firstname Lastname.” For example, use “Peterson, Mary,” not “Mary Peterson.”

docs.title: Advanced search
docs.text:
Advanced search lets you search across the information you have about contacts. You could find “all contacts in Venezuela” or “all advisory group members.” If you specify two or more categories of information, the search displays contacts matching all the categories—for example, advisory group members in Venezuela.

Open Search > Advanced Search from the navigation menu. Search criteria are grouped by type of data, such as addresses, notes, Contributions, and Events. Each group appears as a blue bar called an “accordion,” which expands when clicked. To search for people aged 16 to 18, for example, open Demographics and specify a birth date range.

docs.title: Display settings for results
docs.text: Advanced Search returns Contact records by default. To return another record type, select it from Display Results As. For example, you could search for Membership renewal activities from last week and display the results as Memberships. You could then export name, address, and Membership expiration date to create and post membership cards.

docs.title: Views for display contacts
docs.text:
You can change the columns shown in Advanced search results. The default columns are Name, Street Address, City, State, Postal Code, Country, Email, and Phone.

To use different columns, create a Profile with the Search Views option selected. Set its fields to “Expose Publicly and for Listings” visibility and mark them as Results Columns. For example, to show Gender and Date of Birth but not Country, create a profile with birth date, gender, and address fields.

For more information about creating Profiles, see Profiles in Organising Your Data. You can combine a search view with the “Batch Update via Profile” action to view and update a chosen set of fields across multiple contact records.

docs.title: Search settings
docs.text:
Search Operator determines whether criteria are combined with AND or OR. For example, to find individuals who are in the Volunteers group and have a Volunteer Training activity, use AND. To find everyone who is in the group or has that activity, use OR.

Search in Trash lets you search for contacts that have been deleted but not permanently deleted. Deleting a contact moves the contact and all related data to trash. Only users with the relevant permission can search in trash and restore a contact from it.

docs.title: The date range filter
docs.text:
Most component searches include a date range filter. You can use:

  • An absolute range, such as “1st Jan 2010” to “31 July 2010.”
  • A relative range, such as “Previous week.”

Relative ranges are especially useful for searches you intend to save as Smart Groups: automatically populated groups configured to include contacts who share characteristics or activities. See Groups and tags in Organising your data.

You might use a relative date range to find:

  • Contacts who contributed in the last 7 days (Relative date range - “From 1 Week ago”).
  • This (financial) year’s registered Event Participants (Relative date range - “This Year”).
  • Contacts who are a certain age.

Relative date filters using the “week” interval assume Sunday is the first day of the week. This differs from conventions in Europe and many countries in the Asia/Pacific region, where Monday is considered the first day. To set the first day of the week, go to Administer > Localization > Date Format.

docs.title: Combining search criteria
docs.text:
Different criteria are combined by “ANDing” them. For example, selecting the tag “major donor” and the country “Mexico” returns major donors from Mexico, but not major donors outside Mexico or other contacts in Mexico. You can change the default search operator from AND to OR in Search Settings.

Within criteria groups that let you check more than one value, those options are also combined by “ANDing.” For example, you can search for contacts whose Preferred Communication Method is both Email AND SMS.

Values selected from a dropdown list that allows multiple selections are always combined with OR. For example, you could find contacts who live in Alaska or Arizona.

When you expand a dropdown section and make selections, a cross appears at the right end of its header to show that the panel is used in the search. To stop using Address Fields, closing the panel is not enough: click the cross on its header.

docs.title: Limitations of Advanced Search
docs.text: The Advanced Search is an effective way to search for many things in CiviCRM. However, there is an issue with searches where Contacts are the client in more than one Case, and they are engaged in the same Activity Type in each of these Cases. The Advanced Search is currently not able to filter these Activities correctly by Case Type. This issue is expected to be resolved in the near future.

docs.title: Full-text search
docs.text: Use Full-text search to search for text values in all fields of the database. For example, if you remember words you entered in an activity description but have forgotten the contact’s name, you can search for those words to find the contact and activity.

docs.title: Component searches
docs.text:
Most CiviCRM components provide a search for their own data, such as Find contributions and Find members. These forms work similarly to Advanced Search, but return rows of the component’s main objects rather than contacts. Find Members returns memberships, Find Participants returns event registrations, and Find Contributions returns contributions.

Each component search has its own Action list. See the Component chapters for details.

You can also use Advanced Search with Display Results As to search for component objects using criteria available in Advanced Search. For example, you could find event attendances from contacts who are also members.

docs.title: Search results actions
docs.text: After results appear, an Actions box above them lets you select all records or specific records and act on the selection. See search result actions for the available actions.

docs.title: The contact summary pop-up
docs.text: Hover over the contact icon in the left column of a search result to see detailed information in a pop-up. To adjust its fields, modify the “Summary Overlay” profile at Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Profiles.

docs.title: The wildcard (%)
docs.text:
A wildcard represents any character: a letter, numeral, or punctuation mark. In CiviCRM, the wildcard is %; other applications may use symbols such as *.

Suppose you need to find a first name similar to “Michael,” possibly “Michelle” or “Michał.” Searching for “Mich%” finds these variations, including “Micheal.” You can place a wildcard before, after, or within a word. For example, searching on 'Mich%el' will exclude “Michał” and “Micheal” but still find “Michelle” and “Michael.”

Using % alone can produce unexpected results when a database value is empty rather than NULL: it also returns empty values. To find records with at least one character in a field, use %_% instead. This excludes empty and NULL results.

docs.title: Case sensitivity
docs.text: Searches for character strings are not case-sensitive. Searching for 'brooklyn' can return 'Brooklyn' or 'BROOKLYN'. Entering “mi%el” in lowercase can also find contacts whose names contain an uppercase 'M'.

docs.title: Default number of rows to be returned
docs.text:
In CiviCRM Advanced Searches and reports, the number of rows displayed on screen was previously 50 by default.

As of CiviCRM version 5.39, System Administrators can change the number of rows displayed under Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Search Preferences. Avoid setting the number too high: a higher number makes the screen slower to load.

docs.title: SearchKit
docs.text: SearchKit is more powerful than Advanced Search but requires more technical knowledge. It is suitable for site builders and power users. See SearchKit.

docs.title: Use actions on Search Kit results
docs.text:
After you build a search, the available actions depend on the entity selected. For example, searching for Contacts offers different “Action” options from searching for Contributions.

To make more options under “Action” selectable, select one or more search results. Otherwise, only “Download Spreadsheet” will display.

You can select individual results, click the dark gray box to select all results, or use the dropdown arrow at the upper-left of the results listing to select all results, all results on the page, or no results.

For descriptions of the primary actions available for each selected entity, see Search Result Actions.

docs.title: Creating a FormBuilder interface for the Search Display
docs.text: Once the Search Display has been created, FormBuilder is then used to create an interface to make this display available for users.

docs.title: Create the form
docs.text: A SearchKit saved search is required to create a Search Form. The form can be created either directly from the SearchKit interface or from the FormBuilder interface.

docs.title: From the SearchKit table
docs.text:
1. Create a SearchKit entity table or reuse an existing SearchKit table.
  2. After creating the search, enter an appropriate name for it and click Save.
  3. On successful save, two buttons will be displayed on the right side: Forms and View Results.
  4. Clicking Forms shows a list of existing FormBuilder forms and a button to create a new form using the saved search. Clicking that button navigates to the FormBuilder editor page.

docs.title: From the Formbuilder UI
docs.text: Search forms can also be created using existing SearchKit entity tables. The steps for this are as follows: 1. Navigate to the FormBuilder UI by selecting Administer > Customize Data and Screens > FormBuilder. 2. On the FormBuilder UI, click on the Search Forms tab to see the list of existing Search Forms and to create a new one. 3. Clicking the New Search button shows a dropdown of existing SearchKit saved searches. 4. Selecting the desired search will navigate to the FormBuilder editor page.

docs.title: Configure the form settings
docs.text:
The form configuration screen can be broadly grouped into two parts:

  1. a configuration pane (left) that contains:
    • the title (required and visible on the form)
    • the description (highly recommended for clarity)
    • the permission required to access the form
    • the url at which the form will be found (must start with civicrm/)
    • a checkbox as to whether the form should be accessible from the website front end
    • a checkbox to add the form to the navigation menu
    • a "Placement" drop-down where you can make the form available in a number of places, including the Contact Layout editor, the dashlets interface, a Contact summary tab or block, or to be accessed via tokens
  2. a layout pane (right) that contains:
    • a placeholder for the SearchKit display in the right-hand window
    • a list of the fields that could be exposed as form filters
    • options for specifying hidden filters

docs.title: URL filters in search forms
docs.text:
For search forms with pages you can make them get filter values from a special part of the URL. This means you can link to filtered views of the search form, e.g. from another search form (by using tokens in the Link URL field.)

When looking at the left-side panel with a search display tab selected while editing a form, there's an option called Filters. Select a field, e.g. Hair color, then select URL and then type a codename, e.g. haircolor. If the field you want is missing, it's because that field has not been added to the Search, so jump back and do that first.

To use this feature, the URL can be constructed like this: https://your.example.org/civicrm/path/to/your/searchformpage/#?haircolor=brown i.e. appending #?haircolor=brown. If you had multiple such filters, you would add subsequent ones like #?haircolor=brown&hairlength=short.

When the field has a : in it that indicates that the field is a 'pseudoconstant'. The underlying database value is generally a number which maps to a name and label. In this case the database field payment_instrument_id is a number. In some cases we know the number instead, in which case we could use payment_instrument_id=1 in our URL or payment_instrument_id:name=Cash. As well as being more readable and discoverable, this variant is more useful for implementers who work with multiple sites, since the actual ID numbers will likely change between sites, but the name is fixed.

You can get the exact field name needed by adding the filter on the form setup.

If the field is already filtered (e.g receive date before this week) then the URL filter will further narrow down the results rather than replace the existing filter.

The following formats are acceptable for dates:

  • receive_date=2021-09-23
  • receive_date=20210923
  • receive_date=20210923234040 (i.e. time is 23:40:40)
  • receive_date=this.month (See the list)

You can also filter with the same value on one of a set of multiple fields by adding a hidden field to your form, adding additional fields with Combine multiple fields and then copying the resulting field name from the Markup tab to use in your url. For example, if you want to filter on both first name and last name, you could add the first name field to your form, make it a hidden field, and then use Combine multiple fields to add the last name field to that field. Now you can filter on both fields at once by appending #/?first_name,last_name=foo to your form URL.

docs.title: Example: Listing Contacts who have relationships of the same type
docs.text: You may want a list of contacts who have more than one (or any number) of the same relationship type. For example, a children’s summer camp could find contacts who have more than one child, then turn the results into a mailing list to offer enrollment discounts to multi-child families.

docs.title: Step 1: Create a new search and set initial criteria
docs.text:
1. Go to Administer > Search > SearchKit and click New Search.
  2. Ensure that the default Contacts is selected as the primary entity to Search for.
  3. Select With (required) and Contact Related Contacts on a new entity.
  4. Click the +Group By button and group by both Contact ID and Relationship Type.

docs.title: Step 2: Add the Relationship column to the search
docs.text:
1. Below the criteria, click +Add and select Contact Related Contacts: Relationship.
  2. Though not necessary, you may also add the Contact Related Contacts: Relationship from contact column to indicate the relationship type, especially if your search includes more than one type of relationship.

docs.title: Step 3: Transform the Relationship column
docs.text:
1. Click Field Transformations just below the Having drop down list.
  2. Select Count as the transformation for Relationship.

docs.title: Step 4: Add a Having clause
docs.text:
1. Under Having, select (Count) Contact Related Contact: Relationship from the Select field drop down list.
  2. For this scenario, select the greater than symbol (>) and enter 1 in the field to its right.
  3. Click Search to view your results. Name and save your search as well.

docs.title: Example: Show events attended by employees on an Organization’s contact record
docs.text: Use FormBuilder and SearchKit to show all the events attended by the employees of an Organization on the Organization’s contact record.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the saved search
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Search > SearchKit.
  2. On the Submission Forms tab, click the New Search link.

docs.title: Step 2: Add SearchKit settings
docs.text:
1. Give the search a title ‘Events Attended By Employees’.
  2. On the Search For tab on the left:
  3. Click + Entity and choose Contact Related Contacts, change it to With (required).
  4. Click and change the Relationship to Contact value to Employee of.
  5. Click + Entity and choose Contact Related Contacts - Contact Participants, change it to With (required).
  6. Click + Entity and choose Contact Related Contacts - Contact Participants - Participant Event, change it to With (required).
  7. On the Select Fields tab on the left:
  8. Click on the x symbol to remove Contact ID, Sort Name, Contact Type, Contact Subtype.
  9. Leave Event Title.
  10. Still on the Select Fields tab, use the + Add Field drop down to include:
  11. Contact related contacts - Contact Participants - Participant Event - Start Date
  12. Contact related contacts - First Name
  13. Contact related contacts - Last Name
  14. Contact related contacts - Primary Email
  15. To add a display, click on + Add on the lower left hand side of the screen and choose Table.
  16. Give the Table a name. This name will show on the contact screen as the tab title.
  17. Click Sorting, choose Contact related contacts - Contact Participants - Participant Event - Start Date and change the order to Descending.
  18. Click Columns > Use Custom Columns.
  19. Click the down arrow on Event Title and edit the Header text to be Event Name.
  20. Click the down arrow on Start Date and edit the Header text to be Event Date.
  21. Click Save at the top of the screen.

docs.title: Step 3: Complete the form
docs.text:
1. At the top right of the page, click the Forms link.
  2. Choose Create form for Events Attended By Employees. This will open FormBuilder in a new browser tab.
  3. In the newly opened tab, use the configuration pane on the left side to configure these settings:
  4. Title: Events Attended By Employees
  5. Placement: Contact Summary Tab
  6. Contact Type: Organization
  7. Click Save at the top of the screen.

If you go to an Organization Contact record that has employees who have attended an event, they will be displayed in a new tab on the record, ‘Events Attended By Employees’.

docs.title: Create an invitation list for donor members
docs.text: This example builds an invitation list for members who are major donors and have not previously attended an event.

docs.title: Step 1: Select current members
docs.text:
On the SearchKit page, click New Search and choose a base entity in Search for. The base entity cannot be changed once the search has been saved.

You could start with Contacts and link Memberships, or start with Memberships and link Contacts. Because the goal is a list of contacts, select Contacts from Search for. Change With (optional) to With (required), then select Memberships from +Entity.

To include only active members, go to Where and change Status to is one of New and Current.

Enter a name for the search and click Save. You can click Search to preview the results.

docs.title: Step 2: Find members with no event participant record
docs.text: To find members who have never attended an event, look for contacts without a participant record. Change a second With (optional) field to Without and select Contact Participants.

docs.title: Step 3: Add donors and sum their contributions
docs.text:
Change a third With (optional) to With (required) and select Contact Contributions. Under Where, add a clause that sets Financial Type = Donation.

A contact may have multiple donations. To list each contact only once, select Contact ID from Group By.

Using Group By enables a Field Transformation, such as combine, count, or sum. To sum each contact's contributions, click +Add and select Total Amount to add it to the search results. Under Field Transformation above the results, select Sum from the drop-down menu next to the Total Amount field.

docs.title: Step 4: Filter for major donors
docs.text: To include donors who have contributed at least a specified amount, add a condition on the sum of the total amount. Because the condition uses a field transformation, use Having instead of Where. Set (Sum) Contact Contibution to greater than or equal to the specified amount.

docs.title: Step 5: Add email and phone number
docs.text:
Add the contact's primary email and phone number as entities for the invitation list.

!!! Note: * Not every contact may have an email or phone number in the database, so With (optional) is recommended. * A contact may have specified that they do not want to be phoned or emailed. This is shown on their Contact Summary and needs to be taken into account.

The configured search results will likely look something like this:

docs.title: Step 6: Export as a CSV file
docs.text: Click Actions above the search results to see available actions, including downloading the data as a spreadsheet (CSV file).

docs.title: Create a public membership list
docs.text: An organization with several levels of membership may want filterable, searchable lists on its website populated by live data from CiviCRM. This tutorial uses SearchKit and FormBuilder to create a logo grid with tooltips and links to external websites, such as members' websites. Visitors can filter the grid by membership type.

docs.title: Step 1: Create a new search and define the data
docs.text:
Go to Administer > Search > SearchKit and click New Search. Then:

  1. Give the search a title name (e.g. "Our Members") in the box labeled "Untitled Search".
  2. Select Memberships from the Search for list.
  3. Add a With for Membership Contact so that data can be pulled from the member's contact record (e.g. the display name to show in a tooltip).
  4. Add a second With for Contact Websites to access the link to the member's homepage.

Tap Search to check the results. The criteria above returned six memberships. When you add Membership Contact and Contact Websites, SearchKit automatically adds some columns with data from these sources:

docs.title: Step 2: Add columns to output additional data
docs.text:
The displayed columns determine which data the search returns. To add a column for the logo URL:

  1. Tap the +Add button at the top right of the results table.
  2. Choose the column to display (e.g. Membership Contact: Image URL).
  3. Refresh the results display by clicking Search.

This selection uses the standard contact image. Using custom fields, such as a different image, requires adding another data source first.

The results will now look like this:

Tip

Don't forget to Save your work.

docs.title: Step 3: Add and configure a grid display
docs.text:
To format the search results, click the +Add button underneath the search's title field to add a display. Select a Grid display to organize the output into tiles.

Give the display configuration a title (e.g. "Our Members"). By default, SearchKit adds all the search's fields (columns) to the new display. You can customize these fields, including by dragging and dropping them into a new order.

Click Preview to see the results in a 3x3 pattern grid below the button at the bottom of the page. At this stage, the display does not yet show the intended logos. To configure it:

  1. Remove all items that are not needed by clicking the remove symbol (indicated by the red arrow in the screenshot above) in each item's section. Leave only Membership Contact: Image URL for this example.
  2. Check the Image checkbox to display the logo as an image.
  3. Optionally, set size attributes to make the logo sizes match (e.g. adjust the height to 200px).
  4. Check the Link checkbox, select 'Other...' from the dropdown menu, and select Membership Contact - Contact Websites: Website from the token dropdown.
  5. Attention: remove /civirm from the front of the token: civicrm/[Membership_Contact_contact_id_01_Contact_Website_contact_id_01.url] so that it becomes: [Membership_Contact_contact_id_01_Contact_Website_contact_id_01.url] as the /civicrm portion would inhibit the url from reaching the member's external website.
  6. Check the Tooltip checkbox and make sure the label that pops up to the right is a token for the Display Name.

Click Refresh to see the logos displayed as intended:

Note

This configuration will only show members who have logos associated with their record. To include those without logos, check the Alternative image box.

docs.title: Step 4: Add and configure a form
docs.text:
To show the results on a public website, create a Form. Return to the SearchKit dashboard and click Forms > + Create Form for Our Members Grid:

Then:

  1. Give the Form a name and a description.
  2. Enter the URL for the page on which you want the results displayed (e.g. 'civicrm/members').

After clicking Save, the link View Page will appear. This link shows the fully formatted results grid.

To filter which membership types are shown, switch from the Form Settings tab to the Our Members Grid tab and drag the item Membership Type into the Form Layout tab.

Then:

  1. Change the preset of the filter so that it shows the desired membership types.
  2. Change the layout details, such as the title of a container element.

So long as you are logged into your CiviCRM account, the specified URL (e.g. your.civicrm.tdl/civicrm/members/) will display the configured Form.

docs.title: Step 5: Set permissions
docs.text:
To make the form accessible to anonymous users, return to the search's display configuration and unlock the Enforce Permissions button by clicking it. Once clicked, the button will read Bypass Permissions, as shown below.

Save before going back to the Form configuration.

To make the page containing the results grid viewable on a public website:

  1. Remove all restrictions by selecting 'Generic: Allow all users (including anonymous)' from the dropdown list.
  2. Check the Accessible on front-end of website box.

Users, whether logged in or not, will now be able to view and filter the form.

docs.title: Example: Upcoming Events
docs.text: title: Example: Upcoming Events category: tutorial topic: searchkit subtopic: upcoming-events component: SearchKit audiences: - administrators level: intermediate journey_stage: plan-and-configure summary: Build an upcoming events overview with participant counts, links, optional filters, and a navigation menu item. extensions: [] related: [] review_priority: high review_notes: - Entity settings and participant filters needed to reproduce the search are shown in images but are not fully specified in the text. source_path: searching/searchkit/example-upcoming-events.md official_url: https://docs.civicrm.org/user/en/latest/searching/searchkit/example-upcoming-events/

docs.title: Example: Upcoming Events
docs.text:
When you click the Event tab from the toolbar and then select Manage Events, the default event overview looks like this:

SearchKit provides the option to create an alternative to the Manage Event overview screen that can be customized in many ways:

This SearchKit-built overview includes:

  • A clickable event title that leads to the event's Info and Settings page
  • A list of speakers and hosts for each event
  • The number of registered/attended participants
  • The number of cancellations/no-shows
  • Clickable registered/attended and cancellations/no-shows numbers that lead to lists of participants with those statuses

The following steps show how to create this overview.

docs.title: Step 1: Create a new search
docs.text:
Go to Administer > Search > SearchKit and click New Search.

  1. Enter a name for the search, such as Upcoming Events.
  2. Select Events from the Search for list.
  3. In the Where section, use the drop-down fields to select Event Start Date, then >=, then Now. You can also Pick a Date or tailor the search with other options.

Tip

Don't forget to Save your work.

Click Search to view the result.

docs.title: Step 2: Add event columns
docs.text: By default, the results show the event ID and event title. For this example, also add the event start date by selecting that column from the list on the right-hand side.

docs.title: Step 3: Add participant information
docs.text:
The search currently shows only event information. To show the event's hosts and speakers, add the participants entity:

Add a filter on role in Where:

Use Contains because a participant can have multiple roles, which are stored in the participant role field. The participant role should be either Speaker or Host.

Finally, add the Participant Contact entity to show the names of speakers and hosts. The search now looks like this:

docs.title: Step 4: Group on event ID
docs.text:
If you run the search now, an event appears multiple times when it has more than one speaker or host. Group on event ID to avoid this:

Use a field transformation to display the speakers and hosts as a comma-separated list:

docs.title: Step 5: Add the number of participants
docs.text:
To add the number of participants, use the Count field transformation on Participant ID. Using it now would count only hosts and speakers because of the filter in Where.

Add Event Participants again as an entity:

To display a count of no-shows and cancellations, add another Event Participants entity:

Click Add on the upper right side of the search results display to add the Participant ID (2 and 3) columns. Under Field Transformations, select Count and check the Distinct box next to the Participant ID (2 and 3) labels:

docs.title: Step 6: Change column names and sort order
docs.text:
To change the column names, first create a table display. Click Add... on the left side of the form, under Compose Search, and select Table.

Give the display a name and add a Sort By:

Scroll down and give the columns meaningful names in the Header fields. The preview might now look like this:

docs.title: Step 7: Make the values clickable
docs.text:
Add a Link to each participant count's respective overview page:

For the registered/attended count, enter:

  • civicrm/event/search?reset=1&force=1&event=[id]&status=true

For the cancelled/no-show count, enter:

  • civicrm/event/search?reset=1&force=1&event=[id]&status=false

You can also add a Link to the event title:

  • civicrm/event/manage/settings?reset=1&action=update&id=[id]

This link leads to the event's Info and Settings page. The result looks like this:

docs.title: Step 8: Add optional filtering
docs.text:
You can add a form above the upcoming events list for optional filtering. Use the button in the upper right corner of the search:

This opens FormBuilder. Give the form a name and a page link:

Click the Upcoming Events Table tab. Drag and drop the form elements into the form layout pane:

You may want to add a Container first to lay out the other form elements:

docs.title: Step 9: Add the overview to the navigation menu
docs.text:
The page link specified for the form in the previous step is civicrm/upcoming-events. You can create a navigation menu item with this link.

See Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Navigation Menu.

Users can then access the upcoming events from the menu:

The menu item leads to the finalized search form:

docs.title: Expiration date
docs.text: Some searches are useful only for a defined period. You can set a date for a saved search to be removed from the list instead of manually cleaning up saved searches.

docs.title: How expiration works
docs.text:
The expiration date is set:

The search is given an expiration date:

Searches are not deleted after the expiry date; they are only hidden from the display. They can only be restored to the display by deleting the expiry date via the API explorer or SQL statement.

docs.title: Export and import SearchKit searches
docs.text: You can export saved SearchKit searches to share them with others, and import searches that have been shared with you. This requires some comfort with moving code around, but not with creating it. You can do it all through the graphical interface.

docs.title: Export a saved search
docs.text:
Export is available only after you have saved your SearchKit query.

  1. Visit the main SearchKit page and choose “Export” from the additional actions menu (☰) beside your saved search.

  1. In the export window, copy the coded version of your search to your clipboard. If you have created associated displays, groups or forms, you can include them in the export.

If you want to include the saved search in a custom extension, use “API Explorer Export” instead. Its link is at the top of the export window.

Once you have copied the SearchKit query, you can save it in a file for future reference, import it into another site, or send it to someone else to use and modify on their system.

docs.title: Import a saved search
docs.text:
1. Go to the default SearchKit page and click the “Import” link just under the “New Search” button in the top right corner.
  1. Paste the exported search into the empty box and submit it. You’ll return to the main screen, where you can see the newly imported search.

docs.title: Field transformations
docs.text: Field transformations are formulas applied to fields in your result set. Examples include displaying another field if a value is missing, rounding a numeric value, counting occurrences, and summing values.

docs.title: Transformation categories
docs.text:
Transformations are organized into four categories:

  • Comparison
  • Text
  • Math
  • Aggregate (only available if you used Group By)

docs.title: Option details
docs.text:
See the MySQL documentation for more information:

  • https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/built-in-function-reference.html
  • https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/aggregate-functions.html

Not all MySQL functionality has been implemented in the Search Kit.

docs.title: Group by
docs.text:
“Group By” organizes data around one or more common elements of the selected entity. When you execute the search, the results display one row per value of the selected “Group By” fields.

For example, searches of Contacts can group results by Created Date, Contact Subtype, and Location information, among other options. Searches of Contributions can group results by Contribution Date, Amount, and Payment Method, among other options.

docs.title: Analyze grouped results
docs.text:
“Group By” can help you analyze patterns and relationships in your data by counting, totalling or averaging numeric information, or concatenating data in other fields.

For example, if you’re looking at contacts and their addresses, you can group the results by Country.

In this use case, the results display a count of contacts per Country, because search results display one row per element selected.

If you add more than one “Group By” option, additional rows will display upon clicking “Search” for the elements selected. For example, if you group results of your search by Country and “Address (primary) State/Province”, one row will display for each State/Province of data in the system.

You can drag search result columns left or right to change their display order. If you change the order of the columns, click “Search” again for your results to display.

docs.title: Filter Search Kit results with Having
docs.text: Having filters the data in the result set. Unlike Where, which filters data before it is returned from the database, Having filters the results displayed in the table. This allows you to filter aggregate data or transform field values.

docs.title: Select a result field
docs.text:
After building a search results set from an initial Entity selection and any additional Entity selections using With/Without, you can use Where and Having to further filter and manipulate the results. Both options are in the “Filter Conditions” tab at left.

The available fields differ: Where lets you select any field in the CiviCRM database, while Having lets you select only fields included in the results.

docs.title: Choose an operator and comparison value
docs.text:
Once you have chosen the result field to filter on, select an operator and comparison values.

In general, the operators work like the similarly named SQL operators:

  • Matches Pattern matches a regular expression pattern.
  • Is Like matches a complete field. To find part of a field, you usually need wildcards, such as %search term%.
  • Contains is useful for searching serialized fields, which store multiple values together. For example, Contact Subtype could be Parent, Volunteer, or Staff. Contains matches a full value such as Parent, not part of a value.

Negated operators such as Not Like, ≠, or Doesn't Contain won't match NULL fields that have no value. They only match fields that have a value and whose value doesn't match the criteria. If you want NULL fields as well, you can search for ≠searchterm or Is Empty.

docs.title: Filter by a pattern
docs.text:
This example filters the displayed results to show only phone numbers that match a regular expression describing a particular format.

Reverse the filter to find records with phone numbers that do not match the pattern and may need fixing.

‘Glob-matching’ with % or * can get you a long way, but regular expressions are more flexible and powerful for filtering results. There are many good tutorials online.

docs.title: Compare two fields
docs.text: Although you will most often filter against a value you provide, you can also compare one field with another. This example displays rows where the display name and email address are the same.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Permissions for SearchKit and FormBuilder combine settings in:

  • SearchKit
  • FormBuilder
  • CMS user roles (CiviCRM functionalities)
  • ACL roles (fine-grained permissions)

docs.title: SearchKit
docs.text:
Every display you create in a search, such as a table or grid, has an “Enforce Permissions/ Bypass permissions” button at the top. It is a toggle, and its displayed text indicates the current state:

  • Enforce permissions respects existing permissions defined in CiviCRM. Access control can be set at various levels, including roles in your content management system (CMS) and specific actions controlled by CiviCRM’s more detailed ACL controls. For more information, see Permissions and Access Control.
  • Bypass permissions lets anyone who can view the display see all results, regardless of their permission level. This can be useful, but be careful what you expose.

docs.title: FormBuilder
docs.text:
For both Search forms and Submission forms:

  • The form settings tab has a permission setting that determines who can view the form.
  • Multiple permissions can be joined using “and” to require all of them, or “or” to require only one of them.
  • Available permissions include CMS role permissions (e.g. WordPress : delete_pages) and CiviCRM permissions (e.g. CiviContribute: Access CiviContribute). Either or both can be used in this field.
  • For more examples, see who can use a form and the additional permissions that control whether a form autofills with data from the database.

docs.title: Query info
docs.text: Query Info shows the underlying code behind your search in API and SQL format. You can copy it for use outside SearchKit if needed. It is optional and recommended for users who are comfortable using API and SQL commands directly.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Explain the options and what they do to the search results, for example, list each option available in a dropdown and say what each will do, or if list is variable and too long, explain in more abstract terms.

docs.title: Option Details
docs.text: If the section being described has a long list of options that have a one sentence description in the UI then probably start by just listing all of those options in an unordered list.

docs.title: Search displays
docs.text: Search Displays present search results in different formats on your site. They make SearchKit results accessible across your CiviCRM implementation.

docs.title: Adding a display
docs.text:
A search can have zero, one, or multiple displays, so you can present the same data in multiple ways. To add a display, click the "Add..." button on the left side when editing your saved search.

Default Display

Every search can be displayed as a table without creating a display - that's what you see when clicking the "Search" button. This "Search results table" can be viewed as a standalone page or even embedded in a form in-lieu of creating a display. However, you'll typically want to create your own display instead of using the default so you can set some configuration options.

docs.title: Display types
docs.text:
When adding a search display, first choose the type from the dropdown list:

  • Table: Displays results in rows and columns, with an optional pager and selectable actions. The styling of rows and columns is highly configurable.
  • List: Displays results on one or more lines. Each field can be styled differently or given a custom css class.
  • Grid: Useful for image gallery thumbnails and other content to show side-by side.
  • Tree: Represents hierarchical data in a nested tree structure.
  • Data Entry: Unlike the above displays which output data, this creates a spreadsheet-like input form for batch data entry.
  • Autocomplete: Autocomplete fields give results from the search as the user types. An autocomplete display allows customization of how each result appears in the dropdown. Once created, the display can be selected for use in FormBuilder, or select "Make Default Autocomplte" to affect forms site-wide.
  • DB Entity: Creates a database table or view which can be accessed with SearchKit, the API, or SQL-based tools.

docs.title: Additional extensions
docs.text:
More search displays are provided by extensions in the Extensions Directory:

  • ChartKit: Enable this extension (already bundled with CiviCRM core) for data visualisation in the form of plots, charts, and graphs.
  • SearchKit Calendar: Download this extension for a time-based display of events, activities, etc.
  • SearchKit Maps: Download this extension to show the location of contacts, events, etc. on a map.
  • SearchKit Tokens: Download this extension to create your own tokens with SearchKit, for use in mailings.
  • SearchKit Column Display: Download this extension for a display that stacks fields into columns.
  • And more: Check the Extensions Directory for the latest additions.

docs.title: Configuration options
docs.text:
Each Search Display can be customized with various settings:

  • Field selection and ordering
  • Column headers and labels
  • Sorting preferences
  • Link configurations
  • Inline editing capabilities
  • Access permissions
  • Display-specific styling
  • Pagination settings
  • Formatting and rewriting results

docs.title: Rewriting results in Search Displays
docs.text: Search Displays let you rewrite fields to customize how data is presented to users.

docs.title: Basic field combining
docs.text:
Combine multiple fields using square brackets to reference field names:

[first_name] [last_name]
[street_address], [city] [postal_code]

This creates concatenated values like:

  • "Jane Smith"
  • "123 Main St, Springfield 12345"

docs.title: Smarty rewrites
docs.text:
For more complex formatting, use Smarty template syntax with curly brackets:

  • Conditional Display: 
    {if $nick_name}[nick_name]{else}[first_name]{/if} [last_name]
  • Math Operations: 
    {$total_amount - $fee_amount}
  • Value Transformation: 
    {if $age_years >= 18}Adult{else}Minor{/if}

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
1. Field names in square brackets (e.g. [display_name]) are replaced with their values automatically
  2. Use {$field_name} to access raw field values in Smarty code, so you can get, for example, 125 instead of $125.00.
  3. Smarty modifiers like |date_format and |crmMoney help with common formatting needs
  4. You can combine both square bracket and Smarty syntax in the same rewrite

Tip

Rewritten fields are display-only and won't affect the underlying data storage.

docs.title: Search button
docs.text: Click this button to preview and refresh your search results.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: You must explicitly use the search button whenever you want to see results. The results display will be cleared each time you make a change to the settings.

docs.title: Search For
docs.text: Specify the primary entity (contact, activity, contribution, etc) that you’d like to include in this searchkit query.

docs.title: Primary entities
docs.text:
The primary entities available through the Search For command are:

  • Activity - Past of future actions concerning one or more contacts.
  • Contacts - Individuals, organizations, households, etc.
  • Contributions - Financial records consisting of transactions, line-items, etc.
  • Events - Scheduled in-person or online events which contacts can register for and attend.
  • Grants - Funds applied for and given out by this organization.
  • Individuals - Contacts of type Individual.
  • Memberships - Records of contacts belonging to an organization’s membership program.
  • Organizations - Contacts of type Organization.
  • Participants - Records of contacts’ attendance and roles in events.
  • Pledges - Promises to contribute [to an organization] at a future time, either in full, or at regular intervals until a total goal is reached.
  • More - Other, less-commonly search entities:
    • A long list of less-commonly searched entities.
    • See the list for explanations of the entities, similar to the above.

docs.title: Modifiers and grouping
docs.text:
Once a Search For entity is selected, optional modifier entities are available to be selected, per top-level entity. Each has an appropriate description that assists with construction of the full search capability.

In addition, the results of the searched for entity can be (optionally) grouped, again, with options that depend on the top level entity selected. Each has an appropriate description that assists with construction of the full search capability.

docs.title: Example Soft Credit Search and Display
docs.text:
This example creates a Soft Credit search and a table display.

A little background on Soft Credits

Soft Credits in CiviCRM are a way to keep track of someone you should also thank for a contribution other than the donor. For example, if I ask people to donate for my birthday and John Doe contributes 25 euro I can get recognition for that with a soft credit. For more information read the Soft Credits section.

The search combines data from the contact who has the Soft Credit, the contact who made the contribution, and the contribution itself. This can show who the best contribution solicitors are. The result will look like this:

docs.title: Start from saved searches
docs.text:
Navigate to SearchKit from the Search menu. The saved searches page shows existing searches:

The Soft Credit example is already on the list, but this example creates a new search step by step. Click New Search.

docs.title: Create the search
docs.text:
The New Search button opens an empty search form:

On the left, enter a name in the text box that shows Untitled Search. This example uses “Soft Credit Example Search”.

Below the name, you can add a tag to categorize the search—for example, with other Fundraising searches.

The Add selection box below the tags is covered in Adding a display.

docs.title: Select entities
docs.text:
At the middle top of the form, choose which entity to search. Initially, the value is Contacts:

The list of available entities is extensive.

For this example, the Contribution Soft Credits entity is initially selected. This returns the contacts who have the Soft Credit, the ID of the linked contribution, the Soft Credit amount (which can differ from the contribution amount), and the Soft Credit type.

To include information about the contribution and the contact who made it, specify those entities too. Click the +Entity select menu next to With (optional) to add them. SearchKit works out how to link them: it uses the contribution ID to link to the Contribution and the contact ID in the contribution to link to Contact.

You can add further conditions. This example limits contributions to those with a financial type of Donation, filtering out payments for Memberships or Events. Use the Where box to limit the contributions to a date range of 1 Jan 2021 to 30 April 2022.

The selected entities and conditions look like this:

The Group By box is not used in this example. It lets you group results, such as by Contact Display Name.

docs.title: Select fields
docs.text:
At the bottom of the form, select which fields to display in the results. The default selection typically includes an ID and sometimes a name:

Click Search above the field names to run the search and display its data.

Next to Search, the Action box offers several actions. Its default is to download the results as a CSV file. This standard action can be switched off, which will be shown later.

Use Add on the right side of the form to choose more fields from the selected entities:

In this example, remove Soft Credit ID, keep the name of the Soft Credit contact, and add:

  • the soft credit amount
  • the soft credit type
  • the name of the contributing contact
  • the contribution total amount
  • the contribution date
  • the contribution source
  • the contribution status
  • the contribution payment method

Click Search again to see the updated results:

docs.title: Transform fields
docs.text:
Expand Field Transformations, just below the entities section. It lists the fields included in the search and offers functions to transform each one.

To make the Contact stand out, select the Uppercase function next to the Contribution Contact Name label. To exclude the timestamp when the contribution was received, select Date Only next to the Contribution Receive Date label.

Click Search to view the transformed results:

docs.title: Look at the query
docs.text:
Below Field Transformations, Query Info shows the technical translation of the selected entities and fields. It is useful for developers and can be ignored if you do not need the technical details.

For the Soft Credit example, the query is displayed as:

{
  "version": 4,
  "select": [
    "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01_Contribution_Contact_contact_id_01.display_name",
    "amount",
    "soft_credit_type_id:label",
    "UPPER(ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.contact_id.display_name) AS UPPER_ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01_contact_id_display_name",
    "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.total_amount",
    "DATE(ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.receive_date) AS DATE_ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01_receive_date",
    "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.source",
    "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.contribution_status_id:label",
    "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.payment_instrument_id:label"
  ],
  "orderBy": [],
  "where": [
    [
      "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.receive_date",
      "BETWEEN",
      [
        "2021-01-01 11:09:00",
        "2022-04-30"
      ]
    ]
  ],
  "groupBy": [],
  "join": [
    [
      "Contribution AS ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01",
      "LEFT",
      [
        "contribution_id",
        "=",
        "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.id"
      ],

      ]
    ],

docs.title: View results
docs.text: Click Save in the upper right. Once the search is saved, View Results appears underneath Save. You can view results while customizing the search or after completing it.

docs.title: Adding a display
docs.text:
Once you have specified the search criteria and selected the result fields, click Add... on the left side of the form to choose a display.

Available display types include:

  • Smart Group: creates a smart group of the search results
  • Table: shows the results as an overview in table form
  • List: shows the results as a (vertical) list
  • Grid: shows the results as an unformatted grid

This example uses Table, the most common option. Select Table to open its form:

Give the table a name, then click Save in the upper right corner.

Tip

Do not forget to press Save regularly when building your search or table so you do not lose your progress!

In Sort by, select the fields by which to sort the table. Fields can be sorted in ascending or descending order.

In the section below, you can Enable Actions on the table; set the Page Size, which determines how many results show per page; set the table style; choose the text shown when there are no results; and choose whether the search runs automatically. In this example, the text for no results has been changed and the other settings retain their default values:

The next section lists all fields in the search. To change their order, click and hold a column’s handle, then move it:

To remove a column, click its remove icon:

You can change each column’s heading and alignment, and enable inline editing.

To add a field from the defined search that is not yet displayed in the table, click Add at the top of the column list. You can also use this button to add a link, button, menu, or a bit of custom code.

In this example, add a menu for:

  • viewing the soft credit contact
  • viewing the contribution contact
  • viewing the contribution

Click Add, then select Menu:

A new menu column appears at the bottom of the list. You can edit the menu:

Clicking Add... within the menu section gives you suggestions based on the selected entities.

Click View Results to see the final table:

To make a menu option for the table, copy the URL from the browser:

Navigate to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Navigation Menu and click Add Menu Item:

Enter all the options and paste in the copied URL, starting with civicrm/ onwards.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Tags categorize data in CiviCRM. In SearchKit, you can use them to categorize searches, such as by Department or Initiative. Tags can be enabled for one or more of the following: Contact, Activity, Case, File, and SavedSearch.

As you add Saved Searches, tags can help you find them. On the SearchKit landing page, select one or more tags using “Filter by tags…” in the upper right of the saved-search listing.

You can add tags to SearchKit searches in three ways:

  • When creating a new search
  • When editing an existing search
  • From the Saved Searches main screen

docs.title: Add tags when creating or editing a search
docs.text:
1. Click “Configure Settings” in the left sidebar menu to show the Tags box.
  1. Click the Tags box to select existing tags or add new tags.

docs.title: Add tags from the Saved Search landing page
docs.text:
1. Click the tag icon with the down arrow.
  1. Begin typing in the “Add tag…” tag field. Matching results will appear, or you can select “Create Tag.” This adds a new tag to CiviCRM enabled for “SavedSearch,” allowing it to be used elsewhere in the system, such as from Advanced Search.

Learn more about working with tags.

docs.title: About
docs.text:
SearchKit is a search query builder with extensive options for displaying results. It is appropriate for site builders, power users and developers, but non-technical staff are likely to need training or to spend significant time learning the interface.

Alternatively, a more experienced user or developer may create Search Displays and make them available to other users via the menu system or as a dashlet on the main CiviCRM screen.

Searches built and saved in SearchKit can be targeted for use by different roles of staff users as well as unauthenticated end users.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
You can access SearchKit under the menu Search > SearchKit.

(On older versions of CiviCRM the SearchKit extension might not be enabled by default. You (or your site admin) may need to enable it. Navigate to Administer > System Settings > Extensions. Beside SearchKit, select the Install link then select the Install button.)

docs.title: Concepts and terminology
docs.text: Getting familiar with SearchKit requires some understanding of its components and concepts. There are a number of recipes in this documentation for you to work through, but some introduction is needed.

docs.title: You find 'Entities'
docs.text:
An entity is a technical word for a 'thing'. In most cases, the 'thing' (Entity) you want to search for will be something like a Contact, a Contribution, etc. You start your search by selecting the entity you want to search for, or one of the several you want to find:

Within your search, you can select fields to display. Some appear by default when you click Search. Then you can add others by clicking on the +Add on the right of the list of fields in your selected results, and selecting more fields.

You can delete fields from appearing in the search results by clicking on the x beside the field name in the header row containing field titles of the search results.

docs.title: Filters / criteria / where
docs.text:
The Where section is where you define the criteria that relate to your entity.

In general, the operators are the same as the similarly-named SQL operators. Here are a few tips:

  • Matches Pattern will match a regular expressions pattern.
  • Is Like matches a complete field, so you usually want to use it with wildcards if you want to find parts of the field, like %search term%.
  • Contains is useful for searching in serialized fields (fields that store multiple values together, such as Contact Subtype which could be Parent,Volunteer,Staff). It matches only a full value like Parent, not parts of a value.
  • Negated operators such as Not Like, ≠ or Doesn't Contain won't match NULL fields that have no value. They only match fields that have a value and the value doesn't match the criteria. If you want NULL fields as well, you can search for ≠ searchterm OR Is Empty.

This is particularly important for custom fields, where the custom field group row might not exist in the database at all if there are no values. For example, if you're filtering a Yes or No field and want to get all the entities that are not Yes, you need to use the Is Empty operator (which will find both NULL values and No, i.e. FALSE/0 values) rather than ≠ Yes.

docs.title: With/Without (Joins)
docs.text:
In SearchKit, when you include more than one type of information (referred to as 'entities'), it's known as a join. In the user interface it is represented with the options "with" or "without".

Adding an additional entity can change the number of rows in your results. For instance, consider a search that includes 'Contacts with (optional) Addresses'. The results will display differently based on the number of addresses associated with each contact.

  • If a contact has no address or just one, they will appear in the results as a single row.
  • If a contact has multiple addresses, there will be a separate row for each address.

Here's an example with Timmy and his parents:

Display Name Location Type Street Address Is Primary Timmy Home Sesame Street Yes Timmy's Mum Home Sesame Street Yes Timmy's Mum Work Downing Street No Timmy's Dad
